- understand-anything:graph-reviewer: Validates knowledge graphs for correctness, completeness, and quality.

structure, node/edge relationships, layer architecture, tours, and
dashboard usage. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:project-scanner: Scans a codebase directory to produce a structured inventory of all project files,
detected languages, frameworks, import maps, and estimated complexity. (Tools: All tools)

- understand-anything:tour-builder: Designs guided learning tours through codebases, creating 5-15 pedagogical steps
that teach project architecture and key concepts in logical order. (Tools: All tools)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

<result>## (A) Kanban

**Model: dual-source, not a mirror of sidebarState.**

`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\kanban\hooks\useKanbanActions\useKanbanActions.ts`

Every mutator branches on `card.workspaceId`:
- **Bound card** (id = `workspace:<wsId>`, `kanbanBoundCardId`) → delegates to `useDashboardSidebarState`: `snoozeWorkspace`, `unsnoozeWorkspace`, `archiveWorkspace`, `unarchiveWorkspaces`, `deleteWorkspace`, `restoreWorkspace`, `completeWorkspace`. Writes land on `v2WorkspaceLocalState[wsId].sidebarState`. `ensureBoundRow()` seeds the local-state row first if absent.
- **Unbound (Queued) card** → stamps its OWN `snoozeUntil` / `snoozeLaunchId` / `archivedAt` / `deletedAt` on the `v2KanbanCards` row.

So the card row DOES carry `snoozeUntil`/`snoozeLaunchId`/`archivedAt`/`deletedAt`/`completedAt` columns (`dashboardSidebarLocal/schema.ts` `kanbanCardSchema` L603-652, defaults L696-705), but for bound cards those fields stay `null` and are never read — the workspace sidebarState is the single source of truth.

**Sync direction: one-way, sidebarState → kanban view.** No writeback of card snooze/archive into sidebarState. `useKanbanData.ts` L571+ reads each bound card's bucket via `getWorkspaceSidebarBucket(local?.sidebarState, now, workspace.type)` and maps it into `KanbanCardBucket`; unbound cards use local `queuedCardBucket()` (L96-101). The `"completed"` bucket is the ONE exception with two-way healing (L~440-520: card-column placement is the intent signal and re-stamps/clears `sidebarState.completedAt`), snooze/archive have no such heal.

`KanbanReconciler.tsx` (`_dashboard\components\KanbanReconciler\KanbanReconciler.tsx`) just mounts `useKanbanData()` at dashboard level so the reconcile runs off-route. It is unrelated to the sidebar mirror.

**Helper reuse — all reused, nothing duplicated:**
- `useKanbanActions.ts` imports `APP_LAUNCH_ID`, `getNextTabOrder`, `KANBAN_*_COLUMN_ID`, `kanbanBoundCardId`
- `useKanbanData.ts` imports `getWorkspaceSidebarBucket`, `isWorkspaceSnoozed`, `isWithinRecycleBinWindow`, `APP_LAUNCH_ID`
- `KanbanCard.tsx` imports `SNOOZE_PRESET_OPTIONS`, `computeSnoozeUntil`

All from `...\providers\CollectionsProvider\dashboardSidebarLocal\sidebarVisibility.ts`. Note: `isWorkspaceSnoozed(card, now)` works on a kanban card because the source type is structural (`SidebarWorkspaceStateFields`) and card field names match exactly.

**`formatSnoozeRemaining` is NOT used by kanban** — only by `useDashboardSidebarData.ts:860`. Kanban shows no remaining-time label.

**Snooze submenu: TWO copies, no shared component.**
- `...\DashboardSidebar\...\DashboardSidebarWorkspaceContextMenu\DashboardSidebarWorkspaceContextMenu.tsx:118`
- `...\kanban\components\KanbanCard\KanbanCard.tsx:387`

Both map `SNOOZE_PRESET_OPTIONS` into their own `ContextMenuSub`/`ContextMenuSubContent`. Shared data, duplicated JSX. Sidebar also has a custom "N hours" inline field; kanban's copy has presets only. Sidebar calls `computeSnoozeUntil(duration)` inside `useDashboardSidebarWorkspaceItemActions.ts:164`; kanban calls it inline in the JSX (KanbanCard.tsx:395), special-casing `"next-launch"` at the call site instead.

Auto-unsnooze: kanban runs its own 60s ticker for UNBOUND cards only (`useKanbanData.ts` ~L555-569); bound cards rely on the sidebar ticker.

Sections: `KanbanColumn.tsx` L284-328 renders `KanbanStateSection` "Snoozed"/"Archived" with per-column persisted flags `snoozedCollapsed`/`archivedCollapsed`/`showSnoozed`/`showArchived` (set via `actions.setColumnSectionFlag`).

## (B) host-service

**Fields (device-local SQLite `host.db`), `packages\host-service\src\db\schema.ts`:**
- `sidebarWorkspaceState` (L727+): `archivedAt` L752, `snoozeUntil` L754, `snoozeLaunchId`, `completedAt`, `deletedAt`, `pinnedAt`, `isHidden`, `sectionId`, `tabOrder`
- `sidebarProjectState` L786, `sidebarMirrorMeta` L813 (`appLaunchId`, `lastFullSyncAtMs`, `organizationId`, `contentHash` L846)
- Separate/unrelated: `workspaces.archivedAt` + `workspaces.archiveReason` (`"merged" | "deleted"`) L246-252 — that's git/PR reconcile (`src\runtime\archived-workspace-reconcile.ts`), NOT user snooze/archive.

**Migrations:**
- `packages\host-service\drizzle\0017_dark_hedge_knight.sql` — created all three mirror tables including `archived_at`, `snooze_until`, `snooze_launch_id`
- `packages\host-service\drizzle\0019_small_black_queen.sql` — `ALTER TABLE sidebar_mirror_meta ADD content_hash text`
- `packages\host-service\drizzle\0020_overrated_dreaming_celestial.sql` — `workspaces.archived_at` + `archive_reason` (different feature)
- `0017_nappy_satana.sql` / `0018_greedy_sauron.sql` are unrelated (agent resume args, push fence)

**Writer: yes, exclusively the renderer.** `apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\components\AgentHooks\hooks\useSidebarMirrorSync\useSidebarMirrorSync.ts` — note the path is `_authenticated\components\AgentHooks\...`, not `AgentHooks\hooks\...`. `buildMirrorSnapshot(localStateRows, sidebarProjectRows)` (L240) reads ONLY `collections.v2WorkspaceLocalState` (L454) and `collections.v2SidebarProjects` (L475) via `useLiveQuery`, normalizes every field (`toEpochMs`/`toNullableId`/`toTabOrder`, fail-toward-null), and pushes to `sidebarMirror.sync`. 1s trailing debounce (`SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS`), 5min heartbeat (`MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS = 300_000`), unbounded retry capped at 5min, serialized single in-flight push. `APP_LAUNCH_ID` is sent in meta, not in the snapshot signature — a launch-id change forces a push.

**Server never writes these tables.** `sidebar-mirror.ts` `replaceMirror()` is delete-all-then-insert inside one `db.transaction`, meta row written last. No per-row delete verb by design. `computeContentHash` gates the `publishCompanionMirrorChanged` event so heartbeats don't churn client caches.

**Reader:** `packages\host-service\src\companion\sidebar-filter.ts` — `createSidebarCuration()` + `classifyWorkspace()`, which reproduces `getWorkspaceSidebarBucket` order exactly: deleted → completed → archived (`archivedAt != null || (isHidden && type !== "main")`) → snoozed (`snoozeLaunchId === meta.appLaunchId`, else `snoozeUntil > nowMs`) → hidden → show. `SidebarVerdict` union L100-107. Fails open via `passThroughCuration` on: no meta row, age > `MIRROR_MAX_AGE_MS = 1_200_000` (20min = 4 heartbeats), negative age, or org mismatch.

Consumers: `companion\read-api.ts` (raw SQL SELECT at L238; `visibleWorkspaces` L718-722, `/v1/tree` build L818+) and `companion\index.ts` (`createIsCuratedOffProbe` push gate ~L1590-1690, cached per `config.ts` L215-222). Curation gates listing/push only, never answer resolution.

**Answers to the two questions:**
1. **Snooze/archive IS persisted to a DB — `host.db`, which is device-local.** Nothing goes to cloud/Postgres. The renderer's own source of truth is localStorage (`v2WorkspaceLocalState`), and `host.db` holds a disposable, self-healing projection whose only purpose is letting the companion/phone bridge filter what it lists.
2. **Kanban card snooze/archive is NOT mirrored at all.** `packages\host-service\src` has zero kanban code (the 2 grep hits are prose in comments). `buildMirrorSnapshot` never touches `v2KanbanCards`. Consequence: an unbound Queued card that is snoozed/archived/binned is invisible to host-service; a bound card is covered incidentally because its state lives in `v2WorkspaceLocalState`.</result>

content.text:
Review target: `Review and simplify the current production-code changes for session Archive/Snooze. Preserve behavior and tests; apply quality improvements only.`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

aiTitle: Add archive and snooze to Superset sessions

content.text:
Implemented session Archive and Snooze support in the working tree.

### What changed

- Sessions retain the existing row context-menu actions and snooze presets.
- Added separate **Snoozed Sessions** and **Archived Sessions** subsections.
- Right-clicking the Sessions header provides Show/Hide controls for both subsections.
- Subsection visibility and collapsed state persist using the four approved device-local preference fields.
- Existing preference records are healed automatically; no database migration or cloud schema change was made.
- Snoozed sessions return through the existing expiry and next-launch behavior.
- Removed sessions appear under Archived Sessions, matching non-main project threads.
- Archiving or snoozing the open session does not close or navigate away from its content.
- Added an explicit eligibility boundary ensuring project-less sessions cannot enter Kanban.
- Moved the shared sidebar state-section component to its correct shared parent.
- Updated `FEATURES.md` with a protected `(SESSION-LIFECYCLE)` marker.

### Validation

- Focused tests: **50 passed, 0 failed**
- Biome on all 18 intended files: **passed**
- Feature-marker gate: **all 149 markers present**
- Reference-error gate: **passed**, with zero dangerous diagnostics
- `git diff --check`: **passed**
- Repository typecheck remains blocked by existing accepted type debt, beginning with the Windows ARM64 `@lydell/node-pty` declaration errors. Direct desktop checking also reports existing unrelated route, Mermaid, and nullable-project diagnostics.

No commit or push was made. The implementation remains as 17 unstaged working-tree paths.

<result>## Companion (Android) — `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion`

**Bottom line: there is no release flow. Historically every install was a locally built DEBUG APK.** No CI, no tags, no signed build ever produced.

### Evidence

- No `.github/`, no `scripts/`, no workflow, no `gradlew` wrapper invocation script. Root contains only: `app-phone`, `app-watch`, `core`, `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `gradlew(.bat)`, `DESIGN.html`, `PROTOCOL.md`, `SETUP.md`, `local.properties`, `tmp`.
- 42 commits, single branch `main`, **zero tags**, zero release commits. Last commit `1dc854e` 2026-08-09 22:04.
- Only build outputs that exist:

  - No `apk/release`, no `bundle/`, no `.aab` anywhere. Release variant never assembled.
- APK mtimes track the last commit minute → build was rerun as the final step of the last work session, not a release act.
- `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion/tmp/` holds `gradle-*.log` (6 files, Aug 8) — all show `:app-phone:preDebugBuild`, `:core:preDebugBuild` etc. Debug tasks + unit tests only. No install task, no `assembleRelease`, in any log.

### Version fields

Hardcoded, identical in both app modules, **never bumped** — introduced at baseline commit `79c4261 chore: verified Gradle baseline for phone + watch` and untouched since:

```

versionName = "0.1.0"
```

- `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion/app-phone/build.gradle.kts` lines ~35-36
- `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion/app-watch/build.gradle.kts` (same values, comment says applicationId + key MUST match phone)

Confirmed in both `output-metadata.json` files: `versionCode 1`, `versionName "0.1.0"`, `variantName "debug"`.

No versioning automation — no git-describe, no properties injection, no CI bump. Bumping = editing both files by hand.

### Build config facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| applicationId | `family.khaira.supersetcompanion` — **identical in phone and watch, deliberately** (Wear Data Layer silently drops traffic otherwise) |
| namespace | phone `family.khaira.supersetcompanion`, watch `...wear`, core `...core` |
| compileSdk / targetSdk | 37 / 37 |

Debug = default AOSP debug keystore (that's what shipped). Release signing is wired but never exercised:

- Both app modules read `signing.properties` from, in order: `-PsigningPropertiesFile=...` → env `SUPERSET_COMPANION_SIGNING` → `~/.superset/companion/keystore/signing.properties`.
- Those files **do exist**: `~/.superset/companion/keystore/signing.properties` (562 B) and `superset-companion.jks` (4.4 KB), both dated 2026-07-29. (Not printed.)
- If missing, `release` throws `GradleException` at configuration time with the "phone and watch must be signed with the SAME key" message.
- `gradle.properties` disables the configuration cache **because** of this out-of-tree signing read: `org.gradle.configuration-cache=false`.
- Same directory holds `fcm-service-account.json`, `cloudflare-access.json` — deliberately outside the repo.

- line 309: "one Gradle project, phone and watch sharing an `applicationId` and keystore — the Data Layer silently delivers nothing if either differs"

So: sideload is the intended distribution, explicitly with no update channel. No Play Store, no internal track.

```
cd C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/superset-companion
./gradlew :app-phone:assembleDebug :app-watch:assembleDebug
# then sideload the two debug APKs onto the Pixel phone + Pixel Watch 4
```

Nothing in the repo records the transfer step (no adb command, no device serials, no pairing notes for install). `app-watch` install to a Pixel Watch 4 requires adb-over-Wi-Fi or Play internal delivery — unrecorded either way.

### Gap for a "new installable version"

Doing it properly the first time requires four things that have never happened here: bump `versionCode`/`versionName` in **both** module files together, run `assembleRelease` for both, verify both are signed with the same `~/.superset/companion/keystore` key, and side-load both (watch install has no documented path). ## Desktop fork — `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64`

Fully automated, the exact opposite. Two entry points, one build.

### Manual publish

Dispatch `.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`):

- `publish` (boolean, **default true**) — "Publish the desktop-v\<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)"
- `repair_branch` (string, default = dispatched branch)

Runs `build-attempt-1` on `windows-11-arm` → on failure `repair-1` (Opus 5, credential-less, `scripts/ci-repair.sh collect|agent|push`) → attempt 2 → repair-2 → attempt 3. Max 3 attempts / 2 repairs. `verdict` job is the sole source of truth, outputs `built_sha`. Refuses to run while a nightly is in progress (mutex step).

### Nightly

`.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml` — cron `13 2 * * *`; dispatch inputs `force_tag`, `rehearse`, `rehearse_base`. Concurrency group `nightly-merge`, never cancels.

Flow: compare upstream latest `desktop-v*` against `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt` (**currently `desktop-v1.20.2`**) → merge → Opus 5 resolves conflicts + ports fork call sites → marker/dependency/ReferenceError gates → semantic review loop → assert `desktop-v$(apps/desktop/package.json version)` == `$NEWTAG` → write new baseline → commit `merge upstream <tag>` → push candidate branch → `build` job calls `./.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml` with `ref: <merge sha>`, `publish: true`, `repair_branch: <candidate>` → `advance` fast-forwards `main` to `built_sha` and deletes the candidate.

### Version + release naming

Single source: `apps/desktop/package.json` `version`. In `C:/Users/khair/Code Projects/fork-superset-windows-arm64/scripts/publish-arm64-release.sh`:

```
V=$(node -p "require('./apps/desktop/package.json').version")
TAG="desktop-v${V}"
gh release delete "$TAG" --yes; git push --delete origin "refs/tags/$TAG"
git push origin "$BUILT_SHA:refs/tags/$TAG"
gh release create "$TAG" "$A" --title "Superset $V (Windows ARM64)" --notes "..."
```

## 1. Navigation model

**Routes** — `enum class CompanionRoute { AGENTS, DIAGNOSTICS, PAIRING }`, `app-phone/src/main/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/phone/ui/shell/CompanionShell.kt:32`. Single `when(route)` switch at `CompanionShell.kt:130-189`. No NavHost. Initial route = `AGENTS` if `pairing is PairingState.Paired` else `PAIRING` (`CompanionShell.kt:91-95`). `BackHandler` returns to `AGENTS` (`CompanionShell.kt:116`). Sheet is an overlay, not a route (`CompanionShell.kt:192-235`).

**AGENTS is a list/detail scaffold** — `AgentsPane` (`.../phone/ui/shell/AgentsPane.kt:44`) uses `NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold` (`AgentsPane.kt:84`): listPane = `HomeScreen`, detailPane = `ChatScreen`. `twoPane` computed at `AgentsPane.kt:78-82`; back arrow shown only when not two-pane (`AgentsPane.kt:129`).

**What the top-level list renders** — three nested row kinds plus a fold, from `sealed interface TreeRow` (`.../phone/model/AgentTree.kt:186`):
- `TreeRow.ProjectHeader` (`AgentTree.kt:191`, key `p:<projectId>`) — rendered as a **sticky header** (`.../phone/ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:328`, composable `ProjectHeaderRow` at `HomeScreen.kt:436`). Note user-facing label for a *project* is the word "Workspace": `object UserLabels { const val PROJECT = "Workspace" }` (`AgentTree.kt:37-39`), used only in the expand/collapse content descriptions (`HomeScreen.kt:483-486`).
- `TreeRow.WorkspaceHeader` (`AgentTree.kt:210`, key `ws:<workspaceId>`) — `WorkspaceHeaderRow` (`HomeScreen.kt:534`); shows workspace name + branch (branch hidden when blank or equal to name, `HomeScreen.kt:539`). **Not clickable.**
- `TreeRow.TerminalItem` (`AgentTree.kt:225`, key `t:<terminalId>`) — `TerminalRow` (`HomeScreen.kt:571`); the only navigable row.
- `TreeRow.QuietFold` (`AgentTree.kt:241`, key `q:<projectId>`) — one per project, collapsed bucket of quiet terminals (`HomeScreen.kt:380` `quietFold`, `HomeScreen.kt:751` `QuietFoldRow`).

**Grouping/sorting** (all in `AgentTree.kt`):
- terminals: `terminalOrder` (`AgentTree.kt:274-279`) = status rank → oldest `pendingQuestion.askedAtMs` → most-recent `lastActivityMs` → title.
- workspaces: `workspaceOrder` (`AgentTree.kt:266-272`) = pinned tier → status rank → oldest question → recency → name.
- projects: `compareBy` inside `toRows` (`AgentTree.kt:314-322`) = `pinnedTier(project.pinned)` → rolled-up status rank → min oldest-question across workspaces → max lastActivity desc → project name.
- `AgentStatus.sortRank` NEEDS_INPUT 0 / WORKING 1 / IDLE 2 / UNKNOWN 3 (`AgentTree.kt:27-33`). `pinnedTier` (`AgentTree.kt:139`) treats `null` and `false` identically.

**Taps**:
- Project header tap → collapse/expand only, local `collapsed: Set<String>` of projectIds (`HomeScreen.kt:271`, `HomeScreen.kt:333-339`). Filter: `steady.filter { it is TreeRow.ProjectHeader || it.projectId !in collapsed }` (`HomeScreen.kt:303-305`).
- Workspace header → no gesture.
- Terminal row tap → `onSelectTerminal(terminal.terminalId)` then, if pending, `onOpenQuestion(question.questionId)` (`HomeScreen.kt:598-603`); `AgentsPane.kt:104-112` also `navigator.navigateTo(Detail)`. Click label is `"Answer"` when a question is pending, else `"Open conversation"`.
- Quiet fold tap → toggles `quietOpen: Set<String>` (`HomeScreen.kt:272`, `HomeScreen.kt:365-371`).
- Top bar: Refresh → `session::refresh`; Settings icon → route `DIAGNOSTICS` (`HomeScreen.kt:139-144`).
- Detail (`ChatScreen.kt:130-153`): pending-question banner tap → `onOpenQuestion`; composer sends via `conversation::sendMessage`.
- Notification tap → `MainActivity.consumeQuestionExtra` (`MainActivity.kt:107-114`) → `pendingQuestionId` → `CompanionShell.kt:101-111` selects the owning terminal (`tree.findTerminalForQuestion`), forces route `AGENTS`, `conversation.openQuestion(questionId)`.

---

## 2. Tree → rows

Single function: **`fun TreeSnapshot.toRows(includeIdle: Boolean, nowMs: Long, quietAfterMs: Long = QUIET_AFTER_MS): List<TreeRow>`**, `AgentTree.kt:292-367`. Helpers: `rollupStatus` (`:260`), `oldestQuestionMs` (`:263`), `projectKey`/`workspaceKey` (`:256`,`:258`), `Terminal.isQuiet` (`:162`), `steadyRows` (`:467`), `latchHidesNeedsInput` (`:489`), `latchOrphansRows` (`:523`), `latchMustRelease` (`:548`), `idleTerminalCount` (`:377`), `allTerminals` (`:381`), `withoutQuestions` (`:393`), `pendingQuestionIds` (`:430`).

Flattening is **strictly nested iteration, not a join**: `projects.mapNotNull { project -> project.workspaces.mapNotNull { workspace -> ... } }` (`AgentTree.kt:297-312`), then `ordered.flatMap { (project, workspaces) -> ... }` (`:324-366`) emitting `ProjectHeader` + per-workspace (`WorkspaceHeader` + its `TerminalItem`s) + optional `QuietFold`. `projectId`/`projectName` on each `TerminalItem` are copied *down* from the enclosing project (`:331-332`).

**Workspace with missing/null project** — cannot exist in this model. The wire type has no `projectId` on `Workspace` (`core/src/main/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/core/protocol/Tree.kt:84-100`); workspaces are children of `Project` (`Tree.kt:66-82`). `BridgeMapping.workspace` (`.../phone/data/BridgeMapping.kt:109-118`) copies no parent id. So there is **no orphan branch and no code that handles one** — the phone never re-parents; it inherits. Consequence: a bridge that sent a parentless workspace would have nowhere to put it in JSON at all; a `Project` whose `projectId` is `null`/absent fails decoding outright (see §5).

The only drop branches in `toRows` — the exact code:

```kotlin
            if (shown.isEmpty()) {
                null
            } else {
                // The header's dot must describe the rows under it, not the rows the
                // bridge sent. Re-rolling it here is what keeps "Idle hidden" from
                workspace.copy(terminals = shown, status = rollupStatus(shown.map { it.status }))
            }
```
(`AgentTree.kt:302-309`) and

```kotlin
        if (workspaces.isEmpty()) null else project to workspaces.sortedWith(workspaceOrder)
```
(`AgentTree.kt:311`).

**Unknown/unsupported project kind** — never dropped, never crashes. Decoding falls back to `ProjectKind.UNKNOWN` via `ProjectKindSerializer` (`core/.../protocol/Enums.kt:40-41`, generic fallback in `core/.../protocol/WireEnum.kt:43-47`). `BridgeMapping.projectKind` is an exhaustive `when` over the four members (`BridgeMapping.kt:159-165`) — adding a 5th wire member without recompiling still lands on `UNKNOWN`. Rendering:

```kotlin
private val ProjectKind.label: String?
    get() = when (this) {
        ProjectKind.MULTI_REPO -> "multi-repo"
        ProjectKind.PLAIN -> "folder"
        ProjectKind.GIT, ProjectKind.UNKNOWN -> null
    }
```
(`HomeScreen.kt:519-525`) — unknown kind simply prints no subtitle. `ProjectKind` is not used for ordering, filtering, or answerability anywhere.

**Quiet fold rule** — `Terminal.isQuiet` (`AgentTree.kt:162-167`): never quiet if NEEDS_INPUT/WORKING, never quiet if it holds a pending question, never quiet if `lastActivityMs == null`; else `now - last > QUIET_AFTER_MS` (7 days, `AgentTree.kt:149`). Quiet items get `showWorkspace = true` (`:339`) because their workspace header is suppressed (`:342-345`).

**Freeze/latch** — `HomeScreen.kt:271-302`: touch or scroll → `frozen` (400 ms grace, `FREEZE_GRACE_MS` `HomeScreen.kt:255`) → `latchedOrder = rows.map { it.key }`; `steadyRows` reorders/filters live rows to the latched key order and **never appends** (`AgentTree.kt:467-471`); latch is dropped whenever `latchMustRelease` (new needs-input row hidden, or a rendered row whose parent key is absent) (`HomeScreen.kt:298-300`).

---

## 3. Question flow

**Surfacing**
1. **List badge** — `TerminalRow` renders a primaryContainer card with `question.headline` + `questionLine(...)` (`HomeScreen.kt:638-669`, builder at `HomeScreen.kt:721-740`): `"Waiting <elapsed>"`, `"$questionCount questions"` when `> 1`, `"choose several"` when `multiSelect == true`, then `"answer at the desk"` (not answerable) / `"at last contact · tap to check"` (stale) / `"tap to answer"`. Top-bar `CountStrip` shows `"N waiting"`/`"N working"` (`HomeScreen.kt:409-426`); project header shows a numeric pill of `needsInput` (`HomeScreen.kt:468-476`).
2. **Notification** — FCM `CompanionMessagingService.postQuestion` (`app-phone/src/main/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/push/CompanionMessagingService.kt:150-199`): fetches `repository.loadQuestion`; if `state != QuestionState.PENDING` it retracts instead of posting; on success `CompanionNotifications.postQuestion(detail)` (`.../phone/notifications/CompanionNotifications.kt:106-121`); on failure/timeout `postContentless(questionId, questionCount)` (`:128-139`). Notification tag = questionId, id = `ID_QUESTION`; content intent carries `EXTRA_QUESTION_ID` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:241-244`). Retraction: `retract` (`:176`), foreground `sweep(stillPending)` (`:188-198`) driven by `SessionViewModel.sweepNotifications()` (`.../phone/ui/SessionViewModel.kt:219-238`).
3. **Sheet** — `ConversationViewModel.openQuestion(questionId)` (`.../phone/ui/ConversationViewModel.kt:250-266`) loads `QuestionDetail` and installs `QuestionSheetState(detail, openedAtMs, generation = sheetGenerations.incrementAndGet())`. `CompanionShell.kt:192` renders `QuestionSheet` whenever `sheet != null`.

**What `QuestionSheet` renders** (`.../phone/ui/question/QuestionSheet.kt:83-152`): `ModalBottomSheet` + `LazyColumn` of `SheetHeader` (`:155`), optional `ContextBlock` (last transcript entries, 220.dp scroll strip, `:181`), an unanswerable `NoticeBanner` when `!detail.answerable` (`:113-121`), one `QuestionBlock` per item (`:123-140`), `SheetFooter` (`:489`).
- **single-select**: `SingleSelectOption` buttons (`:294-303`, composable `:323`); tapping calls `onChoose` → `ConversationViewModel.chooseOption` which **submits immediately** when `!requiresExplicitSubmit && allAnswered` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:381-392`).
- **multi-select**: `MultiSelectOption` checkboxes (`:277-286`, composable `:373`) + text "Choosing several. Nothing is sent until you press Submit."; `requiresExplicitSubmit` true (`ConversationViewModel.kt:108-109`).
- **free-text**: `FreeTextOptionBlock` (`:304-312`, composable `:409`) — only offered on non-multiSelect items; `singleLine = true`, `ImeAction.Done`, clamped to `AnswerDraft.FREE_TEXT_MAX` = 4096 (`:456`, `.../phone/model/Question.kt:220`); presence of a `FreeText` choice also forces explicit submit; submit button label becomes `"Confirm and send"` (`:584`).
- **multi-question N>1**: header pill `"${detail.questions.size} questions"` (`:167`), per-block ordinal `"${index+1} of ${size}"` (`:127-131`), submit gated on `allAnswered` = every `questions[i].index` present in `choices` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:111-112`).
- Footer states: `AnswerOutcome.Pending` (spinner + "Check what happened"), `Confirmed` (chip + Done), `Failed` (chip + monospace message, deliberately **no retry**), `Unconfirmed` (chip + check) — `QuestionSheet.kt:504-572`. All send affordances vanish once `state.answerOutstanding` (`:577`).

**Request build + submit**
- `ConversationViewModel.submit(onOutcome)` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:427-528`): guards `answerable`, `allAnswered`, per-choice `AnswerDraft.freeTextError` (`:454-459`); builds `AnswerDraft(questionId, fingerprint, requestId = UUID.randomUUID().toString(), choices, confirmedBiometric = hasFreeText, surface = Surface.PHONE)` (`:470-479`); validates via `AnswerDraft.validationError(detail)` (`.../phone/model/Question.kt:157-217`); takes `LocalAnswerLease.tryAcquire(questionId, requestId)` (`.../phone/data/LocalAnswerLease.kt:35`) and releases in `finally`; calls `repository.submitAnswer(draft)`; result routed through `updateSheetIfStill(questionId, fingerprint, generation)` (`:352-372`) so a stale coroutine cannot write onto a newer sheet; on `Confirmed` pushes `watchBridge.pushResolved(...)`.
- **DTOs**: `AnswerDraft` / `AnswerChoice.Select|MultiSelect|FreeText` (`Question.kt:111-151`) → mapped by **`BridgeMapping.answerRequest(draft)`** (`.../phone/data/BridgeMapping.kt:375-383`) into wire `AnswerRequest(questionId, fingerprint, requestId, answers, confirmedBiometric, surface)` with items `SelectAnswer` / `MultiSelectAnswer` / `FreeTextAnswer` via `answerItem` (`BridgeMapping.kt:385-398`).
- Transport: `BridgeCompanionRepository.submitAnswer` (`.../phone/data/BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:567-641`) — records an `AnswerRecord` before sending, refuses pre-send if the bridge restarted (`write(...)`, `:983-1020`), maps `WireAnswerOutcome` to `AnswerOutcome`, drops the question from the cached tree on confirm (`dropResolvedQuestion`, `:1417`).
- Status re-read: `checkAnswerStatus(requestId, questionId, fingerprint)` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:539-616`) — backoff 400 ms → max 3 s, 30 s deadline; `repository.answerStatusRead` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:643-724`), mapping in `answerOutcomeFor` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:157-228`).
- Sheet auto-invalidation: `watchOpenSheet()` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:283-318`) uses `sheetVerdict(...)` (`.../phone/ui/SheetRevalidation.kt:56-75`); `GONE` → marks detail `answerable = false, unanswerableReason = UnanswerableReason.STALE`.

---

## 4. Locally persisted state

- **`ViewPreferences`** (`.../phone/data/ViewPreferences.kt`): the **only** user-facing view state on disk. File `"companion_view_prefs"`, key `"include_idle"`, default `DEFAULT_INCLUDE_IDLE = false` (`ViewPreferences.kt:42`, `:59-60`). Read once into `SessionViewModel.includeIdleState` (`SessionViewModel.kt:102`), written by `setIncludeIdle` (`:155-160`).
- **Not persisted to disk** — `collapsed` (project collapse) and `quietOpen` are `rememberSaveable` sets in `AgentList` (`HomeScreen.kt:271-272`), i.e. saved-instance-state only, keyed by nothing (lost on cold start). Route + `selectedTerminalId` also `rememberSaveable` (`CompanionShell.kt:91-96`). `ContextBlock` expanded and `ToolChip` expanded likewise (`QuestionSheet.kt:182`, `ChatScreen.kt:300`).
- No filter beyond idle. Curation is **server-side**: `TreeCuration(enabled, lastSyncAgeMs, hiddenWorkspaces)` (`AgentTree.kt:77-81`) mapped from the wire (`BridgeMapping.kt:88-94`) and only *reported* in `emptyListMessage` (`.../phone/model/EmptyListMessage.kt:68-73`). Pins are server-side too (`Project.pinned`/`Workspace.pinned`), never editable on the phone.
- Other prefs files (not view state): `"companion-push-diagnostics"` (`.../phone/notifications/PushDiagnostics.kt:153-167`) and `"companion-background-liveness"` keys `consecutiveFailures`, `needsInputAtLastContact`, `workingAtLastContact` (`.../phone/notifications/BackgroundLivenessWorker.kt:108-111`). Pairing keys/records live in core secure storage under `filesDir/companion` (`.../phone/di/CompanionContainer.kt:81`, `:197`).
- In-memory only: answer records `answersState` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:301`), `questionTerminals`, `submittedCoverage` — all cleared by `forgetPairingLocally()` (`:1207-1226`).

---

## 5. Hardcoded assumptions that would break

1. **`projectId` is a required, non-null wire string.** `core/.../protocol/Tree.kt:67` `val projectId: String` with no default and `explicitNulls = true`, `isLenient = false` in `CompanionJson.format` (`core/.../protocol/CompanionJson.kt:24-31`). A tree containing one project with `"projectId": null` or the field omitted throws `SerializationException` → `ProtocolException` (`CompanionJson.kt:51-55`) → the **entire `/v1/tree` read fails**; `refresh()` takes `is FetchResult.Failure -> watchdog.evaluate(clock())` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:534`) and the phone silently keeps the previous tree. Same for `QuestionSource.projectId` (`core/.../protocol/Question.kt:54`) — one null there breaks the whole question sheet and hence the notification body (falls back to `postContentless`).
2. **A "session"-type entry has no representation.** The tree is exactly 3 levels with no discriminator: `Project.kind` is the only kind field and has 4 members (`Tree.kt:70`, `Enums.kt:32-41`). Anything the desktop calls a session must be squeezed into `Workspace` or `Terminal`; a session emitted as a top-level sibling of `Project` is dropped by `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` **without any log**.
3. **Row identity assumes globally unique ids, and `projectId` doubles as UI group key.** `projectKey(projectId)`/`workspaceKey(workspaceId)` (`AgentTree.kt:256-258`), LazyColumn `key = row.key` (`HomeScreen.kt:328/343/347/390/393`). Two projects sharing a projectId (or an empty-string projectId for orphans) produce duplicate LazyList keys → Compose runtime crash, and `collapsed`/`quietOpen` (`HomeScreen.kt:304`, `:361`) would collapse them as one. `TreeRow.QuietFold.key = "q:$projectId"` (`AgentTree.kt:245`) makes this worse: one fold per projectId.
4. **`state.choices.getValue(item.index)`** — `ConversationViewModel.kt:444`, throws `NoSuchElementException` if reached without `allAnswered`. Currently guarded at `:438-441`, but the guard is the only thing between a partial multi-question answer and a crash.
5. **`AnswerDraft.validationError` indexes by position**: `when (val choice = choices[item.index])` (`Question.kt:174`) — safe only because `:170` first asserts `indexes == question.questions.indices.toList()`; a bridge that numbers questions 1-based or sparsely makes every answer fail validation client-side with `"answers are out of order or incomplete"`.
6. **`CompanionNotifications.postQuestion` throws on an empty question list**: `?: error("question ${detail.questionId} has no items — the bridge must not send that")` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:107-108`). This runs inside the FCM service (`CompanionMessagingService.kt:175`) → a malformed push crashes the messaging service rather than degrading to `postContentless`. `QuestionSheet.SheetHeader` handles the same case gracefully (`QuestionSheet.kt:159` `firstOrNull()?.header.orEmpty()`), so the two disagree.
7. **`submitAnswer` falls back to an empty terminalId**: `?: run { Log.e(...); "" }` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:569-578`). An answer for a question whose terminal is not in the cached tree gets `terminalId = ""`, and `ChatScreen`'s answer log filters `it.terminalId == selectedTerminalId` (`CompanionShell.kt:119-123`), so the record is invisible everywhere.
8. **The "fingerprint" is nominal.** `ConversationViewModel.sendMessage` hardcodes `confirmedBiometric = true` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:640`) and `submit` sets it from `hasFreeText` (`:477`) — `BiometricConfirmer` (`.../phone/security/BiometricConfirmer.kt:22`) is never referenced by any UI or ViewModel (grep: only its own file). The strings "Typing into a live agent asks for your fingerprint first." (`QuestionSheet.kt:475`) and "Typed replies ask for your fingerprint first." (`ChatScreen.kt:418`) and the `Icons.Filled.Fingerprint` send button (`ChatScreen.kt:432`) promise a prompt that never happens.
9. **No `groupBy`, no `!!`, no `requireNotNull`/`checkNotNull` anywhere in `app-phone/src/main`** (verified by grep) — the only `error(` calls are `CompanionNotifications.kt:39` and `:108`. So the orphan risk is a *decoding* failure, not a null-deref.
10. `Workspace.status` from the bridge is deliberately overwritten by a local rollup (`AgentTree.kt:308`), so a bridge that reports a workspace-level status the terminals do not support is silently ignored — intentional, but it means workspace status is unusable as an independent signal.

---

## 6. Unit tests

All under `app-phone/src/test/java/family/khaira/supersetcompanion/`.

- **`.../phone/model/AgentTreeRowsTest.kt`** (27 tests, the main one). Idle filter: hides idle *terminals* not workspaces (`:24`), an emptied workspace takes its header and project with it (`:45`, asserts exact keys `["p:p2","ws:w2","t:t2"]`), filtered workspace header re-rolls its dot (`:57`), `idleTerminalCount` equals what the filter removed (`:80`). Grouping/order: project rows contiguous with exactly one header (`:103`), red leads (`:124`), oldest question first (`:140`), pinned is a tier above status (`:156`), absent pin == explicit false (`:174`), header counts include collapsed content (`:185`). Quiet fold: folds past threshold and sets `showWorkspace` (`:211`), 2-day-old row is not quiet (`:234`), nothing with a pending question is ever folded (`:244`), **null `lastActivityMs` is not "ancient"** (`:273`), all-quiet workspace contributes no header (`:287`), branch printed only on folded rows (`:300`). Freeze/latch: `steadyRows` identity when unfrozen (`:316`), keeps order + live contents (`:324`), drops vanished rows (`:356`), new needs-input releases the latch (`:377`), already-latched red does not (`:401`), a non-waiting new row keeps the freeze (`:412`), **a workspace moving to another project releases the latch** (`:455`, the orphan case), new project mid-press does not release (`:480`), a whole project disappearing does not orphan (`:497`).
- **`.../phone/model/EmptyListMessageTest.kt`** (13 tests): never-arrived tree does not claim calm (`:24`), unreachable desktop defers to the banner (`:37`), stale tree speaks past tense (`:52`), only a live empty tree claims calm (`:59`), filter-emptied list says so (`:67`), hidden count suppressed over a never-arrived tree (`:76`), curation-emptied list says so (`:99`), singular "thread" (`:111`), curation that hid nothing still claims calm (`:124`), disabled curation is never the cause (`:140`).
- **`.../phone/model/TreeFreshnessTest.kt`**: absent ≠ stale (`:19`), inside watchdog window is live (`:28`), one ms past is stale (`:36`), backwards clock clamps (`:48`), seconds are readable (`:57`).
- **`.../phone/ui/SheetRevalidationTest.kt`** (8 tests on `sheetVerdict`): newer tree still listing the question leaves it answerable (`:46`), terminal back at work settles it (`:51`), terminal now holding a *different* question settles it (`:58`), a curated tree missing the terminal proves nothing (`:63`), older tree proves nothing (`:76`), no tree proves nothing (`:87`), unusable connection proves nothing (`:95`), the phone's own in-flight answer is never reported as stale (`:105`).
- **`.../phone/ui/SheetGenerationTest.kt`** (5 tests on `QuestionSheetState.isStill`/`answerOutstanding`): verdict lands on the originating sheet (`:54`), a verdict from a previous sheet of the same question is refused (`:61`), questionId alone is insufficient (`:73`), fresh sheet has no outcome (`:84`), any outcome makes it outstanding (`:93`).

lo = max(client.min, bridge.min); hi = min(client.max, bridge.max)
protocol = (lo <= hi) ? hi : 0 ; degraded = (lo > hi)

**Ordering / dedupe** — three drop clauses, not arrival order (L471-511):
- `outstanding != null && outstanding != result.requestId` → drop (late news for a dead request).
- `stored != null && !WatchAnswerStatus.supersedes(result.status, stored)` → drop. Lattice (`WearProtocol.kt:153-157`): stored `confirmed` → nothing supersedes; stored `failed` → only `confirmed`; stored non-terminal/unknown → anything. Refuses duplicate terminals too.
- `outstanding == null && onScreen != null && onScreen != result.questionId` → drop (adopting would mislabel).
Drops are `Log.i(TAG, "dropping stale answer result: $dropReason")`, never a crash.

**Retries** — none, by contract. `WearProtocol.kt:34-35`: "The watch NEVER retries a write (§11.4)." No retry code path exists; `PhoneLink` sends once per call.

## 4. Answer flow: wrist tap → phone

**Build** — `MainActivity.sendAnswer()` (`app-watch/.../wear/MainActivity.kt:107-206`):
1. Race guards (all `return`, never throw; comment L108-111 "Every guard below is a RACE guard"): question not `Present` → drop (L115); `state.answer !is AnswerState.None` → drop (L119); any item with no selection → drop (L127-137); `WatchChoice.Multi` with empty `optionIndexes` → drop (L143-153).
2. Maps `WatchChoice` → `WatchAnswerItem` for **every** item, in item order (L125-163).
3. `val requestId = UUID.randomUUID().toString()` (L167) — "Minted once, here. Regenerating it for the same user action would defeat the idempotency…(§11.4)".
4. `confirmedBiometric = answers.any { it is WatchAnswerItem.FreeText }` (L176) — true iff free text present; biometric ceremony removed 2026-08-09.
5. `QuestionStore.onAnswerSent(requestId, questionId)` → `AnswerState.Pending` + starts the timeout job (L179).

**Send** — `PhoneLink.sendAnswer` (`PhoneLink.kt:58-65`), two hard preconditions before the wire:
```kotlin
require(intent.answers.isNotEmpty()) { "answer intent with no items: ${intent.requestId}" }
require(intent.answers.map { it.questionIndex } == intent.answers.indices.toList()) { ... }
```
`send()` (L91-134): 10 s `TASK_TIMEOUT_MS`; size check; `Wearable.getNodeClient().connectedNodes`; empty → `PhoneUnreachableException("no connected phone — the watch has no other route to the desktop")`; else sends to **every** connected node; if `delivered == 0` → `SendAmbiguousException("message on $path reached no node (…) — attempted, so delivery is unknown, not disproven")`.

**Local outcome of send failure** — MainActivity L182-204: `PhoneUnreachableException` → synthesised `WatchAnswerResult(status = FAILED, failureCode = WATCH_FAILURE_NOT_SENT)`; `SendAmbiguousException` → synthesised `status = UNCONFIRMED`.

**Ack** — phone replies on `ANSWER_RESULT` → `QuestionStore.onAnswerResult` (L432-524). Status mapping: `confirmed`→`Confirmed`; `failed`→`Failed`, and a `failed` with null `failureCode` **throws** `IllegalArgumentException("failed answer result carries no failureCode: …")` (L443-445); everything else (incl. `unknown` and unrecognised tokens) → `Unconfirmed`.

**Ordering / dedupe** — three drop clauses, not arrival order (L471-511):
- `outstanding != null && outstanding != result.requestId` → drop (late news for a dead request).
- `stored != null && !WatchAnswerStatus.supersedes(result.status, stored)` → drop. Lattice (`WearProtocol.kt:153-157`): stored `confirmed` → nothing supersedes; stored `failed` → only `confirmed`; stored non-terminal/unknown → anything. Refuses duplicate terminals too.
- `outstanding == null && onScreen != null && onScreen != result.questionId` → drop (adopting would mislabel).
Drops are `Log.i(TAG, "dropping stale answer result: $dropReason")`, never a crash.

**Retries** — none, by contract. `WearProtocol.kt:34-35`: "The watch NEVER retries a write (§11.4)." No retry code path exists; `PhoneLink` sends once per call.

**Staleness / expiry** — `ANSWER_RESULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000L` (QuestionStore.kt:30). `onAnswerSent` L416-430 launches a job: after 30 s, if `answer` is still `Pending` with the same `requestId`, flips to `Unconfirmed` — **never** `Failed`. Cancelled on any applied result (L520).

**Recovery read** — `checkAnswerStatus()` (MainActivity.kt:209-231) → `PhoneLink.requestAnswerStatus` → `ANSWER_STATUS_REQUEST` with `WatchAnswerStatusRequest(requestId)`. Only fires when state is `Unconfirmed`; read failure is logged and state stays `unconfirmed` ("nothing is inferred from a failure").

**Render of outcomes** — `AnswerStateScreen` (`app-watch/.../wear/ui/AnswerStateScreen.kt:32-111`), and it outranks everything: `WatchRoot.kt:73-80` renders it and returns whenever `state.answer !is AnswerState.None`.
- `Pending`: title `"Sending…"`, caption `"The desktop is typing your answer into the picker."`
- `Confirmed`: `"Answered"` / `"The desktop confirmed it."` + button `"Done"`.
- `Failed`: `explainFailure(code, detail)` title+detail, then raw `"(${answer.code})"`, then button `"Dismiss"`.
- `Unconfirmed`: `"Not confirmed"`, body `"The answer may or may not have gone through. The watch will not send it again — a repeat could answer a different question."`, buttons `"Check status"` and `"Leave it"`.
- `None`: `"Nothing sent"` (unreachable via WatchRoot).

`explainFailure` (L125-204) — exact code→(title, detail):

| code | title | detail |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_held` | Phone is answering | `"$detail holds the answer. Refused — not queued."` / fallback `"Another device holds the answer. Refused — not queued."` |
| `already_resolved` | Already answered | detail ?: `"Someone answered this first. Nothing was sent."` |
| `stale_question` | Moved on | `"The question changed or was closed. Nothing was written."` |
| `guard_failed` | Refused at the desk | `"The $detail check failed, so nothing was typed."` / `"A pre-write check failed, so nothing was typed."` |
| `capability_unsupported` | Not supported | `"The desktop cannot do this yet. Answer at the desk."` |
| `session_expired` | Desktop restarted | detail ?: `"The connection was rebuilt. Nothing was sent — try again."` |
| `write_disabled` | Writes disabled | `"Panic write-disable is on. Re-enable it at the desktop."` |
| `"access_denied"` (literal) | Access denied | detail ?: `"This device may need re-pairing."` |
| `unknown_device`, `"not_paired"` | Not paired | `"The phone needs to pair with the desktop again."` |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests | `"Wait a moment, then try at the desk."` |
| `"bridge_unavailable"`, `"edge_unverifiable"` | Desktop busy | `"The bridge is not answering. Nothing was sent."` |
| `not_sent` | Not sent | `"The phone could not be reached, so nothing left the watch."` |
| `request_closed` | Closed, not answered | `"The desktop has a durable record that this never arrived. Nothing was typed — answer it again."` |
| `picker_open` | Prompt on screen | `"A prompt is open at the desk, so a message would have committed an answer. Nothing was sent."` |
| `revoked` | Device revoked | `"This pairing was revoked at the desktop. Pair again to use it."` |
| `transport` | Couldn't reach the desktop | detail ?: `"The answer did not get through. Nothing is known about it — check before answering again."` |
| `internal` | Desktop error | detail ?: `"Something went wrong at the desk. Check the terminal."` |
| else | Failed | detail ?: `"The desktop refused it."` |

Note: `WatchFailureCode.UNKNOWN_QUESTION ("unknown_question")`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `REPLAY_DETECTED` have **no** arm → fall to `Failed` / `"The desktop refused it."`.

## 5. Hardcoded assumptions that would break

1. **`projectId` is a required, non-null wire string.** `core/.../protocol/Tree.kt:67` `val projectId: String` with no default and `explicitNulls = true`, `isLenient = false` in `CompanionJson.format` (`core/.../protocol/CompanionJson.kt:24-31`). A tree containing one project with `"projectId": null` or the field omitted throws `SerializationException` → `ProtocolException` (`CompanionJson.kt:51-55`) → the **entire `/v1/tree` read fails**; `refresh()` takes `is FetchResult.Failure -> watchdog.evaluate(clock())` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:534`) and the phone silently keeps the previous tree. Same for `QuestionSource.projectId` (`core/.../protocol/Question.kt:54`) — one null there breaks the whole question sheet and hence the notification body (falls back to `postContentless`).
2. **A "session"-type entry has no representation.** The tree is exactly 3 levels with no discriminator: `Project.kind` is the only kind field and has 4 members (`Tree.kt:70`, `Enums.kt:32-41`). Anything the desktop calls a session must be squeezed into `Workspace` or `Terminal`; a session emitted as a top-level sibling of `Project` is dropped by `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` **without any log**.
3. **Row identity assumes globally unique ids, and `projectId` doubles as UI group key.** `projectKey(projectId)`/`workspaceKey(workspaceId)` (`AgentTree.kt:256-258`), LazyColumn `key = row.key` (`HomeScreen.kt:328/343/347/390/393`). Two projects sharing a projectId (or an empty-string projectId for orphans) produce duplicate LazyList keys → Compose runtime crash, and `collapsed`/`quietOpen` (`HomeScreen.kt:304`, `:361`) would collapse them as one. `TreeRow.QuietFold.key = "q:$projectId"` (`AgentTree.kt:245`) makes this worse: one fold per projectId.

6. **`CompanionNotifications.postQuestion` throws on an empty question list**: `?: error("question ${detail.questionId} has no items — the bridge must not send that")` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:107-108`). This runs inside the FCM service (`CompanionMessagingService.kt:175`) → a malformed push crashes the messaging service rather than degrading to `postContentless`. `QuestionSheet.SheetHeader` handles the same case gracefully (`QuestionSheet.kt:159` `firstOrNull()?.header.orEmpty()`), so the two disagree.
7. **`submitAnswer` falls back to an empty terminalId**: `?: run { Log.e(...); "" }` (`BridgeCompanionRepository.kt:569-578`). An answer for a question whose terminal is not in the cached tree gets `terminalId = ""`, and `ChatScreen`'s answer log filters `it.terminalId == selectedTerminalId` (`CompanionShell.kt:119-123`), so the record is invisible everywhere.
8. **The "fingerprint" is nominal.** `ConversationViewModel.sendMessage` hardcodes `confirmedBiometric = true` (`ConversationViewModel.kt:640`) and `submit` sets it from `hasFreeText` (`:477`) — `BiometricConfirmer` (`.../phone/security/BiometricConfirmer.kt:22`) is never referenced by any UI or ViewModel (grep: only its own file). The strings "Typing into a live agent asks for your fingerprint first." (`QuestionSheet.kt:475`) and "Typed replies ask for your fingerprint first." (`ChatScreen.kt:418`) and the `Icons.Filled.Fingerprint` send button (`ChatScreen.kt:432`) promise a prompt that never happens.
9. **No `groupBy`, no `!!`, no `requireNotNull`/`checkNotNull` anywhere in `app-phone/src/main`** (verified by grep) — the only `error(` calls are `CompanionNotifications.kt:39` and `:108`. So the orphan risk is a *decoding* failure, not a null-deref.

## 4. Answer flow: wrist tap → phone

**Build** — `MainActivity.sendAnswer()` (`app-watch/.../wear/MainActivity.kt:107-206`):
1. Race guards (all `return`, never throw; comment L108-111 "Every guard below is a RACE guard"): question not `Present` → drop (L115); `state.answer !is AnswerState.None` → drop (L119); any item with no selection → drop (L127-137); `WatchChoice.Multi` with empty `optionIndexes` → drop (L143-153).
2. Maps `WatchChoice` → `WatchAnswerItem` for **every** item, in item order (L125-163).
3. `val requestId = UUID.randomUUID().toString()` (L167) — "Minted once, here. Regenerating it for the same user action would defeat the idempotency…(§11.4)".
4. `confirmedBiometric = answers.any { it is WatchAnswerItem.FreeText }` (L176) — true iff free text present; biometric ceremony removed 2026-08-09.
5. `QuestionStore.onAnswerSent(requestId, questionId)` → `AnswerState.Pending` + starts the timeout job (L179).

**Send** — `PhoneLink.sendAnswer` (`PhoneLink.kt:58-65`), two hard preconditions before the wire:
```kotlin
require(intent.answers.isNotEmpty()) { "answer intent with no items: ${intent.requestId}" }
require(intent.answers.map { it.questionIndex } == intent.answers.indices.toList()) { ... }
```
`send()` (L91-134): 10 s `TASK_TIMEOUT_MS`; size check; `Wearable.getNodeClient().connectedNodes`; empty → `PhoneUnreachableException("no connected phone — the watch has no other route to the desktop")`; else sends to **every** connected node; if `delivered == 0` → `SendAmbiguousException("message on $path reached no node (…) — attempted, so delivery is unknown, not disproven")`.

**Local outcome of send failure** — MainActivity L182-204: `PhoneUnreachableException` → synthesised `WatchAnswerResult(status = FAILED, failureCode = WATCH_FAILURE_NOT_SENT)`; `SendAmbiguousException` → synthesised `status = UNCONFIRMED`.

**Ack** — phone replies on `ANSWER_RESULT` → `QuestionStore.onAnswerResult` (L432-524). Status mapping: `confirmed`→`Confirmed`; `failed`→`Failed`, and a `failed` with null `failureCode` **throws** `IllegalArgumentException("failed answer result carries no failureCode: …")` (L443-445); everything else (incl. `unknown` and unrecognised tokens) → `Unconfirmed`.

**Ordering / dedupe** — three drop clauses, not arrival order (L471-511):
- `outstanding != null && outstanding != result.requestId` → drop (late news for a dead request).
- `stored != null && !WatchAnswerStatus.supersedes(result.status, stored)` → drop. Lattice (`WearProtocol.kt:153-157`): stored `confirmed` → nothing supersedes; stored `failed` → only `confirmed`; stored non-terminal/unknown → anything. Refuses duplicate terminals too.
- `outstanding == null && onScreen != null && onScreen != result.questionId` → drop (adopting would mislabel).
Drops are `Log.i(TAG, "dropping stale answer result: $dropReason")`, never a crash.

**Retries** — none, by contract. `WearProtocol.kt:34-35`: "The watch NEVER retries a write (§11.4)." No retry code path exists; `PhoneLink` sends once per call.

**Staleness / expiry** — `ANSWER_RESULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000L` (QuestionStore.kt:30). `onAnswerSent` L416-430 launches a job: after 30 s, if `answer` is still `Pending` with the same `requestId`, flips to `Unconfirmed` — **never** `Failed`. Cancelled on any applied result (L520).

**Recovery read** — `checkAnswerStatus()` (MainActivity.kt:209-231) → `PhoneLink.requestAnswerStatus` → `ANSWER_STATUS_REQUEST` with `WatchAnswerStatusRequest(requestId)`. Only fires when state is `Unconfirmed`; read failure is logged and state stays `unconfirmed` ("nothing is inferred from a failure").

**Render of outcomes** — `AnswerStateScreen` (`app-watch/.../wear/ui/AnswerStateScreen.kt:32-111`), and it outranks everything: `WatchRoot.kt:73-80` renders it and returns whenever `state.answer !is AnswerState.None`.
- `Pending`: title `"Sending…"`, caption `"The desktop is typing your answer into the picker."`
- `Confirmed`: `"Answered"` / `"The desktop confirmed it."` + button `"Done"`.
- `Failed`: `explainFailure(code, detail)` title+detail, then raw `"(${answer.code})"`, then button `"Dismiss"`.
- `Unconfirmed`: `"Not confirmed"`, body `"The answer may or may not have gone through. The watch will not send it again — a repeat could answer a different question."`, buttons `"Check status"` and `"Leave it"`.
- `None`: `"Nothing sent"` (unreachable via WatchRoot).

`explainFailure` (L125-204) — exact code→(title, detail):

| code | title | detail |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_held` | Phone is answering | `"$detail holds the answer. Refused — not queued."` / fallback `"Another device holds the answer. Refused — not queued."` |
| `already_resolved` | Already answered | detail ?: `"Someone answered this first. Nothing was sent."` |
| `stale_question` | Moved on | `"The question changed or was closed. Nothing was written."` |
| `guard_failed` | Refused at the desk | `"The $detail check failed, so nothing was typed."` / `"A pre-write check failed, so nothing was typed."` |
| `capability_unsupported` | Not supported | `"The desktop cannot do this yet. Answer at the desk."` |
| `session_expired` | Desktop restarted | detail ?: `"The connection was rebuilt. Nothing was sent — try again."` |
| `write_disabled` | Writes disabled | `"Panic write-disable is on. Re-enable it at the desktop."` |
| `"access_denied"` (literal) | Access denied | detail ?: `"This device may need re-pairing."` |
| `unknown_device`, `"not_paired"` | Not paired | `"The phone needs to pair with the desktop again."` |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests | `"Wait a moment, then try at the desk."` |
| `"bridge_unavailable"`, `"edge_unverifiable"` | Desktop busy | `"The bridge is not answering. Nothing was sent."` |
| `not_sent` | Not sent | `"The phone could not be reached, so nothing left the watch."` |
| `request_closed` | Closed, not answered | `"The desktop has a durable record that this never arrived. Nothing was typed — answer it again."` |
| `picker_open` | Prompt on screen | `"A prompt is open at the desk, so a message would have committed an answer. Nothing was sent."` |
| `revoked` | Device revoked | `"This pairing was revoked at the desktop. Pair again to use it."` |
| `transport` | Couldn't reach the desktop | detail ?: `"The answer did not get through. Nothing is known about it — check before answering again."` |
| `internal` | Desktop error | detail ?: `"Something went wrong at the desk. Check the terminal."` |
| else | Failed | detail ?: `"The desktop refused it."` |

Note: `WatchFailureCode.UNKNOWN_QUESTION ("unknown_question")`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `REPLAY_DETECTED` have **no** arm → fall to `Failed` / `"The desktop refused it."`.

<result>## 1. How a question reaches the watch

Nothing is persisted on the wear node, so there is nothing to prune; "retraction" is an explicit message.

Publishers, all in `WatchBridge` (`.../phone/wear/WatchBridge.kt`):

| trigger | call site | what is sent |
|---|---|---|
| FCM `PushKind.QUESTION`, question still PENDING | `push/CompanionMessagingService.kt:180-182` → `pushQuestion` (WatchBridge.kt:125) | `WatchQuestion` on `/companion/v1/question` |
| FCM question, already resolved on arrival | `CompanionMessagingService.kt:169-172` → `pushQuestionById` (WatchBridge.kt:152) | notification retracted + `WatchQuestionResolved` |
| FCM `PushKind.RETRACT` | `push/PushRouting.kt:58-62` → `CompanionMessagingService.kt:104-112` | `WatchQuestionResolved(resolvedAtMs=null, surface=UNKNOWN, outcome=UNKNOWN)` |
| watch foreground hello | `WatchBridge.onHello:351-362` | `WatchConnection` + **one** question (oldest pending in the cached tree) |
| watch asks for a body | `onQuestionRequest:342` → `pushQuestionById` | question or resolved |
| phone answers on its own sheet | `phone/ui/ConversationViewModel.kt:515-525` | `pushResolved(PHONE, ANSWERED, resolvedAtMs)` |
| phone foreground sweep | `phone/ui/SessionViewModel.kt:219-238` | `pushResolved(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN)` per swept id |
| status poll settles | `ConversationViewModel.kt:596-608` → `pushSettledOutcome` (WatchBridge.kt:114) | `WatchAnswerResult` |
| connection state changes | `SupersetCompanionApp.kt:47-51` (process-scoped, never cancelled) | `WatchConnection` |

Gates before a question goes out:
- Expiry, inclusive: `PushRouting.kt:55` `if (push.isExpired(nowMs)) return PushRoute.EXPIRED` → nothing posted, nothing sent to watch.
- `unrenderableReason` (WatchBridge.kt:373-387): empty items or non-contiguous item/option indices → `Refused`, logged at error, watch told nothing.

    android:name="com.google.android.wearable.notificationBridgeMode"
