8	/**
9	 * (SIDEBAR-MIRROR) Publishes the renderer's sidebar CURATION into `host.db`.
10	 *
11	 * Everything the user decides about a thread — where it sits, whether it is
12	 * hidden, archived, snoozed, completed, binned, pinned, and in what order —
13	 * lives in two `localStorage` collections that only this process can read.
14	 * Anything outside the renderer that wants to show "the user's sidebar" is
15	 * otherwise reading raw `host.db`, which is every project, workspace and
16	 * session the machine has ever created with no notion of any of those
17	 * judgements. This hook is the one place that closes that gap.
18	 *
19	 * WHY A WHOLE-SNAPSHOT PUSH, NOT PER-MUTATION WRITES. Curation has no single
20	 * choke point: context menus, bulk actions, kanban drags, the snooze submenu,
21	 * drag-reordering and the CLI worktree placer all mutate these collections
22	 * independently, and a new entry point is added roughly every feature. Emitting
23	 * a delta from each one means the mirror is only ever as correct as the last
24	 * person who remembered — and forgetting is silent. Deriving the entire
25	 * snapshot from the collections instead makes the correctness condition
26	 * "something changed", which the live queries below observe for free. It is
27	 * also what makes the mirror SELF-HEALING: a failed sync, a host-service
28	 * restart, or a renderer reload all repair themselves on the next push.
29	 *
30	 * THE DEBOUNCE IS NOT AN OPTIMISATION. Dragging a thread emits a tabOrder write
31	 * per frame; a bulk bin emits one per selected row. Coalescing to a single
32	 * trailing push per quiet period keeps a drag from turning into a hundred
33	 * full-table replaces, and because each push is a complete snapshot, the
34	 * coalesced result is identical to the last one that would have been sent.
35	 *
36	 * ABSENCE IS SAFE; STALENESS IS NOT. Consumers are required to treat a MISSING
37	 * row as "no opinion recorded" and SHOW the row (see `db/schema.ts`), so an
38	 * unfilled mirror can only ever be too noisy. A STALE row is a different animal
39	 * and the two must not be conflated: a row still carrying `deletedAt` /
40	 * `archivedAt` / `isHidden` / `snoozeUntil` from before the user restored the
41	 * thread HIDES something that is no longer hidden — precisely the forbidden
42	 * direction. Nothing about a full-snapshot replace makes that self-correcting on
43	 * its own, so the two mechanisms below are load-bearing, not defensive polish:
44	 *
45	 *  - ONE PUSH IN FLIGHT AT A TIME. Two snapshots on separate loopback
46	 *    connections have no ordering guarantee. If the older one is served last,
47	 *    `host.db` keeps the older snapshot while `lastSyncedSignatureRef` believes
48	 *    the newer one landed, and every future push is suppressed until the next
49	 *    curation change. Serializing removes the reorder, not just its likelihood.
50	 *  - THE RETRY NEVER GIVES UP while the app runs (`RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS`). A
51	 *    bounded retry has a terminal state — attempts exhausted, no signature
52	 *    change coming, a host-service that restarted on the same port so
53	 *    `activeHostUrl` never changes either — and that terminal state is a mirror
54	 *    frozen with stale HIDING fields forever.
55	 *
56	 * What is left after both is the honest floor: with the renderer gone, the
57	 * mirror holds the user's LAST RECORDED curation. It is never an invented
58	 * opinion, and while the renderer runs it lags by at most the debounce plus one
59	 * retry backoff.
60	 *
61	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	 * (MIRROR-HEARTBEAT) THE UNCHANGED SNAPSHOT IS ALSO WORTH PUSHING
63	 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	 * The signature gate below exists to stop identical snapshots from being
65	 * re-sent, and taken alone it makes `sidebar_mirror_meta.last_full_sync_at_ms`
66	 * measure the last CURATION CHANGE rather than renderer liveness. That is not a
67	 * documentation footnote, it is a correctness hole in the consumer: the mirror's
68	 * only permitted failure direction is "too noisy", and the only way a consumer
69	 * can fail toward SHOWING when the desktop is gone is to age the mirror out
70	 * against a timestamp that means "a renderer was alive at this moment". A
71	 * timestamp that only moves when somebody drags a thread cannot carry that
72	 * meaning — an untouched sidebar is indistinguishable from a quit app.
73	 *
74	 * So two things force a push that the signature gate would otherwise suppress:
75	 *
76	 *  - THE LAUNCH ID. `APP_LAUNCH_ID` is a fresh uuid per renderer load and it is
77	 *    the ONLY thing that can evaluate an "until next launch" snooze
78	 *    (`snooze_launch_id === app_launch_id` on the read side). It is carried in
79	 *    the meta row, NOT in the snapshot, so it is invisible to the signature: a
80	 *    launch whose curation happens to serialize identically to the previous
81	 *    one's would leave the mirror claiming the OLD launch, and every thread
82	 *    snoozed-until-next-launch during that old launch stays hidden on the phone
83	 *    even though the desktop already un-snoozed it. Pushing whenever the last
84	 *    PUSHED launch differs from the current one removes that dependence on the
85	 *    snapshot happening to change.
86	 *  - THE HEARTBEAT. Every `MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS` the same snapshot is re-sent, so
87	 *    the meta timestamp advances while a renderer is alive whether or not the
88	 *    user touched anything. The push is a full idempotent replace, so a repeat
89	 *    is free of consequence beyond one loopback request per five minutes — and
90	 *    it is what lets the consumer treat an OLD `last_full_sync_at_ms` as "no
91	 *    renderer is running, stop trusting this curation" instead of "nobody has
92	 *    reordered their sidebar today". It also bounds an otherwise unbounded case
93	 *    the signature gate has: a host-service that restarts against a DIFFERENT
94	 *    `host.db` while the renderer keeps running is reachable only by a push the
95	 *    signature gate suppresses, and the heartbeat caps that at one interval.
96	 */

98	/** Trailing debounce. Long enough to swallow a drag, short enough to feel live. */
99	const SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1_000;

101	/**
102	 * Retry schedule after a failed push. Unlike the first cut of this hook, it does
103	 * NOT stop: every attempt past the schedule waits `RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS`, forever.
104	 * Stopping looked cheap while "stale is safe" was believed, but a mirror holding
105	 * a stale `deletedAt`/`archivedAt`/`snoozeUntil` HIDES a live thread, and the
106	 * exhausted state has no exit — it re-arms only on a curation change or a new
107	 * `activeHostUrl`, and a host-service that restarts on the same port produces
108	 * neither. One request per five minutes against loopback is not a cost worth a
109	 * permanently wrong mirror.
110	 */
111	const RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [5_000, 15_000, 45_000, 120_000] as const;
112	const RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS = 300_000;
113	
114	/**
115	 * (MIRROR-HEARTBEAT) How often the UNCHANGED snapshot is re-sent.
116	 *
117	 * This is the resolution of the consumer's staleness signal, so it is chosen
118	 * against the consumer's age-out window (`sidebar-filter.ts`) rather than
119	 * against any cost here: the window has to be comfortably more than one
120	 * interval so a single missed or retried push cannot make a live desktop look

122	 * trusted in minutes rather than hours. One idempotent full replace over
123	 * loopback every five minutes is not a load worth trading that for.
124	 */
125	const MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS = 300_000;

157	/**
158	 * A curation timestamp, or null. Anything that is not a finite non-negative
159	 * number is not a timestamp a human action produced — it is a corrupt persisted
160	 * row — and it is mapped to "absent" rather than sent on. Sending it would fail
161	 * the bridge's boundary validation and reject the WHOLE snapshot, freezing the
162	 * mirror on one bad row; absent is the fail-toward-showing direction. The count
163	 * is surfaced by the caller so this stays visible rather than silent.
164	 */
165	function toEpochMs(value: unknown, reject: () => void): number | null {
166		if (value == null) return null;
167		if (typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
168			reject();
169			return null;
170		}
171		return Math.trunc(value);
172	}

174	/** Manual drag order. Negative is legitimate (prepend); non-finite is not. */
175	function toTabOrder(value: unknown, reject: () => void): number {
176		if (typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
177			reject();
178			return 0;
179		}
180		return Math.trunc(value);
181	}

184	 * A non-empty id, or null. These fields are typed `string`, but they are NOT

187	 * deliberately refuses to synthesize identity fields — `workspaceId` and
188	 * `sidebarState.projectId` "must come from the stored row" or not at all. A
189	 * legacy or corrupt row therefore hands back `undefined` behind a `string`

197	function toNullableId(value: unknown): string | null {

207	 * trusted, and it is what makes the crash below impossible to reintroduce.
208	 */
209	interface LocalStateRowLike {
210		workspaceId: unknown;
211		projectId: unknown;
212		sectionId: unknown;
213		tabOrder: unknown;
214		isHidden: unknown;
215		archivedAt: unknown;

217		snoozeLaunchId: unknown;

230	/**
231	 * Derive the snapshot the mirror publishes from the two collections.
232	 *
233	 * Sorted by key, so the signature the hook derives from it is a function of
234	 * CONTENT only — without that, every live-query emission would produce a new
235	 * signature and re-push an identical snapshot.
236	 *
237	 * Exported, and free of React, so the normalization can be exercised directly;
238	 * `useSidebarMirrorSync` is the only production caller.
239	 */
240	export function buildMirrorSnapshot(
241		localStateRows: readonly LocalStateRowLike[],
242		sidebarProjectRows: readonly SidebarProjectRowLike[],
243	): MirrorSnapshot {
244		let rejectedFields = 0;
245		let droppedRows = 0;
246		const reject = (): void => {
247			rejectedFields += 1;
248		};
249		const workspaces = localStateRows
250			.map((row): MirrorWorkspaceRow | null => {
251				// Identity and placement go through `toNullableId` for the reason
252				// documented on it: both are `string` by declared type and can be
253				// `undefined` at runtime, so this must be a null check and never a
254				// `.length` one.
255				const workspaceId = toNullableId(row.workspaceId);
256				const projectId = toNullableId(row.projectId);
257				// A row with no identity, or whose placement project is missing, cannot
258				// be mirrored: the column is NOT NULL on the far side, and a placement
259				// of "nowhere" is not a statement the mirror can make. Dropping it means
260				// the consumer sees no opinion and shows the thread — the safe direction.
261				if (workspaceId === null || projectId === null) {
262					droppedRows += 1;
263					return null;
264				}
265				return {
266					workspaceId,
267					projectId,
268					sectionId: toNullableId(row.sectionId),
269					tabOrder: toTabOrder(row.tabOrder, reject),
270					isHidden: row.isHidden === true,
271					archivedAt: toEpochMs(row.archivedAt, reject),
272					snoozeUntil: toEpochMs(row.snoozeUntil, reject),
273					snoozeLaunchId: toNullableId(row.snoozeLaunchId),
274					completedAt: toEpochMs(row.completedAt, reject),
275					deletedAt: toEpochMs(row.deletedAt, reject),
276					pinnedAt: toEpochMs(row.pinnedAt, reject),
277				};
278			})
279			.filter((row): row is MirrorWorkspaceRow => row !== null)
280			.sort((left, right) => left.workspaceId.localeCompare(right.workspaceId));
281	
282		const projects = sidebarProjectRows
283			.map((row): MirrorProjectRow | null => {
284				const projectId = toNullableId(row.projectId);
285				if (projectId === null) {
286					droppedRows += 1;
287					return null;
288				}
289				return {
290					projectId,
291					tabOrder: toTabOrder(row.tabOrder, reject),
292					isPinned: row.isPinned === true,
293					isCollapsed: row.isCollapsed === true,
294				};
295			})
296			.filter((row): row is MirrorProjectRow => row !== null)
297			.sort((left, right) => left.projectId.localeCompare(right.projectId));
298	
299		return { workspaces, projects, rejectedFields, droppedRows };
300	}

351	}

407					// whether a later snapshot needs pushing has to agree with the

/**
 * (SIDEBAR-MIRROR) Publishes the renderer's sidebar CURATION into `host.db`.
 *
 * Everything the user decides about a thread — where it sits, whether it is
 * hidden, archived, snoozed, completed, binned, pinned, and in what order —
 * lives in two `localStorage` collections that only this process can read.
 * Anything outside the renderer that wants to show "the user's sidebar" is
 * otherwise reading raw `host.db`, which is every project, workspace and
 * session the machine has ever created with no notion of any of those
 * judgements. This hook is the one place that closes that gap.
 *
 * WHY A WHOLE-SNAPSHOT PUSH, NOT PER-MUTATION WRITES. Curation has no single
 * choke point: context menus, bulk actions, kanban drags, the snooze submenu,
 * drag-reordering and the CLI worktree placer all mutate these collections
 * independently, and a new entry point is added roughly every feature. Emitting
 * a delta from each one means the mirror is only ever as correct as the last
 * person who remembered — and forgetting is silent. Deriving the entire
 * snapshot from the collections instead makes the correctness condition
 * "something changed", which the live queries below observe for free. It is
 * also what makes the mirror SELF-HEALING: a failed sync, a host-service
 * restart, or a renderer reload all repair themselves on the next push.
 *
 * THE DEBOUNCE IS NOT AN OPTIMISATION. Dragging a thread emits a tabOrder write
 * per frame; a bulk bin emits one per selected row. Coalescing to a single
 * trailing push per quiet period keeps a drag from turning into a hundred
 * full-table replaces, and because each push is a complete snapshot, the
 * coalesced result is identical to the last one that would have been sent.
 *
 * ABSENCE IS SAFE; STALENESS IS NOT. Consumers are required to treat a MISSING
 * row as "no opinion recorded" and SHOW the row (see `db/schema.ts`), so an
 * unfilled mirror can only ever be too noisy. A STALE row is a different animal
 * and the two must not be conflated: a row still carrying `deletedAt` /
 * `archivedAt` / `isHidden` / `snoozeUntil` from before the user restored the
 * thread HIDES something that is no longer hidden — precisely the forbidden
 * direction. Nothing about a full-snapshot replace makes that self-correcting on
 * its own, so the two mechanisms below are load-bearing, not defensive polish:
 *
 *  - ONE PUSH IN FLIGHT AT A TIME. Two snapshots on separate loopback
 *    connections have no ordering guarantee. If the older one is served last,
 *    `host.db` keeps the older snapshot while `lastSyncedSignatureRef` believes
 *    the newer one landed, and every future push is suppressed until the next
 *    curation change. Serializing removes the reorder, not just its likelihood.
 *  - THE RETRY NEVER GIVES UP while the app runs (`RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS`). A
 *    bounded retry has a terminal state — attempts exhausted, no signature
 *    change coming, a host-service that restarted on the same port so
 *    `activeHostUrl` never changes either — and that terminal state is a mirror
 *    frozen with stale HIDING fields forever.
 *

 * mirror holds the user's LAST RECORDED curation. It is never an invented
 * opinion, and while the renderer runs it lags by at most the debounce plus one
 * retry backoff.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * (MIRROR-HEARTBEAT) THE UNCHANGED SNAPSHOT IS ALSO WORTH PUSHING

 * re-sent, and taken alone it makes `sidebar_mirror_meta.last_full_sync_at_ms`
 * measure the last CURATION CHANGE rather than renderer liveness. That is not a
 * documentation footnote, it is a correctness hole in the consumer: the mirror's
 * only permitted failure direction is "too noisy", and the only way a consumer
 * can fail toward SHOWING when the desktop is gone is to age the mirror out
 * against a timestamp that means "a renderer was alive at this moment". A
 * timestamp that only moves when somebody drags a thread cannot carry that
 * meaning — an untouched sidebar is indistinguishable from a quit app.
 *

 *
 *  - THE LAUNCH ID. `APP_LAUNCH_ID` is a fresh uuid per renderer load and it is
 *    the ONLY thing that can evaluate an "until next launch" snooze
 *    (`snooze_launch_id === app_launch_id` on the read side). It is carried in
 *    the meta row, NOT in the snapshot, so it is invisible to the signature: a
 *    launch whose curation happens to serialize identically to the previous
 *    one's would leave the mirror claiming the OLD launch, and every thread
 *    snoozed-until-next-launch during that old launch stays hidden on the phone
 *    even though the desktop already un-snoozed it. Pushing whenever the last
 *    PUSHED launch differs from the current one removes that dependence on the
 *    snapshot happening to change.
 *  - THE HEARTBEAT. Every `MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS` the same snapshot is re-sent, so
 *    the meta timestamp advances while a renderer is alive whether or not the
 *    user touched anything. The push is a full idempotent replace, so a repeat
 *    is free of consequence beyond one loopback request per five minutes — and
 *    it is what lets the consumer treat an OLD `last_full_sync_at_ms` as "no
 *    renderer is running, stop trusting this curation" instead of "nobody has
 *    reordered their sidebar today". It also bounds an otherwise unbounded case
 *    the signature gate has: a host-service that restarts against a DIFFERENT
 *    `host.db` while the renderer keeps running is reachable only by a push the
 *    signature gate suppresses, and the heartbeat caps that at one interval.
 */

/** Trailing debounce. Long enough to swallow a drag, short enough to feel live. */
const SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1_000;

/**
 * Retry schedule after a failed push. Unlike the first cut of this hook, it does
 * NOT stop: every attempt past the schedule waits `RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS`, forever.
 * Stopping looked cheap while "stale is safe" was believed, but a mirror holding

const RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS = 300_000;

/**

 *

 * trusted in minutes rather than hours. One idempotent full replace over
 * loopback every five minutes is not a load worth trading that for.
 */
const MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS = 300_000;

interface MirrorWorkspaceRow {
	workspaceId: string;
	projectId: string;
	sectionId: string | null;
	tabOrder: number;
	isHidden: boolean;
	archivedAt: number | null;
	snoozeUntil: number | null;
	snoozeLaunchId: string | null;
	completedAt: number | null;
	deletedAt: number | null;
	pinnedAt: number | null;
}

interface MirrorProjectRow {
	projectId: string;
	tabOrder: number;
	isPinned: boolean;
	isCollapsed: boolean;
}

export interface MirrorSnapshot {
	workspaces: MirrorWorkspaceRow[];
	projects: MirrorProjectRow[];
	/** Values the normalizers refused. Reported once per snapshot, never hidden. */
	rejectedFields: number;
	/** Rows with no usable identity/placement. Dropped, and never silently. */
	droppedRows: number;
}

/**
 * A curation timestamp, or null. Anything that is not a finite non-negative
 * number is not a timestamp a human action produced — it is a corrupt persisted
 * row — and it is mapped to "absent" rather than sent on. Sending it would fail
 * the bridge's boundary validation and reject the WHOLE snapshot, freezing the
 * mirror on one bad row; absent is the fail-toward-showing direction. The count
 * is surfaced by the caller so this stays visible rather than silent.
 */
function toEpochMs(value: unknown, reject: () => void): number | null {
	if (value == null) return null;
	if (typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
		reject();
		return null;
	}
	return Math.trunc(value);
}

/** Manual drag order. Negative is legitimate (prepend); non-finite is not. */
function toTabOrder(value: unknown, reject: () => void): number {
	if (typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
		reject();
		return 0;
	}
	return Math.trunc(value);
}

/**
 * A non-empty id, or null. These fields are typed `string`, but they are NOT
 * guaranteed to be one at runtime: localStorage collections do not run the zod
 * schema on READS (see `CollectionsProvider/withReadHeal.ts`), and the heal
 * deliberately refuses to synthesize identity fields — `workspaceId` and
 * `sidebarState.projectId` "must come from the stored row" or not at all. A
 * legacy or corrupt row therefore hands back `undefined` behind a `string`
 * type, and every existing reader of `sidebarState.projectId` compares it with
 * `===` and degrades to "row not shown". Touching `.length` on it instead
 * throws inside the `useMemo` below — and because `AgentHooks` is mounted
 * unconditionally with no boundary nearer than the ROOT route, that one row
 * would replace the entire app with the error page and take the command
 * watcher, device presence and worktree placer down with it.
 */
function toNullableId(value: unknown): string | null {
	return typeof value === "string" && value.length > 0 ? value : null;
}

/**
 * The live-query rows AS THEY ACTUALLY ARRIVE. Every field is `unknown` on
 * purpose. The collections declare them `string`/`number`, but a localStorage
 * collection validates on WRITE only, so the declared type is a claim about
 * what was once written and not about what comes back. Typing them honestly
 * here is what forces every field through a normalizer instead of being
 * trusted, and it is what makes the crash below impossible to reintroduce.
 */
interface LocalStateRowLike {
	workspaceId: unknown;
	projectId: unknown;
	sectionId: unknown;
	tabOrder: unknown;
	isHidden: unknown;
	archivedAt: unknown;
	snoozeUntil: unknown;
	snoozeLaunchId: unknown;
	completedAt: unknown;
	deletedAt: unknown;
	pinnedAt: unknown;
}

interface SidebarProjectRowLike {
	projectId: unknown;
	tabOrder: unknown;
	isPinned: unknown;
	isCollapsed: unknown;
}

/**
 * Derive the snapshot the mirror publishes from the two collections.
 *
 * Sorted by key, so the signature the hook derives from it is a function of
 * CONTENT only — without that, every live-query emission would produce a new
 * signature and re-push an identical snapshot.
 *
 * Exported, and free of React, so the normalization can be exercised directly;
 * `useSidebarMirrorSync` is the only production caller.
 */
export function buildMirrorSnapshot(
	localStateRows: readonly LocalStateRowLike[],
	sidebarProjectRows: readonly SidebarProjectRowLike[],
): MirrorSnapshot {
	let rejectedFields = 0;
	let droppedRows = 0;
	const reject = (): void => {
		rejectedFields += 1;
	};
	const workspaces = localStateRows
		.map((row): MirrorWorkspaceRow | null => {
			// Identity and placement go through `toNullableId` for the reason
			// documented on it: both are `string` by declared type and can be
			// `undefined` at runtime, so this must be a null check and never a
			// `.length` one.
			const workspaceId = toNullableId(row.workspaceId);
			const projectId = toNullableId(row.projectId);
			// A row with no identity, or whose placement project is missing, cannot
			// be mirrored: the column is NOT NULL on the far side, and a placement
			// of "nowhere" is not a statement the mirror can make. Dropping it means
			// the consumer sees no opinion and shows the thread — the safe direction.
			if (workspaceId === null || projectId === null) {
				droppedRows += 1;
				return null;
			}
			return {
				workspaceId,
				projectId,
				sectionId: toNullableId(row.sectionId),
				tabOrder: toTabOrder(row.tabOrder, reject),
				isHidden: row.isHidden === true,
				archivedAt: toEpochMs(row.archivedAt, reject),
				snoozeUntil: toEpochMs(row.snoozeUntil, reject),
				snoozeLaunchId: toNullableId(row.snoozeLaunchId),
				completedAt: toEpochMs(row.completedAt, reject),
				deletedAt: toEpochMs(row.deletedAt, reject),
				pinnedAt: toEpochMs(row.pinnedAt, reject),
			};
		})
		.filter((row): row is MirrorWorkspaceRow => row !== null)
		.sort((left, right) => left.workspaceId.localeCompare(right.workspaceId));

	const projects = sidebarProjectRows
		.map((row): MirrorProjectRow | null => {
			const projectId = toNullableId(row.projectId);
			if (projectId === null) {
				droppedRows += 1;
				return null;
			}
			return {
				projectId,
				tabOrder: toTabOrder(row.tabOrder, reject),
				isPinned: row.isPinned === true,
				isCollapsed: row.isCollapsed === true,
			};
		})
		.filter((row): row is MirrorProjectRow => row !== null)
		.sort((left, right) => left.projectId.localeCompare(right.projectId));

	return { workspaces, projects, rejectedFields, droppedRows };
}

/**
 * The content identity of a snapshot: what changed, ignoring how the rows were
 * ordered on the way in (`buildMirrorSnapshot` has already key-sorted both

 * than the curation.
 *
 * Exported so a test can name the same identity the hook compares on.
 */
export function signatureOf(snapshot: MirrorSnapshot): string {
	return JSON.stringify([snapshot.workspaces, snapshot.projects]);
}

export interface MirrorPushLoopDeps {
	/**

	getSnapshot: () => MirrorSnapshot;

export interface MirrorPushLoop {
	start: () => void;
	cancel: () => void;
}

/**

export function createMirrorPushLoop(deps: MirrorPushLoopDeps): MirrorPushLoop {

	const retryDelaysMs = deps.retryDelaysMs ?? RETRY_DELAYS_MS;
	const retryCapMs = deps.retryCapMs ?? RETRY_DELAY_CAP_MS;

		const inFlight = deps.inFlight.current;

	);

		useLiveQuery(
			(query) =>

					.from({ sidebarProject: collections.v2SidebarProjects })
					.select(({ sidebarProject }) => ({
						projectId: sidebarProject.projectId,
						tabOrder: sidebarProject.tabOrder,

	 * Without that, every live-query emission would produce a new signature and
	 * re-push an identical snapshot.

		[localStateRows, sidebarProjectRows],
	);

	// content must not re-run it just because the live query handed back new
	// array identities.
	const snapshotRef = useRef(snapshot);
	snapshotRef.current = snapshot;

	const lastSyncedSignatureRef = useRef<string | null>(null);

	 * heartbeat beat that was last pushed. Both are things the signature CANNOT

	 * payload at all — so each needs its own record of what actually landed. Refs

	 * only thing it has to be is DIFFERENT from the last beat that was pushed —
	 * which is also why the interval can run unconditionally: a tick while the
	 * collections are still hydrating, or with no host-service yet, is absorbed by
	 * the same guards every other push goes through.

		const timer = setInterval(() => {
			setHeartbeat((beat) => beat + 1);
		}, MIRROR_HEARTBEAT_MS);

			clearInterval(timer);

	 * effect runs. Serializing pushes is a correctness requirement, not a load

		// launch-id force is carried by the `launchStale` comparison above, which
		// re-evaluates on every run of this effect; there is nothing for a
		// dependency to trigger.
	}, [ready, activeHostUrl, signature, heartbeat]);

	ctx: SealedRequestContext,
	request: TreeRequest,
): Promise<TreeResponse> {
	const includeIdle = requireBooleanField(request.includeIdle, "includeIdle");
	if (
		request.since !== undefined &&
		request.since !== null &&
		!Number.isInteger(request.since)
	) {
		throw badRequest("since must be an integer epoch-ms or null");
	}

	// Protocol 0 / no `tree.read`: baseline fields only (§6.1, §7.2). The
	// non-baseline fields are still present because the shape is fixed, but they
	// carry the enum's designated `unknown` / `null` members rather than data
	// the client has not been granted.
	const full = ctx.granted.includes("tree.read");

	// (BRIDGE-LIVENESS) Refresh before reading, because this is one of the two
	// handlers that can afford a daemon round trip. Never throws — a failure
	// degrades to "no evidence", which shows everything.
	await deps.liveness.refresh();

	const nowMs = Date.now();
	const answerability: AnswerabilityContext = { granted: ctx.granted };
	const curation = createSidebarCuration(
		deps.db.readSidebarMirror(),
		nowMs,
		deps.organizationId,
	);
	const projects = deps.db.listProjects();
	const allWorkspaces = deps.db.listWorkspaces();
	const visible = visibleWorkspaces(allWorkspaces, curation);
	const terminals = listLiveTerminals(deps.db, deps.liveness);
	const bindings = new Map(
		deps.db.listBindings().map((b) => [b.terminalId, b]),
	);

	const counts: StatusCounts = { needsInput: 0, working: 0, idle: 0 };
	const terminalsByWorkspace = new Map<string, Terminal[]>();

	for (const row of terminals) {
		if (row.originWorkspaceId === null) continue;
		const pending = deps.questions.byHostTerminal(row.id);
		if (!terminalPiercesCuration(visible, row.originWorkspaceId, pending))
			continue;
		const binding = bindings.get(row.id);

		const status = deriveSessionStatus(pending, binding);
		tallyStatus(counts, status);

		let pendingRef: PendingQuestionRef | null = null;
		if (pending !== null) {
			pendingRef = {
				questionId: pending.questionId,
				askedAtMs: pending.askedAtMs,
				answerable:
					deps.questions.unanswerableReason(pending, answerability) === null,
				headline: deps.questions.headline(pending),
				// (EMIT-OPTIONAL-FIELDS) The headline is the FIRST question's header
				// only; without the count a 3-question capture renders exactly like a
				// 1-question one, and `multiSelect` changes what answering even means.
				// Pending-question identity is baseline data: a paired device must be able
				// to discover the question even before capability negotiation.
				questionCount: pending.questions.length,
				multiSelect: pending.questions.some((item) => item.multiSelect),
			};
		}

		const terminal: Terminal = {
			terminalId: deriveHandle("terminal", row.id) as unknown as TerminalId,
			title: terminalTitle(binding),
			status,
			agent: full
				? {
						kind:
							binding === undefined ? "none" : agentKindFromId(binding.agentId),
						bound: binding !== undefined,
						subagent:
							pending !== null && pending.agentType !== null
								? { agentType: pending.agentType }
								: null,
					}
				: { kind: "unknown", bound: false, subagent: null },
			pendingQuestion: pendingRef,
			lastActivityMs: full
				? (binding?.lastEventAt ?? row.lastAttachedAt ?? row.createdAt)
				: null,
		};

		const list = terminalsByWorkspace.get(row.originWorkspaceId);
		if (list === undefined) {
			terminalsByWorkspace.set(row.originWorkspaceId, [terminal]);
		} else {
			list.push(terminal);
		}
	}

	// (BRIDGE-SIDEBAR-FILTER) Grouped by the SIDEBAR's placement, not by
	// `workspaces.project_id`: moving a thread under another repo is a curation
	// act, and the phone mirrors where the user put it.
	const workspacesByProject = new Map<string, Workspace[]>();
	// Keyed on `workspaces.project_id` — the OWNING project — and deliberately
	// NOT on the placement above. Kind is a fact about a repository (is its
	// `repo_path` the multi-repo anchor, do its workspaces carry the non-git
	// branch sentinel), and curation cannot change a repository. Feeding the
	// placement map to `deriveProjectKind` made dragging one git branch under a
	// non-git project flip that project from `plain` to `git` on the phone, and
	// dragging the last workspace out of a project made it `unknown` — a display
	// kind that changed because of where the user dropped a thread.
	const workspaceRowsByOwningProject = new Map<string, HostWorkspaceRow[]>();
	for (const row of allWorkspaces) {
		const placement = curation.effectiveProjectId(row);
		const kindRows = workspaceRowsByOwningProject.get(row.projectId);
		if (kindRows === undefined)
			workspaceRowsByOwningProject.set(row.projectId, [row]);
		else kindRows.push(row);

		const all = terminalsByWorkspace.get(row.id) ?? [];
		const status = rollup(all.map((t) => t.status));
		const shown = includeIdle ? all : all.filter((t) => t.status !== "idle");
		// A workspace with nothing to show is dropped UNCONDITIONALLY. Emptiness
		// is not an idle question: 63 workspaces on this machine have zero live
		// terminals, and each one rendered an inert header row the user cannot
		// even tap (only terminal rows are answerable). The skip used to sit
		// behind `!includeIdle`, which every automatic client path sets to true —
		// so it never once fired.
		if (shown.length === 0) continue;

		sortTerminals(shown);

		const workspacePinned = curation.workspacePinned(row.id);
		const workspace: Workspace = {
			workspaceId: deriveHandle("workspace", row.id) as unknown as WorkspaceId,
			name: row.name.length > 0 ? row.name : row.branch,
			branch: full ? (row.branch.length > 0 ? row.branch : null) : null,
			status,
			terminals: shown,
			lastActivityMs: full
				? shown.reduce<number | null>(
						(acc, t) =>
							t.lastActivityMs === null
								? acc
								: acc === null
									? t.lastActivityMs
									: Math.max(acc, t.lastActivityMs),
						null,
					)
				: null,
			// (EMIT-OPTIONAL-FIELDS) Pinning is the one act of curation that changes
			// ORDER rather than membership, so a filter that only decides what to
			// hide could never carry it. Not gated on `full`: it says nothing about
			// content that the row's own name and status do not already say.
			//
			// OMITTED, not `false`, when curation has no opinion (never mirrored,
			// aged out, another org). §7.2 distinguishes a field the bridge does not
			// report from one it reports as false, and emitting `false` there told
			// the phone "this row is not pinned" on the strength of a mirror that was
			// never written.
			...(workspacePinned === null ? {} : { pinned: workspacePinned }),
		};

		const list = workspacesByProject.get(placement);
		if (list === undefined) {
			workspacesByProject.set(placement, [workspace]);
		} else {
			list.push(workspace);
		}
	}

	const outProjects: Project[] = [];
	for (const row of projects) {
		const ws = workspacesByProject.get(row.id) ?? [];
		// A project omitted from the sidebar still carries a pending-question
		// workspace admitted above. The workspace list is the final visibility fact.
		// Same unconditional skip, for the same reason: a project whose every
		// workspace was dropped is a header with nothing under it.
		if (ws.length === 0) continue;
		ws.sort(
			(a, b) =>
				STATUS_RANK[a.status] - STATUS_RANK[b.status] ||
				(b.lastActivityMs ?? 0) - (a.lastActivityMs ?? 0),
		);
		const projectPinned = curation.projectPinned(row.id);
		outProjects.push({
			projectId: deriveHandle("project", row.id) as unknown as ProjectId,
			name:
				row.name.length > 0 ? row.name : path.basename(row.repoPath || row.id),
			kind: full
				? deriveProjectKind(row, workspaceRowsByOwningProject.get(row.id) ?? [])
				: PROJECT_KIND_UNKNOWN,
			workspaces: ws,
			// (EMIT-OPTIONAL-FIELDS) `sidebar_project_state.is_pinned`, omitted on
			// the same terms as a workspace's.
			...(projectPinned === null ? {} : { pinned: projectPinned }),
		});
	}
	outProjects.sort((a, b) => {
		const aStatus = rollup(a.workspaces.map((w) => w.status));
		const bStatus = rollup(b.workspaces.map((w) => w.status));
		return STATUS_RANK[aStatus] - STATUS_RANK[bStatus];
	});

	return {
		generatedAtMs: Date.now(),
		// Always a full tree. §7.2 says the bridge MAY answer `since` with a
		// delta; it does not, because a delta the client mis-applies is a silently
		// wrong tree, and the whole payload is small.
		complete: true,
		gseq: full ? deps.currentGseq() : 0,
		projects: outProjects,
		counts,
		// (CURATION-PROVENANCE) Emitted on every tree, not only empty ones: the
		// question "is this tree short because nothing is running, or because the
		// mirror hid it?" is asked of a tree that is merely SMALLER than expected
		// at least as often as of one that is empty.
		curation: {
			enabled: curation.enabled,
			lastSyncAgeMs: curation.lastSyncAgeMs,
			hiddenWorkspaces: allWorkspaces.length - visible.size,
		},
	};
}

/**
 * Reference order (§7.2): `needs_input` first, oldest `askedAtMs` first, then
 * `working`, then `idle`, ties broken by `lastActivityMs` descending.
 */
function sortTerminals(terminals: Terminal[]): void {
	terminals.sort((a, b) => {
		const rank = STATUS_RANK[a.status] - STATUS_RANK[b.status];
		if (rank !== 0) return rank;
		if (a.status === "needs_input") {
			const aAsked = a.pendingQuestion?.askedAtMs ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
			const bAsked = b.pendingQuestion?.askedAtMs ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
			if (aAsked !== bAsked) return aAsked - bAsked;
		}
		return (b.lastActivityMs ?? 0) - (a.lastActivityMs ?? 0);
	});
}

			workspaceId: deriveHandle(

			) as WorkspaceId,
			questionCount: question.questions.length,
			expiresAtMs: question.askedAtMs + PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS,

/**
 * Counts are over TERMINALS — the leaf where a status is an observed fact — and
 * over exactly the terminals `/v1/tree` would render: live (`(BRIDGE-LIVENESS)`)
 * and inside a curated workspace (`(BRIDGE-SIDEBAR-FILTER)`). Before both
 * filters this returned `{needsInput: 8, working: 3, idle: 297}` on a machine
 * whose eight "blocked" agents had last spoken 18-23 days earlier.
 */
function countStatuses(deps: ReadDeps, nowMs: EpochMs): StatusCounts {
	const counts: StatusCounts = { needsInput: 0, working: 0, idle: 0 };
	const curation = createSidebarCuration(
		deps.db.readSidebarMirror(),
		nowMs,
		deps.organizationId,
	);
	const visible = visibleWorkspaces(deps.db.listWorkspaces(), curation);
	const bindings = new Map(
		deps.db.listBindings().map((b) => [b.terminalId, b]),
	);
	for (const row of listLiveTerminals(deps.db, deps.liveness)) {
		if (row.originWorkspaceId === null) continue;
		const pending = deps.questions.byHostTerminal(row.id);
		if (!terminalPiercesCuration(visible, row.originWorkspaceId, pending))
			continue;
		tallyStatus(counts, deriveSessionStatus(pending, bindings.get(row.id)));
	}
	return counts;
}

interface TreeFixture {
	projects: HostProjectRow[];
	workspaces: HostWorkspaceRow[];
	terminals: HostTerminalRow[];
	bindings: HostBindingRow[];
	mirror: SidebarMirrorSnapshot;
	pendingByHostTerminal?: Record<string, PendingQuestion>;
}

function treeDeps(fixture: TreeFixture): ReadDeps {
	const db: HostDbReader = {
		listProjects: () => fixture.projects,
		listWorkspaces: () => fixture.workspaces,
		listActiveTerminals: () => fixture.terminals,
		listBindings: () => fixture.bindings,
		findWorkspace: (id) => fixture.workspaces.find((w) => w.id === id) ?? null,
		findBinding: (id) =>
			fixture.bindings.find((b) => b.terminalId === id) ?? null,
		findTerminal: (id) => fixture.terminals.find((t) => t.id === id) ?? null,
		readSidebarMirror: () => fixture.mirror,
		resolveTerminal: () => null,
		resolveActiveTerminal: () => null,
		resolveTranscriptPath: () => null,
		resolveTerminalActivityMs: () => NOW,
		close: () => {},
	};
	const pending = fixture.pendingByHostTerminal ?? {};
	return {
		db,
		log: () => {},
		questions: {
			byHostTerminal: (hostTerminalId: string) =>
				pending[hostTerminalId] ?? null,
			unanswerableReason: () => null,
			headline: (question: PendingQuestion) =>
				question.questions[0]?.header ?? "",
			reconcile: async () => [],
			oldestPendingAgeMs: () => null,
		} as unknown as ReadDeps["questions"],
		liveness: {
			refresh: async () => {},
			isLive: () => true,
			isProvablyGone: () => false,
			describe: () => ({
				hasSnapshot: true,
				aliveCount: fixture.terminals.length,
				takenAtMs: NOW,
			}),
		},
		organizationId: ORG,
		versions: { appVersion: "0", hostServiceVersion: "0", forkTag: "0" },
		bridgeStartedMs: NOW,
		ledger: { currentEpoch: () => "epoch" } as unknown as ReadDeps["ledger"],
		currentGseq: () => 7,
		onQuestionsSettled: () => {},
	};
}

function terminal(
	id: string,
	originWorkspaceId: string,
	overrides: Partial<HostTerminalRow> = {},
): HostTerminalRow {
	return {
		id,
		originWorkspaceId,
		status: "active",
		createdAt: NOW - 100_000,
		lastAttachedAt: NOW - 1_000,
		endedAt: null,
		...overrides,
	};
}

function workspaceRow(
	id: string,
	projectId: string,
	overrides: Partial<HostWorkspaceRow> = {},
): HostWorkspaceRow {
	return {
		id,
		projectId,
		name: id,
		branch: id,
		worktreePath: `C:/wt/${id}`,
		type: "worktree",
		createdAt: NOW - 200_000,
		...overrides,
	};
}

const FULL_CTX = {
	granted: ["tree.read"],
	device: { revokedAtMs: null, writesDisabledAtMs: null },
} as unknown as SealedRequestContext;

const BASELINE_CTX = {
	granted: [],
	device: { revokedAtMs: null, writesDisabledAtMs: null },
} as unknown as SealedRequestContext;

async function tree(
	fixture: TreeFixture,
	ctx: SealedRequestContext = FULL_CTX,
): Promise<TreeResponse> {
	return handleTree(treeDeps(fixture), ctx, { includeIdle: true });
}

describe("(BRIDGE-SIDEBAR-FILTER) handleTree over a curated fixture", () => {
	const baseProjects: HostProjectRow[] = [
		{ id: "p-git", name: "repo", repoPath: "C:/repo", worktreeBaseDir: null },
	];

	it("drops a binned thread and reports it in the curation provenance", async () => {
		const response = await tree({
			projects: baseProjects,
			workspaces: [
				workspaceRow("w-live", "p-git"),
				workspaceRow("w-binned", "p-git"),
			],
			terminals: [
				terminal("t-live", "w-live"),
				terminal("t-binned", "w-binned"),
			],
			bindings: [],
			mirror: snapshot(
				[
					mirrorWorkspace("w-live", { projectId: "p-git" }),
					mirrorWorkspace("w-binned", {
						projectId: "p-git",
						deletedAt: NOW - 10,
					}),
				],
				[mirrorProject("p-git")],
			),
		});
		const workspaceIds = response.projects
			.flatMap((p) => p.workspaces)
			.map((w) => w.name);
		expect(workspaceIds).toEqual(["w-live"]);
		expect(response.counts.idle).toBe(1);
		expect(response.curation?.enabled).toBe(true);
		expect(response.curation?.hiddenWorkspaces).toBe(1);
		// A real age, measured against the real clock the handler reads. The upper
		// bound is the window that actually means something — a mirror still in
		// force — and NOT a round 60s: `NOW` is captured when this module loads, so
		// a 60s bound was really an assertion about how long the whole suite takes
		// to reach this line, and it started failing when the file grew.
		expect(response.curation?.lastSyncAgeMs).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1_000);
		expect(response.curation?.lastSyncAgeMs).toBeLessThan(MIRROR_MAX_AGE_MS);
	});

	it("offers a pending question even when curation hides its workspace and no tree capability was negotiated", async () => {
		const pending = pendingQuestionFixture({ hostTerminalId: "t-binned" });
		const response = await tree(
			{
				projects: baseProjects,
				workspaces: [workspaceRow("w-binned", "p-git")],
				terminals: [terminal("t-binned", "w-binned")],
				bindings: [],
				mirror: snapshot(
					[
						mirrorWorkspace("w-binned", {
							projectId: "p-git",
							deletedAt: NOW - 10,
						}),
					],
					[],
				),
				pendingByHostTerminal: { "t-binned": pending },
			},
			BASELINE_CTX,
		);

		const workspace = response.projects[0]?.workspaces[0];
		expect(workspace?.name).toBe("w-binned");
		expect(workspace?.terminals[0]?.pendingQuestion).toMatchObject({
			questionId: pending.questionId,
			answerable: true,
		});
		expect(response.curation?.hiddenWorkspaces).toBe(1);
		expect(response.counts.needsInput).toBe(1);
	});

	it("an EMPTY tree is now distinguishable from an over-filtered one", async () => {
		const overFiltered = await tree({
			projects: baseProjects,
			workspaces: [workspaceRow("w-1", "p-git")],
			terminals: [terminal("t-1", "w-1")],
			bindings: [],
			mirror: snapshot(
				[mirrorWorkspace("w-1", { projectId: "p-git", deletedAt: NOW - 10 })],
				[mirrorProject("p-git")],
			),
		});
		expect(overFiltered.projects).toEqual([]);
		expect(overFiltered.curation?.hiddenWorkspaces).toBe(1);

		const genuinelyEmpty = await tree({
			projects: baseProjects,
			workspaces: [],
			terminals: [],
			bindings: [],
			mirror: snapshot([], [mirrorProject("p-git")]),
		});
		expect(genuinelyEmpty.projects).toEqual([]);
		expect(genuinelyEmpty.curation?.hiddenWorkspaces).toBe(0);
	});

export const SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID = "superset:sessions";

export const SESSIONS_PROJECT_NAME = "Sessions";

/** Namespace for the synthetic workspace id minted per session. */
export const SESSION_WORKSPACE_ID_PREFIX = "superset:session:";

/**

 * mirrored under and the id its tree handle is derived from.

 * Throws on an empty id rather than minting a bare prefix: an id that maps
 * every session to the same key would curate all of them together, and that is
 * a caller bug worth failing loudly on.

export function sessionWorkspaceId(sessionId: string): string {
	if (sessionId.length === 0) {

		);
	}

export function sessionIdFromWorkspaceId(workspaceId: string): string | null {
	if (!workspaceId.startsWith(SESSION_WORKSPACE_ID_PREFIX)) return null;
	const sessionId = workspaceId.slice(SESSION_WORKSPACE_ID_PREFIX.length);
	return sessionId.length > 0 ? sessionId : null;
}

export function isSessionsProjectId(projectId: string): boolean {
	return projectId === SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID;
}

export function isSessionWorkspaceId(workspaceId: string): boolean {
	return sessionIdFromWorkspaceId(workspaceId) !== null;
}

 * session, which the two joined statements above cannot express.
 *
 * Both of them inner-join `workspaces`, so a session with
 * `origin_workspace_id IS NULL` resolves to nothing — and a `null` source is a
 * REFUSAL upstream: `capture` declines the question ("names no active terminal
 * joined to a workspace in host.db") and `/v1/question` 500s on the record. The
 * effect was that an agent blocked in a session was invisible to the phone even
 * though the hook delivered its question intact.
 *
 * The synthesis is narrow on purpose. It fires ONLY when host.db has the row
 * and the row's workspace is NULL. A terminal that names a workspace which is
 * missing from `workspaces` still resolves to `null`, because that is a broken
 * reference and not a session — inventing a placement for it would file a real
 * thread under Sessions and lose it.
 */
function sessionTerminalSource(
	db: Pick<HostDbReader, "findTerminal" | "findBinding">,
	hostTerminalId: string,
	requireActive: boolean,
): TerminalSource | null {
	const row = db.findTerminal(hostTerminalId);
	if (row === null || row.originWorkspaceId !== null) return null;
	// (CAPTURE-BOUNDED) The same session predicate the active statement carries,
	// applied to the same columns — one source of truth for "still running".
	if (requireActive && (row.status !== "active" || row.endedAt !== null)) {
		return null;
	}
	return {
		hostProjectId: SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID,
		hostWorkspaceId: sessionWorkspaceId(row.id),
		agentId: db.findBinding(row.id)?.agentId ?? null,
	};
}

function memoryLedger(): AttemptLedger {
	const records = new Map<string, LedgerRecord>();
	return {
		currentEpoch: () => "epoch-guardless",
		claimForAnswer: (claim) => {
			const previous = records.get(claim.requestId);
			if (previous !== undefined) return { kind: "replay", record: previous };
			records.set(
				claim.requestId,
				ledgerRow({
					requestId: claim.requestId,
					status: "claimed",
					questionId: claim.questionId,
					deviceId: claim.deviceId,
					surface: claim.surface,
					leaseId: null,
					startedAtMs: claim.startedAtMs,
					createdAtMs: claim.startedAtMs,
					resolvedAtMs: null,
				}),
			);
			return { kind: "claimed", coverageEpoch: "epoch-guardless" };
		},
		beginWrite: (requestId, leaseId) => {
			const current = records.get(requestId);
			if (current?.status !== "claimed") throw new Error("missing claim");
			for (const record of records.values()) {
				if (
					record.requestId !== requestId &&
					record.questionId === current.questionId &&
					(record.status === "in_flight" ||
						record.status === "confirmed" ||
						record.status === "unconfirmed")
				) {
					return record;
				}
			}
			records.set(requestId, {
				...current,
				status: "in_flight",
				leaseId,
			});
			return null;
		},
		recordOutcome: (outcome) => {
			const current = records.get(outcome.requestId);
			if (current?.status !== "claimed" && current?.status !== "in_flight")
				return;
			records.set(outcome.requestId, {
				...current,
				...outcome,
				guardsPassed: [...outcome.guardsPassed],
			});
		},
		get: (requestId) => records.get(requestId) ?? null,
		resolveStatus: () => ({ kind: "unconfirmed", why: "unused in this test" }),
		rotateEpoch: () => "epoch-rotated",
	};
}

	terminalId: TerminalId,
): Promise<HostTerminalRef> {

## Correction that drove the rework

My first pass modelled a "session" as a terminal with `origin_workspace_id IS NULL`. That was wrong. Tracing `createAnswerDeps.resolveHostTerminal` → `getOrAdoptSession` → `createTerminalSessionInternal` showed why it mattered: adoption does `db.query.workspaces.findFirst({id: workspaceId})` and returns `"Workspace not found"` for anything it can't look up, and `writableSession` re-checks `session.workspaceId`. Any synthetic workspace id breaks writes.

`packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/workspace-creation/procedures/create-session.ts:141` settles it: a session is an **ordinary `workspaces` row** — real id, real worktree in `~/.superset/sessions`, `type: "session"` — with `projectId: null`. So adoption, locks and pty writes already work on sessions; the only broken axis is **grouping by project**, plus one crash on the answer path. Nothing is invented anywhere in the final patch: the real workspace id is passed through untouched, only the NULL *project* is mapped.

## Final patch

**New `packages/host-service/src/companion/session-project.ts`** (exported as `@superset/host-service/session-project`): `SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID = "superset:sessions"`, `SESSIONS_PROJECT_NAME = "Sessions"`, `placementProjectId(projectId)` — the single place the NULL is interpreted — and `isSessionsProjectId`.

**`sidebar-filter.ts`**: `WorkspaceCurationInput.projectId` is now `string | null` (matching the column). `placementOf` = mirrored placement → row's own project → Sessions; the pass-through curation normalises too, so a disabled mirror never answers NULL. `isInSidebar` exempts the synthetic project from the project-absence-means-hide rule (it can never have a `sidebar_project_state` row). Per-row curation is untouched, so a binned/snoozed/archived session still hides.

**`read-api.ts`**: `HostWorkspaceRow.projectId: string | null`; new exported `toTerminalSource()` wraps both source statements — **this is the remote-answer fix**: `resolveSource` mints `deriveHandle("project", hostProjectId)` for every `/v1/question` (the call the phone makes to open a question before answering), and a session's NULL project reached it. The workspace id is passed through verbatim. `handleTree` emits the synthetic project from the existing placement map (so a session dragged under a repo groups there instead), `kind: "unknown"`, no `pinned`; counts follow the same path.

**`useSidebarMirrorSync.ts`**: a local-state row with no placement is now mirrored under `SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID` instead of dropped, so the bridge has a real opinion about a curated session. Identity-less rows are still dropped and counted.

No schema change; `project_id` stays NULL and every existing join keeps its meaning.

## Tests

- `session-answer.test.ts` (new, 9 tests) — against a **real migrated host.db**: a session terminal resolves to `{hostProjectId: SESSIONS_PROJECT_ID, hostWorkspaceId: "w-session"}`; a closed session still resolves on the unrestricted resolver; a repo terminal keeps its real project id; an orphan (`origin_workspace_id IS NULL`) is still refused; a question captured on the session builds a §7.4 source and reports `answerable: true`. Then `handleAnswer` from **phone and watch** returns `confirmed`, and every write/prepare/repaint target is asserted to equal the session's real `(terminal, workspace)` pair. Guards intact: already-resolved and fingerprint-mismatch both reject with zero writes.
- `session-project.test.ts` (5) — placement mapping, membership exemption, binned/removed still hidden, drag-to-repo wins, pass-through normalisation.
- `session-tree.test.ts` (3) — session rendered under Sessions alongside a repo, binned session dropped, dragged session grouped under the repo.
- Regression runs: `bun test src/companion` **241 pass / 0 fail** (incl. `curation-gates`, `question-lifecycle`, `answer-guardless`); `sidebar-mirror` suite green; desktop AgentHooks **19 pass / 1 fail**.

content.text:
Review target: `Review and simplify the complete current production diff for desktop Sessions archive/snooze plus phone/watch companion session parity. Preserve behavior and tests.`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"

Aliases:

Use "entire checkpoint [command] --help" for more information about a command.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The user’s initial request was to extend Superset’s recently added project-less Sessions feature:

   - Sessions are useful for temporary, non-project work.
   - Sessions must support the existing Archive and Snooze behavior.
   - Sessions must never appear on the Kanban board.
   - Requirements had to be clarified through the AskUser tool.
   - All work should be delegated to Opus subagents where possible.
   - Production plans/code should be reviewed by Fable, Sol, and Opus agents.
   - Finished agents should be stopped to keep the status bar clean.

   User decisions collected through AskUser:

   - Session actions should match the existing project-thread context-menu UI.
   - Hidden sessions should appear in dedicated “Snoozed Sessions” and “Archived Sessions” subsections.
   - Snooze durations, next-launch behavior, expiry, sorting, restoration, and archive behavior should match existing thread behavior exactly.
   - Snoozing or archiving the currently open session must leave its content open.
   - Four booleans may be added to the existing device-local preferences schema to persist section visibility/collapse state.
   - Sessions removed from the sidebar should appear under Archived Sessions, matching non-main thread behavior.

   The user later expanded the scope:

   - Commit and push everything to `main`.
   - Build and download a new Windows ARM64 installer using the project’s normal established flow.
   - Investigate the custom phone and watch apps before asking further questions.
   - Make Sessions behave on phone and watch as Projects currently do.

   After exploration, “phone/watch parity” was implemented as:

   - Phone displays Sessions as a normal synthetic top-level Project named “Sessions”.
   - Phone can open session terminals/questions and submit answers.

- Present becomes away → release held alert

Unlike questions, ready/error alerts are point events and normally need no later retraction. They should have a bounded expiry to avoid delayed “ready” or “failed” alerts becoming misleading hours later.

**Validation points:** (1) tRPC zod at the unauthenticated localhost route — the same posture as `companionQuestion` (`companion-question-sink.ts:126-142`); (2) scheduler re-validates in-process, because a future non-tRPC producer bypasses the schema; (3) `assertPushDataSafe` throws before any byte leaves the process (`push.ts:311-373`) — a text leak is structurally impossible, not merely unlikely.

**Persistence:** `companion_lifecycle_cycle` row, written synchronously before any FCM await (same discipline as `evaluate`'s "accounting is SYNCHRONOUS end to end", `push.ts:1490-1497`). host.db `terminal_sessions` remains the source of truth for terminal→workspace.

## 4. Event identity, dedupe key, bounds, deletion

**Alert id (deterministic, restart-stable, 22-char base64url → satisfies both `PUSH_VALUE_PATTERN` and `Ids.requireOpaque16`):**

```
alertId = b64url(SHA-256("sc/v2 alertId" ‖ 0x00 ‖ kind ‖ 0x00 ‖ hostTerminalId ‖ 0x00 ‖ (agentSessionId ?? "") ‖ 0x00 ‖ String(cycleSeq))[0..16])
```

Same construction as `deriveHandle` / `mintQuestionId` (`packages\host-service\src\companion\question-store.ts:205-220`, `:1565-1578`). Derived, never minted-and-remembered → a restart recomputes the identical id, so the device's `collapse_key` dedupe holds across a bridge restart.

**Dedupe key (host):** the row `(hostTerminalId)` plus the per-axis state. One `sent` per `(hostTerminalId, cycleSeq, kind)`. A second `Stop` with no intervening `Start` finds `ready: 'sent'` → no-op. That is "never repeat while stable". A `Start` bumps `cycleSeq` → both axes re-arm. That is "re-arm on next cycle".

**Bounds:**
- One row per terminal — bounded by open terminals, not by traffic.
- Soft cap `LIFECYCLE_ROWS_MAX = 2_048`, oldest-`updatedAtMs` eviction, **logged loudly** (an evicted row is a lost dedupe → a possible duplicate buzz), mirroring `PUSH_MAX_SENT_RECORDS` (`push.ts:196-202, 1646-1655`).

**Deletion (stated, not implied):**
- `Detached` → immediate delete.
- Terminal not in `listActiveTerminals()` / `liveness.isProvablyGone` (corroborated, `liveness.ts:126`) → delete.
- `updatedAtMs` older than `LIFECYCLE_ROW_RETENTION_MS = 86_400_000` → pruned at `load()` and on the sweep.
- Held alert older than `ALERT_HOLD_CEILING_MS` (recommend 30 min for ready, 6 h for error, matching `PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS`) → dropped, logged. A "it finished" buzz hours late is noise.
- Malformed row → dropped individually + reported, never a whole-load failure (`push-fence.ts:14-18`).

---

## 5. Ordering / auto-resume semantics

- **Failure and ready are mutually exclusive per cycle.** A `Stop` carrying `agentTurnFailure` fires error and sets ready → `disarmed` for that cycle. Without this, Claude's failed turn buzzes "ready for review" (`pane-map-hook.ts:1885`).
- **Auto-resume's re-send produces a fresh `Start`** (`manager.ts` → host-send → terminal → `UserPromptSubmit` → `Start`), bumping `cycleSeq`. A still-**held** error alert for the previous cycle is cancelled (the condition is being handled). An already-**sent** one is not retracted — the wrist already buzzed and retraction here buys nothing.
- **Error episode dedupe:** consecutive failures with no intervening clean `Stop` fire **once**. The error axis re-arms only on a clean `Stop` or `Detached`. A 5-hour rate-limit that fails on 4 retries = 1 buzz.
- **Holds compose independently** (presence, curation, in-flight cycle) — each is a `continue` over the armed entry, never a combined verdict, exactly as `evaluate` does it (`push.ts:1517-1532`). Curation must be asked while still armed, or "not now" silently means "never".
- **No ordering guarantee between a question push and a lifecycle alert** — different `collapse_key`s, different chains. Acceptable: they describe different facts. Within one terminal, ready and error can never both be in flight.
- **Presence fail direction:** away/uncertain → fire (`presence.ts:110-112`). Curation fail direction → `false`/fire (`index.ts` curation gate docblock). Keep both; they are opposite on purpose.

---

2. `PushSender.sendAlert`. Verify: a test that a v2 frame reaches the fake device set and that a v1 question path is untouched.

8. Kotlin `Push.kt` v2 + `PushRouting.kt` + JVM tests. Verify: `./gradlew :core:test :app-phone:test`.
9. Phone notification/channels/watch relay; watch listener + `AlertNotifier`.
10. `FEATURES.md` row + markers.

**Tests to write**

---

## 7. Risks and edge cases

- **Highest:** a Claude failure looks like a clean `Stop` on the wire. If step 7 (hook field) regresses or the field is stripped by the retry fallback, every failed turn buzzes "ready". Mitigation: on the strip-retry path the hook logs `companion-rejected-dot-posted`; add an assertion test that the failure field is present for a StopFailure payload.
- **Schema/migration:** needs your permission; a migration that rebuilds tables runs with FKs off and is FK-checked after (`packages\host-service\src\db\db.ts:47-70`). A new standalone table is low risk there.
- **Old phone installs** log an alert as "malformed or notification-bearing payload" via `recordPushRefused` (`CompanionMessagingService.kt:68-76`). Harmless, but it pollutes push diagnostics until the phone updates. Optional fix in the same PR: distinguish "unknown version" from "malformed".
- **Phone foreground sweep** deletes any `ID_QUESTION`-id notification not in `stillPending` (`CompanionNotifications.kt:188-198`). Reusing that id for alerts = silently vanishing alerts. Hard requirement: separate id.
- **Storm:** N terminals finishing while away = N buzzes at once. Nothing in the design coalesces. If that proves annoying, the fix is a per-sweep send cap with deferral — I did **not** design it in, because inventing a coalescing rule you did not ask for would change the "once per cycle" contract.
- **Concurrency:** the scheduler is synchronous through the fence write before any `await`, matching `evaluate`. A slow FCM send cannot let the next sweep re-collect the same cycle.
- **Clock steps:** every age comparison must clamp at 0 and treat a future stamp as a miss — the `(CLOCK-STEP-FAILS-OPEN)` rule in `index.ts`'s curation cache exists because that exact bug latched a hold.
- **Terminal id reuse:** a recycled `terminalId` with a different `agentSessionId` must reset the row rather than inherit `cycleSeq`. Store `agentSessionId`; a mismatch = new cycle, row reset.
- **Backward compat:** an older desktop build posts no `agentTurnFailure` → every Stop reads clean → failures silently become "ready". Version-gate or accept; I recommend accepting (both ship together in this fork) but logging when a Claude terminal has never sent the field.
- **Nightly merge:** the additive hook field and the sink extension sit in fork-owned files (`companion-question-sink.ts` exists precisely for this, `:118-124`); the one-line change inside upstream-owned `notifications.ts` is the merge-risk surface. Keep it to one call.
- **FEATURES gate:** a new fork feature without a `FEATURES.md` marker is invisible to `scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` and can be silently deleted by a merge.

## 1. Recommended approach

Additive, content-free FCM v2 lifecycle alerts, driven by a host-side per-terminal work-cycle state machine fed from the existing hook seam. Fork logic stays in fork-only files (merge-safety idiom of `companion-question-sink.ts:118-124`).

**Core mechanism**
- Python notify hook gains one additive payload field `companionLifecycle: "turn-failed" | "session-end"` — NOT a changed eventType.
- Router forwards every mapped lifecycle event + marker to a new module-level lifecycle sink (parallel to `setCompanionQuestionSink`).
- Bridge runs per-terminal cycle machine: `Start/SubagentActive/PermissionRequest` → arm; `Stop` clean+armed → ready alert once; `turn-failed` → error alert once; `BackgroundRunning` → hold armed; `session-end`/`Detached` → silent disarm. Durable fence row per terminal = dedupe.
- New FCM v2 data payload (`v:"2"`, `k:"g"|"e"`), same closed key shape `{v,k,i,w,n,x}`, opaque ids only. Phone posts fixed local text on two new channels, relays to watch over a new Wear path.

**Alternatives rejected**
1. *Hook returns `"Failed"` eventType* — loses. MAIN StopFailure branch returns `"Stop"` or `"SubagentActive"` (codex-companion hold) at `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts:1872-1885`; forcing `"Failed"` would (a) lose the codex-hold case entirely, (b) inject an event value `TerminalAgentStore.recordEvent` stores raw (`packages\host-service\src\terminal-agents\store.ts:158`) that keep-awake's WORKING set and the BUS-RESYNC snapshot never handle, (c) change renderer dot behavior (`statusTransitions.ts:98-113` treats Failed identically to Stop only by fallthrough). Marker field decouples alerting from dot semantics — zero dot risk.
2. *Renderer visible-green as source* — loses per user decision; renderer green depends on visibility/blue axes; host semantic state is `TerminalAgentStore` (confirmed authoritative by `apps\desktop\src\main\lib\keep-awake\agent-activity.ts:6-11`).
3. *Reuse QuestionStore/PushSender.schedule* — loses. `PushSender` is question-shaped end to end: questionId fence columns `transcriptPath`/`toolUseId`, question-store fireVerdict, per-question promise chains (`packages\host-service\src\companion\push.ts:946-1020, 1213-1264`). Entangling per-terminal cycle state would risk the heavily-reasoned question invariants. Instead extract the shared FCM transport (`tokens()`/`targets()`/`deliver()`/`raiseFault` internals, `push.ts:1274-1318`) into `createFcmTransport` used by both senders — single-source precedent is the GUARD5-ANCHOR lesson (`companion-question-sink.ts:236-243`).
4. *In-memory dedupe only* — loses. Same restart argument that forced the question fence to disk (`packages\host-service\src\db\schema.ts:594-622`): host restart mid-cycle would either lose the armed cycle (missed alert) or re-alert a sent one.
5. *New FCM kinds under `v:"1"`* — loses hard. Kotlin v1 parser THROWS on unknown `k` (`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\Push.kt:77-79`); `v:"2"` returns `null` = graceful drop on old clients (`Push.kt:59`). Host v1 assert hard-pins `v==="1"`, `k∈{q,r}` (`push.ts:335-340`) — stays untouched; parallel v2 builder/assert.

**Corrections to your proposed direction**
- "StopFailure maps Failed" is a dead path for Claude: `map-event-type.ts:100-106` Failed branch is unreachable from the hook (collapsed at `pane-map-hook.ts:1872-1885`). Confirmed your finding.
- Codex failure signal does not exist anywhere: notify template maps only turn-complete/task_started/approvals (`apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-setup\templates\notify-hook.template.sh:69-75`); watcher sniffs `turn_aborted` as an explicit STOP (`agent-jsonl-watcher.ts:199-203`). Codex error alerts = phase 2 (out of scope below).
- `SessionEnd` also POSTs `"Stop"` (`pane-map-hook.ts:1886-1897`) and `Interrupt` maps to Stop (`map-event-type.ts:107-117`) — both would fire false greens without the `session-end` marker + the present-at-stop rule.
- Ready alerts: recommend **fire-only-if-away-at-transition** (present → cycle consumed, never held) instead of question-style hold. Present user saw the green; a held green firing hours later is stale noise. Errors KEEP hold semantics (actionable; fires on presence lapse if no new Start since). Presence fails toward away (`presence.ts` contract cited in `push.ts:1196-1202`), so a broken beacon fires rather than silences — correct direction for both kinds.
- Curation: reuse `isCuratedOffSidebar` shape (`companion\index.ts:1589-1620`) keyed by hostWorkspaceId; for greens curated-off = consume (skip), for errors = hold (question idiom).

## 3. Data flow / sequence

1. Claude turn ends → hook `_decide_event_type` → POST `{terminalId, eventType, agent, companionLifecycle?}` → `notifications.hook`.
2. Router: zod boundary validation (caps, additive optional field) → `mapEventType` → terminal-session lookup (`notifications.ts:213-255`) → dot work (broadcast :260, `recordEvent` :268) → `forwardCompanionCapture` :283 → `forwardCompanionLifecycle` (new, last; a throw = logged 500, dot already moved).
3. Sink → bridge `lifecycle-alerts`: load/create fence row for terminalId. Transitions write-through to sqlite BEFORE any await (commit-before-await precedent in `evaluate()`, `push.ts`). DB = source of truth across restarts.
4. On clean Stop + armed: presence verdict now — away → mint `alertWireId = deriveHandle("lifecycle-alert", terminalId + ":" + cycleStartedAtMs + ":" + kind)` (deterministic, restart-stable), fence → `readySent`, build v2 payload, `assertPushDataSafeV2` (throw, never log-and-continue), transport sends to all non-revoked tokened devices; present → fence `consumed`, no send, ever, this cycle.
5. On `turn-failed`: away → send error now (`errorSent`); present → `heldError`; sweep fires it on presence lapse unless a newer Start arrived (auto-resume recovery cancels it).
6. Phone FCM: refuse `notification` block (`CompanionMessagingService.kt:131`) → parse (v2) → route → post local fixed text on kind channel → relay to watch path → `LifecycleNotifier` posts on watch (bridging already disabled both ends: `NotificationBridging.kt:50`, `CompanionNotifications.kt:233`).
7. Re-arm: next `Start` with same/new session overwrites fence row with new `cycleStartedAtMs`, state `armed`.

**Identity/ordering**: `occurredAt` stamped at ingress (`notifications.ts:258`); sink calls synchronous, single process → processing order = arrival order. Straggler Start after Stop merely re-arms early (alert only fires on a subsequent Stop — harmless). Dedupe key = fence row (terminalId) + cycle (`cycleStartedAtMs`); sent states never overwritten for same cycle → restart cannot re-send. Bounds: one row per terminal; deleted on `session-end`/`Detached`; load-prune rows `updatedAtMs` > 7d (push-fence precedent). Auto-resume: each resend → new Start → new cycle; repeat failure → new error alert, bounded by auto-resume backoff + tombstones (`registry.ts:147-160`); "once per genuine error" = once per failed cycle, matching `makeFailureId`'s per-occurrence identity philosophy.

## 4. Build order

1. `PROTOCOL.md` §13.4/§15 — contract first (both impls move together, §16).
2. **Ask user: schema permission.** Then schema + migration + `lifecycle-fence.ts` + tests.
3. `push.ts` transport extraction + v2 builders/asserts + tests (question path proven unchanged by existing push tests).
4. `lifecycle-alerts.ts` state machine + tests (pure, synthetic events — fully verifiable standalone).
5. Sink file + router wiring + bridge composition + tests (feature live host-side; sends nothing until phone parses v2 — old clients drop null).
6. `pane-map-hook.ts` markers + hook tests.
7. Phone: Push.kt v2 + routing + channels + tests.
8. Watch: wear path + notifier.
9. `FEATURES.md` markers; device e2e (away/present, failure via forced api-error, restart mid-cycle).

## 5. Risks and edge cases

- **Schema change** — blocked on explicit user permission; migration runs on the FULL-sync host db (failed migration throws, never serves half-migrated: `db.ts:59-60`).
- **Nightly-merge surface**: router + pane-map-hook are AI-merged nightly; fork logic must stay in fork-only files with FEATURES.md marker tokens over the new python lines, else the SIDEBAR-STATE-PROJECTION failure mode repeats (`companion-question-sink.ts:118-124`).
- **Claude fail + codex-companion hold**: error alert fires while dot stays yellow (intended — Claude run died); codex finishing later hits a disarmed cycle → no ready alert for that codex tail. Accepted miss.

  - final event timestamp (`lastEventAt`)

I recommend ensuring the card immediately so the transition is observable without first visiting Kanban, while reusing deriveCardTitle/buildCompletedContext and the same timestamp.
- “Top” is not a manual rank operation. Completed cards are sorted newest-first by completedAt, with tabOrder only as a tie-break (`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\kanban\hooks\useKanbanData\useKanbanData.ts:62`).
