2. Files to modify/create
- Host hook/router/composition: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts`; `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\notifications\notifications.ts`; `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\registry.ts`; `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\packages\host-service\src\companion\index.ts`; a small lifecycle manager beside companion push; extract/reuse strict FCM transport from `...\companion\push.ts` without changing question scheduling.
- Companion protocol/phone/watch: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\core\src\main\java\family\khaira\supersetcompanion\core\protocol\Push.kt`; `...\core\wear\WearProtocol.kt`; phone messaging/routing/container/notification/WatchLink/WatchBridge files; watch listener plus a new separate lifecycle notifier. Co-locate tests with current protocol/routing tests; watch tests may be new because no app-watch test tree was found.
- Kanban/sidebar: `...\kanban\hooks\useKanbanActions\useKanbanActions.ts`; `...\kanban\components\KanbanBoard\KanbanBoard.tsx`; workspace item action hook; context menu; both workspace-item call sites. No schema file change is needed: completedAt already exists on workspace/card schemas (`C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\providers\CollectionsProvider\dashboardSidebarLocal\schema.ts:139` and `:662`).

3. Data flow
- Hook validates semantic event -> mints/reuses event ID -> tRPC boundary validates optional opaque ID and resolves authoritative workspace -> existing dot broadcast/store runs unchanged -> lifecycle manager dedups -> updates ready arm/error state -> one-shot presence and sidebar classification -> strict opaque FCM send.
- Phone rejects notification payload/unknown keys/version/expiry -> staged persistent claim -> sealed local tree lookup -> posts local ready/error notification -> explicit typed Wear send -> marks each completed stage. Watch validates model/expiry and event ID -> dedups -> posts local notification.
- Sidebar right-click -> predicate confirms current host worktree + sidebar-project membership + non-deleted -> shared useKanbanActions completion -> deterministic bound card becomes Completed with one timestamp/snapshot -> same timestamp stamps workspace sidebar row -> row leaves active sidebar, current route and pane layout remain mounted -> Completed read model sorts it first by timestamp.

4. Build order
1. Correct StopFailure and add stable hook event identity, with hook normalization tests.
2. Add strict router boundary and lifecycle state-machine unit tests.
3. Extract/reuse strict FCM transport; compose one-shot lifecycle manager; test presence/curation/dedup and disabled bridge behavior.
4. Add v2 Android parser and persistent staged ledger, then phone notifications.
5. Add Wear protocol/relay/listener/notifier and compatibility tests.
6. Refactor Kanban completion into one shared workspace action; keep drag on it.
7. Wire the sidebar menu predicate/handler and add regressions.
8. Cross-repo end-to-end checks with present/away, curated states, retry, host/phone restart, old protocol, connected/disconnected watch, and active workspace content.

5. Risks/edge cases
- No host schema means suppression/dedup decisions do not survive a host crash. Phone/watch persistent event IDs prevent delivered duplicates, but an event suppressed for presence and then replayed only after host restart can be reconsidered. This limitation must be documented rather than claiming durable host exactly-once. Achieving durable suppression across host restart would require approved persistence.
- A host crash before FCM send can lose an event because hooks are not a durable event log. Do not describe the design as guaranteed delivery.
- Main StopFailure while Codex holds is the highest-risk false-ready path; test it explicitly.
- clearWorkspaceStatuses sets administrative Stop and must never create remote ready.
- FCM collapse is optimization, not deduplication; event ledger is authoritative.
- Completing without a pre-existing card/column, completing an active pinned/grouped/snoozed/archived row, timestamp ties, missing host workspace, and removed sidebar project need tests. Missing authoritative workspace/project data should fail loud and make no partial card/sidebar mutation.
- The two local collection writes are not transactional. Centralize them with one timestamp and validate all prerequisites before either write; reconciliation may heal crash-interrupted state, but tests must cover card-only and sidebar-only partial state.

6. Minimum tests
- Hook: clean Stop, repeated Stop, StopFailure, PostToolUseFailure, Codex-held pending failure release, retry reuses ID.
- Host: malformed optional ID rejected; legacy missing ID keeps dots but no remote notice; ready arm matrix; each unique Failed; duplicate ID; presence suppression; every sidebar curation bucket; stale/missing/error curation sends; administrative Stop silent; FCM exact keys/opaque values.
- Android: strict v1 unchanged, exact v2 lifecycle keys, unknown version/kind/extra key/notification/expired rejected; staged duplicate/resume; local label and generic fallback; separate channels; no text from FCM; stable ID.
- Wear: new path decode, unknown old-client path harmless, duplicate ID, expiry, ready/error channel and stable ID.
- Kanban: shared action produces the same card+sidebar snapshot as drag; no-card-before-board path; completedAt newest-first/top; main/session/removed-project/deleted/missing-host rejected with no partial writes; snoozed/archived clears match drag; pinned/group placement semantics preserved; active `/v2-workspace/...` and `/kanban?cardId=...` route/search unchanged and paneLayout untouched; menu appears in collapsed and expanded worktree rows only.

Out of scope: schema/migrations, FCM display text, widening the companion tree status enum, question push/retraction behavior changes, workspace deep links from lifecycle notification taps, guaranteed offline Wear delivery, durable host exactly-once across crashes, or changing how Completed records are filtered/deleted.
</agent-message>

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

+    "android": {

+|---|---|---|
+| `v` | `"2"` | payload version — lifecycle alerts only |
+| `k` | `"g"` \| `"e"` | `g` = ready for review, `e` = stopped on an error |
+| `i` | 22 chars | `eventId` — opaque; identity of this event, used to alert once |
+| `w` | 22 chars | `workspaceId` — opaque; identity of the row the alert replaces |
+| `x` | 13 digits | expiry; after this the client discards the push unopened |

+client could not explain without text it is not allowed to have.

+and payloads are untouched.

+name, no project name, no file path, no agent output. Same runtime assertions in
+the bridge — closed key set, every value matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,43}$`, size

+alerts checks `v` *before* it checks its own closed key set, so a v2 payload

+at-least-once and the bridge may re-send after a reconnect, so the client
+remembers recent `eventId`s (bounded window, persisted — the FCM service is

+consume the alert its event was entitled to.

Adversarial review of uncommitted changes in both repos. All findings verified by reading code paths + running targeted tests (host-service 21/21 pass, desktop 8/8 pass — tests don't cover the defects below).

[BLOCKER] C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts:~2327-2340
Defect: lifecycle_seed includes payload.get("timestamp") and payload.get("tool_use_id"), but Claude Stop/StopFailure hook payloads carry neither (grep confirms "timestamp" is read nowhere else in the hook; both resolve to ""). Seed collapses to terminal_id+session_id+event+hook_event_name → identical lifecycle_event_id for EVERY Stop in a session.
Failure: user runs turn 1 in a terminal → ready alert fires. Turn 2, same session, hours later → same eventId → same alertId → lifecycle-alerts.ts mint() hits `deps.fence.knows(alertId)` (lifecycle-alerts.ts:112) and silently drops it. Fence retains sent records 7 days, so ALL subsequent ready alerts for that session are lost — feature degrades to once-per-session, not once-per-work-cycle. Same collapse for "e" (StopFailure). Note lifecycle-fence.ts:19-20/85-89 documents the INTENDED identity — armedAtMs via a `deriveLifecycleAlertId` — which was never implemented; implementing that (seed alertId from cycle.armedAtMs, unique per cycle) is the fix consistent with the restart-recompute guarantee the comment describes.
Fix: derive alert id from the armed cycle's armedAtMs (+terminal) as the fence header specifies, or add a per-cycle nonce (e.g. cycle armedAtMs) into the Python seed. Don't rely on payload timestamp fields that don't exist.

[MAJOR] C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\PROTOCOL.md §13.4
Defect: documents v2 collapse_key as `"<k>:<workspaceId>"` ("deliberate difference from v1" so newer alerts supersede in-flight ones). Implementation (fork push.ts) sets and asserts collapse_key = data.i (the alertId) for BOTH versions.
Failure: reader implements/audits against the doc → mismatch; the documented supersede-in-flight behavior does not exist (each alert has unique collapse key). Mitigated client-side only by notification tag + onlyAlertOnce.
Fix: either implement `k:workspaceId` collapse in push.ts sendLifecycleAlert or correct §13.4 to state collapse_key = alertId.

[MAJOR] C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion\PROTOCOL.md §13.4 + app-phone\...\wear\WatchLink.kt:87-136
Defect: doc claims "the Data Layer queues while the watch is off the wrist... delivers on reconnect". WatchLink uses MessageClient.sendMessage (fire-and-forget, no queueing); empty connectedNodes → NoWatchPaired, alert dropped.
Failure: watch on charger when agent finishes → phone notifies, watch mirror silently lost forever — phone-side SeenLifecycleEvents dedupe already consumed the eventId, so no path re-delivers to the watch. Contradicts documented behavior.
Fix: use DataClient (Data Layer items, which DO queue) for lifecycle mirroring, or correct the doc and accept the loss explicitly.

[MAJOR] C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\kanban\hooks\useKanbanActions\useKanbanActions.ts:~216 + useCompleteWorkspaceCard.ts
Defect: completeCard for a workspace-bound card now delegates entirely to completeWorkspaceCard, which refuses (console.error no-op) when the host workspace row is missing or project left sidebar; canDropCard still returns "ok" for that same card (only rejects type "main").
Failure: branch deleted while its card sits on the board (prune grace window) → user drags card to Completed → drop accepted, nothing happens, no toast; card then pruned when grace expires. Old code froze it as a completed record. Silent data loss of the completion record + UX dead-end.
Fix: in the missing-workspace case fall back to plain card completion (freeze record, old behavior), or make canDropCard reject with visible feedback; surface refusals as toasts, not console.error.

[MINOR] fork packages\host-service\src\trpc\router\notifications\companion-lifecycle-sink.ts:15 vs companion-lifecycle-sink.ts:9 / lifecycle-alerts.ts:137
Defect: zod enum + runtime pass "progress" but CompanionLifecycleEvent.outcome type omits it → TS2367 at lifecycle-alerts.ts:137, TS2345 at call site. Runtime correct; accepted type debt per repo policy, but the comparison-appears-unintentional warning will confuse future merges.
Fix: add "progress" to the outcome union.

[MINOR] fork packages\host-service\src\companion\lifecycle-fence.ts:19-20,85-89
Defect: header/JSDoc claims alert id derives from armedAtMs via `deriveLifecycleAlertId` — function doesn't exist; actual derivation is lifecycleAlertId(eventId) in lifecycle-alerts.ts:46. (Also the root cause pointer for the BLOCKER.)
Fix: align doc with implementation once the BLOCKER identity fix lands.

[MINOR] fork packages\host-service\src\companion\push.ts (broadcast log)
Defect: "nothing to push/retract" log labels all non-"q" kinds "retract" — v2 "g"/"e" mislabeled in diagnostics.
Fix: log the kind literal.

[MINOR] fork ...\kanban\hooks\useCompleteWorkspaceCard\useCompleteWorkspaceCard.ts
Defect: all refusal paths are console.error-only; user action (context-menu "Mark completed", drop) silently no-ops. Soft violation of fail-loud rule.
Fix: toast on refusal.

Checked clean: v2 push privacy (opaque-only closed key sets both ends, version-first parse, no text), assertPushDataSafe throw semantics, fence atomicity/bounds/corruption handling/restart reconstruction, markSent-before-await no-double-send, presence + sidebar-curation gating parity with question push (2s sweep both), bridge wiring + LIFO unwind, sink registration guard, strip-and-retry compatibility with old host-service, subagent/tool-failure exclusion from lifecycle outcomes, codex-hold pendingFailure latch/release, renderer Failed handling (statusTransitions parity with Stop, chime + "Error" title), Android channel setup timing, watch-side expiry re-check, phone dedupe order (expiry→dup→alert), SeenLifecycleEvents bounds/thread-safety, Mark completed eligibility gating (canMarkWorkspaceCompleted), completeWorkspace semantics (main refusal, snooze/archive clear), buildCompletedWorkspaceCard invariants + snooze/archive preservation, frozen-record exclusion in useKanbanData.

Verdict: **FIX-FIRST** — the BLOCKER guts the feature's core promise (ready alert per work cycle) after the first turn of every session.

diff --git a/FEATURES.md b/FEATURES.md
index 6c3328efbd..976d1bb883 100644
--- a/FEATURES.md
+++ b/FEATURES.md
@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ in the merge that drops it (the only legitimate way a marker leaves this list).
 | Window controls | native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close set on Windows | `titleBarOverlay` |
 | Windows behaviour fixes | child-process patch, cmd.exe fallback, force-foreground, watchdog, WebGL recovery, fast startup | `windows-child-process` |
 | Agent status dots (Claude + Codex) | per-terminal dot + workspace rollup; host-service POST + JSONL watcher | `pane-map-hook`, `StatusIndicator` |
+| Companion lifecycle alerts | phone + custom watch receive distinct ready-for-review and terminal-agent-failure notifications; ready fires once per real work cycle, tool/subagent/admin failures are excluded, and presence/sidebar curation match blocked-agent push behavior | `(COMPANION-LIFECYCLE-ALERTS)` |
 | Claude Stop unhooked from notify.sh | upstream's raw Stop passthrough must never race superset-notify.py (it wiped the blue dot + yellow-hold) | `CLAUDE-STOP-UNHOOKED` |
 | Compaction shows working | Claude context compaction (manual /compact + auto) drives the yellow dot via PreCompact / SessionStart(source=compact) | `(COMPACT-YELLOW)` |
 | Team/workflow work shows working | background_tasks[] entry types split the post-turn dot: agent-type work (teammate/subagent/workflow) holds yellow; shell-only goes blue | `(TEAM-YELLOW)` |
@@ -46,7 +47,7 @@ in the merge that drops it (the only legitimate way a marker leaves this list).
 | Agent-hook bash-wrap | Gemini/Cursor `.sh` hooks run via Git-for-Windows bash | `agent-wrappers` |
 | Kanban board | device-local board mirroring branches + Queued column | `v2KanbanCards`, `KANBAN_QUEUE_COLUMN_ID` |
 | Kanban host-served workspace source | every fork surface that needs the workspace universe (kanban seed/prune/render, bound-card actions, collapse-split, recycle-bin destroy URL, sidebar snooze/archive fallbacks, is-local gate) reads the host-served lists (`useHostWorkspaces`), NEVER the Electric `v2Workspaces` mirror — upstream's offline-first migration stopped writing new rows to the cloud table, so Electric reads silently miss every post-migration branch | `(KANBAN-HOST-SOURCE)` |
-| Kanban Completed column | fixed FINAL column: dropping a card stamps an editable completed date and hides the thread from the sidebar ENTIRELY (drag out un-completes/restores); per-column date filter (all / last calendar month / custom range) for work-done reports; completed cards survive branch deletion as frozen records; main cards can't complete | `KANBAN_COMPLETED_COLUMN_ID` |
+| Kanban Completed column | fixed FINAL column: dropping a card or choosing Mark completed on an active non-main worktree stamps an editable completed date and hides the thread from the sidebar ENTIRELY (drag out un-completes/restores); per-column date filter (all / last calendar month / custom range) for work-done reports; completed cards survive branch deletion as frozen records; main cards can't complete | `KANBAN_COMPLETED_COLUMN_ID`, `(KANBAN-MARK-COMPLETED)` |
 | Kanban append-only backup | daily write-once JSON snapshot of the board; code can never delete/overwrite one | `writeKanbanBackup` |
 | Kanban sidebar button toggles | sidebar Kanban press: anywhere → full-screen board; part-screen split → full-screen (closing then reopens that workspace full size); full-screen → close back to the remembered previous page (fallback Workspaces list) | `(KANBAN-TOGGLE)` |
 | Subagent tool events never stomp the red | a PostToolUse whose payload carries `agent_id` (ran inside a subagent) maps to the red-respecting SubagentActive — background agents' tool completions must not clear a pending AskUserQuestion/permission red; only a main-loop completion does. SubagentStart likewise | `(SUBTOOL-RED)` |

 ### 13.1 The payload — opaque ids only
 
+This section describes `v` = `"1"`, which carries questions and retractions.
+Lifecycle alerts ("an agent finished", "an agent failed") are `v` = `"2"` with
+their own closed key set — see §13.4.

 from a phone that was dozing, so foreground-sweep is required, not optional.
 
+### 13.4 Lifecycle alerts — an agent finished, an agent failed
+
+A question means *an agent is blocked on you*. Two other things happen that are
+worth a glance and are not that: an agent **finished** and its work is waiting to
+be reviewed, and an agent **stopped on an error** and will not continue by
+itself. Neither can be answered from a companion device, and neither should
+arrive looking like something that can.
+
+They travel as a **separate payload version**, `v` = `"2"`, with its own closed
+key set — deliberately not a third `k` inside v1:
+
+```json
+{
+  "message": {
+    "token": "<device fcm token>",
+    "android": {
+      "priority": "high",
+      "ttl": "900s",
+      "collapse_key": "<alertId>"
+    },
+    "data": {
+      "v": "2",
+      "k": "g",
+      "i": "<alertId, 22 chars>",
+      "w": "<workspaceId, 22 chars>",
+      "x": "<expiresAtMs, 13 digits>"
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+| Key | Values | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `v` | `"2"` | payload version — lifecycle alerts only |
+| `k` | `"g"` \| `"e"` | `g` = ready for review, `e` = stopped on an error |
+| `i` | 22 chars | `alertId` — opaque; minted by the bridge from the armed work cycle and alert kind. The identity of the alert everywhere: `collapse_key`, the client's dedupe window, and the client's notification id |
+| `w` | 22 chars | `workspaceId` — opaque; which workspace the alert is about |
+| `x` | 13 digits | expiry; after this the client discards the push unopened |
+
+There is no `n`: an alert is about one event, and a count would be a number the
+client could not explain without text it is not allowed to have.
+
+**`collapse_key` is `data.i`, the same assertion as v1.** For v1 that lets a
+retraction overtake the question it cancels. For v2 there is no retraction, and
+`i` is a new id per lifecycle event, so collapsing on it merges only a redelivery
+of the *same* alert — which is exactly what should merge. Two different events
+for one workspace are two different facts and both land, on the wire and on the
+screen: the clients identify a notification by `i` as well, so an alert is never
+silently swallowed by an unrelated one that happens to share a workspace.
+
+**The §13.1 hard constraint applies unchanged.** No workspace name, no branch
+name, no project name, no file path, no agent output. Same runtime assertions in
+the bridge — closed key set, every value matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,43}$`, size
+cap, no `notification` block — and the client asserts them again on arrival.
+
+**Why a new version rather than a new kind.** A client that predates lifecycle
+alerts checks `v` *before* it checks its own closed key set, so a v2 payload
+comes back as "a version I do not implement" and is ignored silently. Had this
+been `k: "g"` inside v1, the same client would have refused it as a malformed
+question — logged as a protocol violation, counted as a refused push, and
+indistinguishable from a real leak attempt. The client test suite pins the order
+of those two checks for exactly this reason.
+
+**One alert per event, one row per alert.** FCM is at-least-once and the bridge
+may re-send after a reconnect, so the client remembers recent `i`s (bounded
+window, persisted — the FCM service is rebuilt per message and the process dies
+between deliveries) and alerts once per alert id. That same id is the
+notification's identity on the phone and on the watch, so a redelivery that did
+get through would update its own row rather than add one, and an unrelated event
+for the same workspace keeps its own. Expiry is checked **before** dedupe, so an
+expired duplicate cannot consume the alert its event was entitled to.
+
+**Surfaces.** The phone posts on its own channels — "Ready for review"
+(no vibration; nothing is blocked) and "Agent errors" (vibrates; it will not
+recover on its own) — separate from "Blocked agents" so each can be turned off
+independently. The wording is fixed and local; there is nothing to fetch and
+nothing to interpolate. The notification is `localOnly`, and the phone relays the
+alert to the watch itself over a dedicated Data Layer path
+`/companion/v1/lifecycle`:
+
+```ts
+type WatchLifecycleAlert = {
+  kind: "ready" | "error";
+  eventId: string;      // opaque; the alertId carried through from `i`
+  workspaceId: string;  // opaque
+  raisedAtMs: number;
+  expiresAtMs: number;  // carried through from `x`
+};
+```
+
+The watch re-checks `expiresAtMs` itself and drops an expired alert, rather than
+trusting the phone's check. The phone's check answers a question about a
+different moment and a different clock: `MessageClient` is best-effort and does
+**not** queue for a disconnected watch — an alert sent while the watch is out of
+range is dropped, not replayed on reconnect — but a message that does get through
+can still sit before the watch's listener handles it. Without the wrist's own
+boundary, a delayed message could buzz for an agent that finished hours ago.
+`expiresAtMs` has no default in the message — an alert that arrives without it is
+refused, not treated as "never expires".
+
+A wrist alert is therefore best-effort by design. The phone's notification is the
+one that is guaranteed to exist; the watch copy is a convenience that a watch out
+of range simply does not get, and the user finds the finished work on the phone
+or at the desk instead.
+
+That path is not the question path, and that is the point: a lifecycle alert
+never enters the watch's question state machine, never displaces a question the
+user is part-way through answering, and never cancels a question's notification.
+The watch renders its own alert on its own channels and a tap opens the app at
+**home** — there is no answer screen behind it, because there is nothing to
+answer.
+
+Lifecycle alerts are not retracted (§13.3). A question stops being true when
+someone answers it; "an agent finished" stays true, and the alert simply expires
+or is dismissed.
+
+**What the bridge guarantees, and what the client must not assume.** `g` fires
+once per armed work-cycle that reaches a clean final stop — a duplicate stop is
+silent, and a later start re-arms — and `e` fires only on a terminal agent
+failure, never on a tool, background or subagent failure. Presence and sidebar
+curation *hold* an alert rather than consume it, so an alert may arrive well
+after the event it describes but never twice for the same event. The client
+therefore treats lateness as normal (which is what `x` bounds) and still dedupes
+on `i` itself: "the bridge sends it once" is a property of the bridge, and a
+client that leaned on it would buzz twice the first time FCM redelivered.
+

+of the *same* alert — which is exactly what should merge. Two different events
+for one workspace are two different facts and both land, on the wire and on the
+screen: the clients identify a notification by `i` as well, so an alert is never
+silently swallowed by an unrelated one that happens to share a workspace.
+
+**The §13.1 hard constraint applies unchanged.** No workspace name, no branch
+name, no project name, no file path, no agent output. Same runtime assertions in
+the bridge — closed key set, every value matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,43}$`, size
+cap, no `notification` block — and the client asserts them again on arrival.
+
+**Why a new version rather than a new kind.** A client that predates lifecycle
+alerts checks `v` *before* it checks its own closed key set, so a v2 payload
+comes back as "a version I do not implement" and is ignored silently. Had this
+been `k: "g"` inside v1, the same client would have refused it as a malformed
+question — logged as a protocol violation, counted as a refused push, and
+indistinguishable from a real leak attempt. The client test suite pins the order
+of those two checks for exactly this reason.
+
+**One alert per event, one row per alert.** FCM is at-least-once and the bridge
+may re-send after a reconnect, so the client remembers recent `i`s (bounded
+window, persisted — the FCM service is rebuilt per message and the process dies
+between deliveries) and alerts once per alert id. That same id is the
+notification's identity on the phone and on the watch, so a redelivery that did
+get through would update its own row rather than add one, and an unrelated event
+for the same workspace keeps its own. Expiry is checked **before** dedupe, so an
+expired duplicate cannot consume the alert its event was entitled to.
+
+**Surfaces.** The phone posts on its own channels — "Ready for review"
+(no vibration; nothing is blocked) and "Agent errors" (vibrates; it will not
+recover on its own) — separate from "Blocked agents" so each can be turned off
+independently. The wording is fixed and local; there is nothing to fetch and
+nothing to interpolate. The notification is `localOnly`, and the phone relays the
+alert to the watch itself over a dedicated Data Layer path
+`/companion/v1/lifecycle`:
+
+```ts
+type WatchLifecycleAlert = {
+  kind: "ready" | "error";
+  eventId: string;      // opaque; the alertId carried through from `i`
+  workspaceId: string;  // opaque
+  raisedAtMs: number;
+  expiresAtMs: number;  // carried through from `x`
+};
+```
+
+The watch re-checks `expiresAtMs` itself and drops an expired alert, rather than
+trusting the phone's check. The phone's check answers a question about a
+different moment and a different clock: `MessageClient` is best-effort and does
+**not** queue for a disconnected watch — an alert sent while the watch is out of
+range is dropped, not replayed on reconnect — but a message that does get through
+can still sit before the watch's listener handles it. Without the wrist's own
+boundary, a delayed message could buzz for an agent that finished hours ago.
+`expiresAtMs` has no default in the message — an alert that arrives without it is
+refused, not treated as "never expires".
+
+A wrist alert is therefore best-effort by design. The phone's notification is the
+one that is guaranteed to exist; the watch copy is a convenience that a watch out
+of range simply does not get, and the user finds the finished work on the phone
+or at the desk instead.
+
+That path is not the question path, and that is the point: a lifecycle alert
+never enters the watch's question state machine, never displaces a question the
+user is part-way through answering, and never cancels a question's notification.
+The watch renders its own alert on its own channels and a tap opens the app at
+**home** — there is no answer screen behind it, because there is nothing to
+answer.
+
+Lifecycle alerts are not retracted (§13.3). A question stops being true when
+someone answers it; "an agent finished" stays true, and the alert simply expires
+or is dismissed.
+
+**What the bridge guarantees, and what the client must not assume.** `g` fires
+once per armed work-cycle that reaches a clean final stop — a duplicate stop is
+silent, and a later start re-arms — and `e` fires only on a terminal agent
+failure, never on a tool, background or subagent failure. Presence and sidebar
+curation *hold* an alert rather than consume it, so an alert may arrive well
+after the event it describes but never twice for the same event. The client
+therefore treats lateness as normal (which is what `x` bounds) and still dedupes
+on `i` itself: "the bridge sends it once" is a property of the bridge, and a
+client that leaned on it would buzz twice the first time FCM redelivered.
+

content.text:
Implemented both requested features locally across the desktop and companion repositories.

## New phone/watch notifications

Added separate alerts for:

- **Ready for review** — fires once after each genuine agent work cycle finishes.
- **Agent error** — fires only when the terminal agent itself fails, not when an individual tool, background task, or subagent fails.
- Existing blocked/question notifications remain unchanged.

Behavior:

- Phone and custom watch use distinct notification channels and wording.
- Alerts are deduplicated by event.
- Phone notifications open Superset rather than an answer screen.
- Watch alerts use a dedicated message path and never interfere with pending questions.
- FCM payloads remain content-free and strictly validated.
- Snoozed, archived, completed, or hidden work remains curated using existing sidebar rules.
- Desktop errors now say **Error**, rather than incorrectly appearing as normal completion.
- No database schema or migration was added.

Important limitations:

- Watch delivery is best-effort while connected; its current message transport does not queue alerts while disconnected.
- A host-service restart can lose a ready/error alert still being held because the user is present. The database remains the source of lifecycle transition truth, but durable held-alert storage would require a schema change and explicit permission.

## Mark completed

Added **Mark completed** to the right-click menu for active, non-main project worktrees.

It:

- Uses the same completion operation as dragging a card to Completed.
- Places the card at the top of Completed.
- Creates the Kanban card if it has not yet been created.
- Removes the worktree from the active sidebar exactly like Kanban drag.
- Keeps currently open terminals and content visible.
- Excludes main workspaces, Sessions, inactive lifecycle rows, and ineligible worktrees.
- Preserves frozen completion records if the underlying worktree has disappeared.
- Shows a visible error instead of silently failing.

## Validation

Passed:

- Host companion suite: **246 passed, 0 failed**
- Lifecycle/Kanban focused tests: **12 passed, 0 failed**
- Notification router tests: **14 passed, 0 failed**
- Desktop watcher tests: **23 passed, 0 failed**
- Desktop error notification tests: **4 passed, 0 failed**
- Android lifecycle tests for core, phone, and watch: **passed**
- Biome on every changed Superset source file: **clean**
- Reference-error gate: **0 dangerous diagnostics**
- Feature marker gate: **all 149 markers present**
- Diff checks: **clean**

The broader Android core suite reached compilation but still has two existing cross-runtime vector test failures unrelated to these changes.

`/simplify` was completed, and a Fable adversarial re-review returned **SHIP** after its findings were fixed. Sol and Opus review agents were also run, but they did not return final reports before being stopped to clear the status bar.

The changes remain **uncommitted and unpushed** in:

- `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64`
- `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\superset-companion`

     Alert identity derives from:

     ```ts
     function lifecycleAlertId(input: {
       hostTerminalId: string;
       armedAtMs: number;
       kind: "g" | "e";
     }): string {
       return createHash("sha256")
         .update("sc/v2 lifecycle alert\0", "utf8")
         .update(input.kind, "utf8")
         .update("\0", "utf8")
         .update(input.hostTerminalId, "utf8")
         .update("\0", "utf8")
         .update(String(input.armedAtMs), "utf8")
         .digest("base64url")
         .slice(0, 22);
     }
     ```

     Current transition gate:

     ```ts
     if (input.outcome !== "ready" && input.outcome !== "failed") return;

     if (
       input.previousEventAtMs === null ||
       (input.previousEventType !== "Start" &&
         input.previousEventType !== "SubagentActive" &&
         input.previousEventType !== "BackgroundRunning")
     ) {
       return;
     }

     mint(
       input,
       input.previousEventAtMs,
       input.outcome === "failed" ? "e" : "g",
     );
     ```

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

4. If results are broad, rerun `entire search --json` with a narrower query instead of switching tools.
5. Summarize the strongest matches with the relevant commit, session, file, and prompt details available in the results.

Keep answers concise and evidence-based.

#!/bin/bash
# Wrapper for biome check that fails on ANY diagnostic (info, warn, or error)

output=$(bunx @biomejs/biome@2.4.2 check "$@" 2>&1)
exit_code=$?

echo "$output"

# Check if there are any diagnostics (errors, warnings, or infos)
if echo "$output" | grep -qE "Found [0-9]+ (error|info|warning)"; then
  exit 1
fi

# Run every guard even after one fails, so a contributor sees all violations
# in a single pass. Don't use `set -e` here: it would abort before the biome
# output above is echoed.
./scripts/check-desktop-git-env.sh || exit_code=1
./scripts/check-git-ref-strings.sh || exit_code=1
./scripts/check-cloud-workspace-usage.sh || exit_code=1
./scripts/check-simple-git-usage.sh || exit_code=1

exit $exit_code

1	/**
2	 * (COMPANION-BRIDGE) — FCM push: registration, the delayed timer, retraction (§7.6, §13).
3	 *
4	 * HARD CONSTRAINT OF THE FORMAT: no question text, no option text, no workspace
5	 * name, no branch name, no project name, no file path and no free text of any
6	 * kind may EVER appear in an FCM message. Google is not in the trust boundary.
7	 * This is not a guideline — `assertPushDataSafe` THROWS, it never logs and
8	 * continues.
9	 *
10	 * The message is data-only. `message.notification` must be absent: setting it
11	 * would have Android render text supplied through Google's infrastructure,
12	 * breaking the constraint by construction. `assertPushDataSafe` enforces a
13	 * CLOSED key set on the envelope as well as on `data`, so no later edit can add
14	 * an `apns`/`webpush`/`notification` block carrying text without failing.
15	 *
16	 * PRESENCE IS THE FEATURE, AND IT REPLACED A DELAY. A red does not wait three
17	 * minutes any more; it pushes IMMEDIATELY when the user is away and NEVER while
18	 * they are at the desk. This module does not own that judgement —
19	 * `companion/presence.ts` does, from two signals (human keystrokes into a
20	 * terminal, and the Electron beacon carrying OS idle time and lock state). This
21	 * module owns what to DO with it:
22	 *
23	 *   away at capture      -> fire now, zero latency. The user cannot see the
24	 *                           question, so every second of delay is a blocked
25	 *                           agent nobody knows about.
26	 *   present at capture   -> HOLD, with no deadline. They can see it. A push for
27	 *                           a question already on their screen is exactly the
28	 *                           noise that gets a watch muted inside a week, and a
29	 *                           muted watch is the same as one never built.
30	 *   present -> away      -> the sweep fires everything still held. Walking away,
31	 *                           or locking the screen, is the trigger.
32	 *   answered at the desk -> `cancelPending` disarms it and it never buzzes.
33	 *
34	 * There is NO CEILING on a hold. "You have been looking at this question for N
35	 * minutes, so let me also buzz your wrist" is a notification about something
36	 * already in front of the user. A hold ends by absence, or by the question
37	 * expiring (`PUSH_QUESTION_EXPIRY_MS`) — never by a timer.
38	 *
39	 * The 30-80 questions a day this handles are mostly answered at the desk within
40	 * seconds. Under the old delay they cost three minutes of silence each when
41	 * nobody was there; under presence gating they buzz at once when nobody is
42	 * there, and not at all when somebody is. The notification's meaning is
43	 * unchanged and is the whole point: *nobody has dealt with this.*
44	 *
45	 * -- Sleep / resume (still no per-question `setTimeout`) ----------------------
46	 *
47	 * VERIFIED, not assumed, and the reasoning survives the redesign intact. Node
48	 * timers are driven by libuv's monotonic clock (`uv_hrtime`), which on Windows
49	 * is `QueryPerformanceCounter`, and Microsoft documents QPC's suspend behaviour
50	 * explicitly:
51	 *
52	 *   "QueryPerformanceCounter reads the performance counter and returns the
53	 *    total number of ticks that have occurred since the Windows operating
54	 *    system was started, INCLUDING THE TIME WHEN THE MACHINE WAS IN A SLEEP
55	 *    STATE such as standby, hibernate, or connected standby."
56	 *   -- learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/sysinfo/acquiring-high-resolution-time-stamps
57	 *
58	 * So a `setTimeout` deadline armed before a six-hour suspend does not fire at
59	 * its deadline and does not fire some grace period after the lid opens: it
60	 * fires the instant the process thaws, for every question at once, at the exact
61	 * moment the user sits back down. That is why there is no per-question timer
62	 * here, only a coarse repeating sweep that re-evaluates presence and therefore
63	 * has no deadline to miss.
64	 *
65	 * The batched-buzz-at-lid-open failure the old awake-time accounting existed to
66	 * prevent has NOT been forgotten — it moved to where it belongs. A machine that
67	 * has just woken has a keystroke stamp from before the suspend and no fresh
68	 * beacon, which reads as "away" and would fire everything held. `presence.ts`
69	 * opens a ten-second settling window on an Electron `resume`/`unlock` beacon, in
70	 * which held questions stay held (F7). It delays a correct push by ten seconds;
71	 * it never cancels one.
72	 *
73	 * `Date.now()` is wall-clock, so it is corrected on resume and stepped by NTP in
74	 * either direction. Every age computed from it in this feature is clamped at
75	 * zero and discarded past a future tolerance, and both failure directions
76	 * resolve towards "away" — see `human-input.ts` and `presence.ts`.
77	 *
78	 * -- Serialising a send against its own retraction ----------------------------
79	 *
80	 * A send takes tens of seconds in the worst case (bounded retries with backoff).
81	 * The old code committed the sent record, started the broadcast, and let
82	 * `retract` run independently — so an answer arriving mid-send could complete
83	 * its retraction while the ORIGINAL push was still in FCM's queue, and the
84	 * original would then be delivered AFTER the retraction that was supposed to
85	 * cancel it. The notification outlives its subject, which is the one thing §13.3
86	 * exists to prevent.
87	 *
88	 * So every FCM operation for a questionId runs on a per-question promise chain,
89	 * and a retraction additionally CANCELS the in-flight send (the cancel is
90	 * checked between attempts, so a retraction does not wait out four backoffs).
91	 * Chaining per question is strictly stronger than the per-(questionId, device)
92	 * ordering that is actually required, and is far simpler to prove.
93	 *
94	 * -- Restart (the fence) ------------------------------------------------------
95	 *
96	 * Schedule state used to be deliberately in-memory: a restart drops it, but a
97	 * restart also drops the question store, so questions are re-captured from the
98	 * hook path and re-armed from zero. True, and harmless for a three-minute delay.
99	 * Not harmless now — a HELD question has no deadline, so losing it loses the
100	 * push entirely, and a question already pushed would be re-armed and pushed a
101	 * SECOND time. Both the armed set and the sent set are therefore rows in host.db
102	 * (`push-fence.ts`), reconstructed at start.
103	 *
104	 * The sweeper still never trusts `cancelPending`: at fire time it re-asks the
105	 * question store whether the question is still unanswered.
106	 *
107	 * ── Trust / secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
108	 *
109	 * The service account at `~/.superset/companion/fcm-service-account.json` lives
110	 * OUTSIDE both repos. Its contents are never logged, never included in an error
111	 * message, and never returned to a caller: failures name the FIELD or the PATH,
112	 * never a value. Minted OAuth access tokens are held in memory only and are
113	 * likewise never logged.
114	 *
115	 * An auth failure FAILS LOUD. A broken service account must not degrade to
116	 * silence — silence is indistinguishable from "no questions", which is the one
117	 * state the user must never be wrong about.
118	 */

37	        val manager = NotificationManagerCompat.from(context)

39	        // was never granted, or notifications are disabled for the app or its channel.
40	        // The permission check is inline rather than behind a helper because it is also

62	            return false
63	        }

65

67

69	        // alert that is not about a question must not send it looking for one.
70	        val open = Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java).apply {
71	            action = Intent.ACTION_MAIN

82	            .setSmallIcon(R.drawable.ic_launcher_foreground)
83	            .setContentTitle(presentation.title)
84	            .setContentText(presentation.text)
85	            .setContentIntent(pending)
86	            .setCategory(
87	                if (presentation.vibrates) {
88	                    NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_ERROR
89	                } else {

package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.notify

import android.app.NotificationChannel
import android.app.NotificationManager
import android.app.PendingIntent
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.util.Log
import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat
import androidx.core.app.NotificationManagerCompat
import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchQuestion
import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchQuestionOversize
import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.MainActivity
import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.R

const val EXTRA_QUESTION_ID = "family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.QUESTION_ID"

private const val CHANNEL_ID = "companion.questions"
private const val TAG = "CompanionNotify"

/**
 * The buzz, and nothing else.
 *
 * > **Question text NEVER goes through a notification.** Android clamps notification strings
 * > to 1 024 characters and truncates SILENTLY, and 64% of this user's real questions are
 * > longer than that. A user answering a question whose second half they never saw is the
 * > precise failure this whole app exists to prevent. The notification carries the headline
 * > (contract-bounded to 80 chars, PROTOCOL.md §9.4) and a count; the body lives in the app.
 *
 * Any change here that puts `WatchQuestionItem.question` — or an option label, or a free-text
 * value — into a notification field is a regression, not a feature.
 */
object QuestionNotifier {

    fun notifyQuestion(context: Context, question: WatchQuestion): Boolean {
        val itemCount = question.items.size
        val subtitle = buildString {
            append(if (itemCount == 1) "1 question" else "$itemCount questions")
            question.sourceLabel?.let { append(" · ").append(it) }
        }
        return post(
            context = context,
            questionId = question.questionId,
            title = question.headline,
            text = subtitle,
        )
    }

    fun notifyOversize(context: Context, info: WatchQuestionOversize): Boolean = post(
        context = context,
        questionId = info.questionId,
        title = info.headline,
        text = "Too large for the watch — answer on the phone",
    )

    fun cancel(context: Context, questionId: String) {
        NotificationManagerCompat.from(context).cancel(notificationId(questionId))
    }

    /**
     * @return whether the user was actually buzzed. `false` means notifications are switched
     * off for this app — reported, never papered over: the in-app banner tells the user their
     * watch will stay silent.
     */
    private fun post(context: Context, questionId: String, title: String, text: String): Boolean {
        val manager = NotificationManagerCompat.from(context)
        if (!manager.areNotificationsEnabled()) {
            Log.e(
                TAG,
                "notifications are disabled for this app — question $questionId will not buzz",
            )
            return false
        }
        ensureChannel(context)

2	
3	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.ProtocolException
4	
5	/** `k` in a lifecycle push payload (PROTOCOL.md §13.4). */
6	enum class LifecycleKind(val wire: String) {
7	    /** An agent finished and its work is waiting to be reviewed. Nothing is blocked. */
8	    READY("g"),
9	
10	    /** An agent stopped on an error. Nothing is blocked either; nothing can proceed. */
11	    ERROR("e"),
12	    ;
13	
14	    companion object {
15	        fun fromWire(raw: String): LifecycleKind? = entries.firstOrNull { it.wire == raw }
16	    }
17	}
18	
19	/**
20	 * A lifecycle alert delivered as an FCM data-only message (PROTOCOL.md §13.4).
21	 *
22	 * These are **not** questions. A question blocks an agent and can be answered from the
23	 * phone or the wrist; a lifecycle alert only says that something changed state, so every
24	 * surface it reaches is read-only and opens the app rather than offering an answer.
25	 *
26	 * > **The §13.1 hard constraint applies unchanged: no workspace name, no branch name, no
27	 * > project name, no file path, no agent output, and no free text of any kind.** Google
28	 * > is not in the trust boundary and a lifecycle alert does not get an exemption because
29	 * > its text would have been short. The wording the user sees is a fixed local string.
30	 *
31	 * The payload is a **separate closed key set under `v` = [VERSION]**, deliberately not an
32	 * extra `k` inside v1. A build that predates lifecycle alerts stops at the version check
33	 * in [PushData.parse] — before its own closed-key check — and returns `null`, so an old
34	 * phone ignores these silently instead of refusing them as malformed. That ordering is
35	 * the whole backward-safety story and is pinned by a test.
36	 *
37	 * Like a question push it carries **nothing displayable**: [eventId] and [workspaceId]
38	 * are opaque, and the client renders fixed wording. It never invents text and it never
39	 * fetches text to put in a lifecycle alert.
40	 */
41	class LifecyclePushData private constructor(
42	    val kind: LifecycleKind,
43	    /**
44	     * `i` — the bridge's alert id: one per lifecycle alert, minted from the armed work
45	     * cycle that ended and the kind it ended in. It is the identity of the alert
46	     * everywhere, on the wire (`collapse_key`) and on both clients (the dedupe window and
47	     * the notification identity).
48	     */
49	    val eventId: String,
50	    val workspaceId: String,
51	    val expiresAtMs: Long,
52	) {
53	    fun isExpired(nowMs: Long): Boolean = nowMs >= expiresAtMs
54	
55	    override fun toString(): String =
56	        "LifecyclePushData(kind=${kind.wire}, eventId=$eventId, workspaceId=$workspaceId)"
57	
58	    companion object {
59	        /** The payload version that carries lifecycle alerts. v1 is questions only. */
60	        const val VERSION = "2"
61	
62	        private const val LABEL = "lifecycle payload"
63	        private val KEYS = setOf("v", "k", "i", "w", "x")
64	
65	        /**
66	         * @return `null` when `v` is not [VERSION] — this parser owns exactly one version
67	         *   and says nothing about the others; [CompanionPush.parse] dispatches. Anything
68	         *   else malformed is a hard error, because it means either a bridge bug or an
69	         *   attempt to smuggle content through Google.
70	         */
71	        fun parse(data: Map<String, String>): LifecyclePushData? {
72	            if (PushEnvelope.version(data) != VERSION) return null
73	            PushEnvelope.requireClosedAndOpaque(data, KEYS, LABEL, "§13.4")
74	
75	            val kind =
76	                LifecycleKind.fromWire(required(data, "k"))
77	                    ?: throw ProtocolException("lifecycle payload 'k' is not a known kind")
78	            val expiry =
79	                required(data, "x").toLongOrNull()
80	                    ?: throw ProtocolException("lifecycle payload 'x' is not a number")
81	
82	            return LifecyclePushData(
83	                kind = kind,
84	                eventId = Ids.requireOpaque16(required(data, "i"), "lifecycle.i"),
85	                workspaceId = Ids.requireOpaque16(required(data, "w"), "lifecycle.w"),
86	                expiresAtMs = expiry,
87	            )
88	        }
89	
90	        private fun required(data: Map<String, String>, key: String): String =
91	            PushEnvelope.required(data, key, LABEL)
92	    }
93	}
94	
95	/**
96	 * What arrived over FCM, once `v` has decided which closed key set applies.
97	 *
98	 * Version dispatch happens here and nowhere else, so adding a version can never loosen
99	 * the validation of an existing one: each parser still refuses every key it does not own.
100	 */
101	sealed interface CompanionPush {
102	
103	    /** A question is pending, or one was retracted. The answerable path (§13.1). */
104	    data class Blocked(val data: PushData) : CompanionPush
105	
106	    /** An agent finished or failed. Read-only on every surface (§13.4). */
107	    data class Lifecycle(val data: LifecyclePushData) : CompanionPush
108	
109	    companion object {
110	        /**
111	         * @return `null` for a payload version this build does not implement. That is the
112	         *   forward-compatibility hinge in the other direction: a newer bridge can add a
113	         *   `v` and this build ignores it instead of guessing what it meant.
114	         */
115	        fun parse(data: Map<String, String>): CompanionPush? =
116	            when (PushEnvelope.version(data)) {
117	                PushData.VERSION -> PushData.parse(data)?.let { Blocked(it) }
118	                LifecyclePushData.VERSION -> LifecyclePushData.parse(data)?.let { Lifecycle(it) }
119	                else -> null
120	            }
121	    }
122	}

2	
3	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.ProtocolException
4	
5	/**
6	 * The envelope rules every FCM payload version shares: a closed key set, and values that
7	 * no natural-language string can satisfy.
8	 *
9	 * Shared between [PushData] (§13.1) and [LifecyclePushData] (§13.4) deliberately. These
10	 * are the checks that catch a text leak, and a leak does not announce which version it
11	 * arrived on — a second copy of them is a second chance to weaken one. Each version still
12	 * owns its own key set, its own kinds and its own field parsing; only the envelope is
13	 * common, and every message still names the version that refused the payload.
14	 */
15	internal object PushEnvelope {
16	
17	    private val SAFE_VALUE = Regex("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,43}$")
18	
19	    /** @throws ProtocolException when there is no `v` at all, which is a bridge bug. */
20	    fun version(data: Map<String, String>): String =
21	        data["v"] ?: throw ProtocolException("push payload has no 'v'")
22	
23	    /**
24	     * @param keys everything this version is allowed to carry. Anything else is refused.
25	     * @param label how the version names itself in an error, e.g. `"lifecycle payload"`.
26	     * @param section the PROTOCOL.md section that closes [keys], quoted in the error.
27	     */
28	    fun requireClosedAndOpaque(
29	        data: Map<String, String>,
30	        keys: Set<String>,
31	        label: String,
32	        section: String,
33	    ) {
34	        val unexpected = data.keys - keys
35	        if (unexpected.isNotEmpty()) {
36	            throw ProtocolException(
37	                "$label carries unexpected key(s) $unexpected — the key set is closed by " +
38	                    "PROTOCOL.md $section and an addition is how a text leak would arrive",
39	            )
40	        }
41	        for ((key, value) in data) {
42	            if (!SAFE_VALUE.matches(value)) {
43	                throw ProtocolException(
44	                    "$label key '$key' does not match the opaque-value pattern; " +
45	                        "no natural-language string can, so this is a leak or a bug",
46	                )
47	            }
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    fun required(data: Map<String, String>, key: String, label: String): String =
52	        data[key] ?: throw ProtocolException("$label has no '$key'")
53	}

1	package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol
2	
3	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.ProtocolException
4	
5	/** `k` in the push payload. */
6	enum class PushKind(val wire: String) {
7	    /** A question is pending and nobody has dealt with it. */
8	    QUESTION("q"),
9	
10	    /** Retraction — the question resolved somewhere. Cancel the notification. */
11	    RETRACT("r"),
12	    ;
13	
14	    companion object {
15	        fun fromWire(raw: String): PushKind? = entries.firstOrNull { it.wire == raw }
16	    }
17	}
18	
19	/**
20	 * An FCM data-only message (PROTOCOL.md §13.1).
21	 *
22	 * > **No question text, no option text, no workspace name, no branch name, no project
23	 * > name, no file path, and no free text of any kind may ever appear in an FCM message.**
24	 *
25	 * Google is not in the trust boundary. The bridge asserts that at runtime; this class
26	 * asserts it again on arrival, because a client that quietly accepted an extra key would
27	 * make a future leak invisible. Every value must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,43}$`, which no
28	 * natural-language string can satisfy.
29	 *
30	 * Consequently a push carries **nothing displayable**. The client fetches `/v1/question`
31	 * over the sealed channel and only then renders a notification; if it cannot fetch —
32	 * offline, locked, revoked — it shows a contentless "an agent needs you". It never
33	 * invents text.
34	 */
35	class PushData private constructor(
36	    val kind: PushKind,
37	    val questionId: String,
38	    val workspaceId: String,
39	    val questionCount: Int,
40	    val expiresAtMs: Long,
41	) {
42	    fun isExpired(nowMs: Long): Boolean = nowMs >= expiresAtMs
43	
44	    override fun toString(): String =
45	        "PushData(kind=${kind.wire}, questionId=$questionId, workspaceId=$workspaceId, n=$questionCount)"
46	
47	    companion object {
48	        /**
49	         * The question payload version. Lifecycle alerts are a separate closed key set
50	         * under [LifecyclePushData.VERSION]; this parser owns v1 and refuses everything
51	         * that is not exactly v1's shape.
52	         */
53	        const val VERSION = "1"
54	
55	        private const val LABEL = "push payload"
56	        private val KEYS = setOf("v", "k", "i", "w", "n", "x")
57	
58	        /**
59	         * @return `null` when `v` is a payload version this build does not implement —
60	         *   the caller shows the contentless notification and moves on, which is the
61	         *   documented degradation. Anything else malformed is a hard error, because it
62	         *   means either a bridge bug or an attempt to smuggle content through Google.
63	         */
64	        fun parse(data: Map<String, String>): PushData? {
65	            if (PushEnvelope.version(data) != VERSION) return null
66	            PushEnvelope.requireClosedAndOpaque(data, KEYS, LABEL, "§13.1")
67	
68	            val kind =
69	                PushKind.fromWire(required(data, "k"))
70	                    ?: throw ProtocolException("push payload 'k' is not a known kind")
71	            val count =
72	                required(data, "n").toIntOrNull()
73	                    ?: throw ProtocolException("push payload 'n' is not a number")
74	            val expiry =
75	                required(data, "x").toLongOrNull()
76	                    ?: throw ProtocolException("push payload 'x' is not a number")
77	
78	            return PushData(
79	                kind = kind,
80	                questionId = Ids.requireOpaque16(required(data, "i"), "push.i"),
81	                workspaceId = Ids.requireOpaque16(required(data, "w"), "push.w"),
82	                questionCount = count,
83	                expiresAtMs = expiry,
84	            )
85	        }
86	
87	        private fun required(data: Map<String, String>, key: String): String =
88	            PushEnvelope.required(data, key, LABEL)
89	    }
90	}

1	package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.push

3	import android.util.Log
4	import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService
5	import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage
6	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.ProtocolException
7	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.CompanionPush
8	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.LifecyclePushData
9	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.PushData
10	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchActorSurface
11	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchResolutionOutcome
12	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.di.CompanionContainer
13	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.model.FetchResult
14	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.model.QuestionState
15	import kotlinx.coroutines.TimeoutCancellationException
16	import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
17	import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeout
18	
19	/**
20	 * Receives the wake-up push for a blocked agent.
21	 *
22	 * The payload carries OPAQUE IDS ONLY — no question text, no option text, no workspace
23	 * names. Nothing about what an agent asked may ever reach Google. The real content is
24	 * fetched from the bridge over the sealed channel once this wakes the app, and if that
25	 * fetch cannot happen the notification is posted **contentless**. This service never
26	 * invents text and never renders anything that arrived through FCM.
27	 *
28	 * A push here also means something specific: *nobody has dealt with this*. The bridge
29	 * gates on presence (§13.2) — it holds the push while it believes you are at the desk and
30	 * sends it when it believes you are away — so reds answered at the keyboard, most of them,
31	 * never reach this class at all. That is the only reason a watch buzz stays meaningful.
32	 * The gating is entirely the bridge's; this client applies no delay of its own.
33	 */
34	class CompanionMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService() {
35	
36	    private val container: CompanionContainer by lazy {
37	        CompanionContainer.get(applicationContext)
38	    }
39	
40	    /**
41	     * Trigger (c): Firebase rotated this phone's token.
42	     *
43	     * Always necessary, never sufficient — a token minted before pairing (the ordinary
44	     * case, since Firebase mints one on first launch and the QR is scanned minutes later)
45	     * produces no second `onNewToken`, so this callback alone could never register it. The
46	     * pairing-success and foreground triggers cover that; this one covers rotation.
47	     */
48	    override fun onNewToken(token: String) {
49	        // The token value itself is never recorded — only that there is one.
50	        container.pushDiagnostics.recordTokenAcquired(System.currentTimeMillis())
51	        runBlocking {
52	            try {
53	                withTimeout(WORK_TIMEOUT_MS) { container.pushRegistrar.onNewToken(token) }
54	            } catch (e: TimeoutCancellationException) {
55	                // (ROTATION-RETRY-FLOOR) Logging is all this catch has to do, but only
56	                // because the registrar guarantees the retry. A timeout CANCELS the
57	                // coroutine rather than returning, so nothing inside `onNewToken` past the
58	                // suspension point runs — including its own RETRY branch — and this catch
59	                // sits outside the mutex and outside the pairing check, so it is the wrong
60	                // place to queue one. `PushRegistrar.onNewToken` queues it from a `finally`
61	                // that does run while cancelled. Remove that and a rotated token is
62	                // silently dropped again, which is a phone that stops being wakeable.
63	                Log.e(TAG, "FCM token registration timed out; a retry is queued", e)
64	            }
65	        }
66	    }
67	
68	    override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) {
69	        val push = parse(message)
70	        if (push == null) {
71	            // Recorded, not just logged: a bridge that sends malformed or notification-bearing
72	            // pushes is silent-from-the-pocket in exactly the same way as a denied permission.
73	            container.pushDiagnostics.recordPushRefused(
74	                System.currentTimeMillis(),
75	                "malformed or notification-bearing payload — see logcat $TAG",
76	            )
77	            return
78	        }
79	        when (push) {
80	            is CompanionPush.Blocked -> onBlocked(push.data)
81	            is CompanionPush.Lifecycle -> onLifecycle(push.data)
82	        }
83	    }
84	
85	    private fun onBlocked(push: PushData) {
86	        container.pushDiagnostics.recordPushReceived(
87	            System.currentTimeMillis(),
88	            push.kind.name.lowercase(),
89	        )
90	        // (PUSH-ROUTING) The decision is `routePush`, which is testable; everything below
91	        // needs a Context or a coroutine and stays here behind the surface.
92	        val route = routePush(push, System.currentTimeMillis(), surface)
93	        if (route == PushRoute.EXPIRED) {
94	            // A push that outlived its window describes a moment that has passed. Showing
95	            // it would be worse than showing nothing: the user would walk to the desk for
96	            // a question that is fifteen minutes stale.
97	            Log.i(TAG, "dropping expired push for ${push.questionId}")
98	        }
99	    }
100	
101	    private fun onLifecycle(push: LifecyclePushData) {
102	        container.pushDiagnostics.recordPushReceived(
103	            System.currentTimeMillis(),
104	            push.kind.name.lowercase(),
105	        )
106	        // (LIFECYCLE-ROUTING) Same split as the question path: the decision is testable,
107	        // the notification manager and the Data Layer send stay behind the surface.
108	        val route = routeLifecyclePush(
109	            push = push,
110	            nowMs = System.currentTimeMillis(),
111	            gate = container.seenLifecycleEvents,
112	            surface = lifecycleSurface,
113	        )
114	        when (route) {
115	            // "An agent finished" is only true of a moment; an expired one describes a
116	            // workspace the user has probably already looked at.
117	            LifecycleRoute.EXPIRED -> Log.i(TAG, "dropping expired lifecycle push ${push.eventId}")
118	            // FCM is at-least-once. A second buzz for one event is the reason a whole
119	            // alert class gets muted, so it is dropped here rather than deduped by the
120	            // notification tag, which would still vibrate.
121	            LifecycleRoute.DUPLICATE -> Log.i(TAG, "already alerted for ${push.eventId}")
122	            LifecycleRoute.ALERTED -> Unit
123	        }
124	    }
125	
126	    private val surface = object : PushSurface {
127	
128	        override fun retractNotification(questionId: String) {
129	            container.notifications.retract(questionId)
130	        }
131	
132	        override fun tellWatchResolved(questionId: String) {
133	            // The watch has no independent route to the desktop, so this message is the
134	            // only way its screen and its own notification learn the question is over.
135	            // Provenance is genuinely unknown here — a retract push says a question
136	            // stopped being answerable, not who ended it — and it is reported as
137	            // unknown rather than guessed.
138	            pushToWatch("retract $questionId") {
139	                container.watchBridge.pushResolved(
140	                    questionId = questionId,
141	                    resolvedAtMs = null,
142	                    resolvedBySurface = WatchActorSurface.UNKNOWN,
143	                    resolvedByLabel = null,
144	                    outcome = WatchResolutionOutcome.UNKNOWN,
145	                )
146	            }
147	        }
148	
149	        override fun deliverQuestion(push: PushData) = postQuestion(push)
150	    }
151	
152	    private val lifecycleSurface = object : LifecyclePushSurface {
153	
154	        /**
155	         * The phone's own notification is `setLocalOnly`, so the Data Layer send is the
156	         * only way the wrist hears about it — and it is a send the watch renders itself,
157	         * in wording written for a watch, instead of a truncated bridged copy.
158	         */
159	        override fun post(push: LifecyclePushData) {
160	            container.notifications.postLifecycle(push)
161	            pushToWatch("lifecycle ${push.eventId}") {
162	                container.watchBridge.pushLifecycle(push, System.currentTimeMillis())
163	            }
164	        }
165	    }
166	
167	    /**
168	     * Parsing is where a text leak would be caught, so it is deliberately strict: the key
169	     * set is closed and every value must match an opaque-id pattern that no
170	     * natural-language string can satisfy (PROTOCOL §13.1 for questions, §13.4 for
171	     * lifecycle alerts; `CompanionPush.parse` dispatches on `v` and each version's parser
172	     * refuses every key it does not own).
173	     *
174	     * A violation is logged at ERROR and the push is dropped. It is *not* rethrown, and
175	     * that is a considered trade-off rather than a softened failure: this callback runs
176	     * inside FCM's delivery path, so throwing would crash the process on every redelivery
177	     * of the same message — turning one malformed payload into a permanent crash loop that
178	     * an attacker, or a bridge bug, could hold the app in. Dropping loudly keeps the
179	     * failure visible without handing anyone a remote kill switch.
180	     */
181	    private fun parse(message: RemoteMessage): CompanionPush? {
182	        if (message.notification != null) {
183	            // The bridge must send data-only messages. A `notification` block means text
184	            // came through Google's infrastructure, which is the exact property the
185	            // payload format exists to make impossible.
186	            Log.e(
187	                TAG,
188	                "REFUSING push carrying a notification block — the bridge must send " +
189	                    "data-only messages; text must never traverse FCM",
190	            )
191	            return null
192	        }
193	        return try {
194	            CompanionPush.parse(message.data)
195	        } catch (e: ProtocolException) {
196	            Log.e(TAG, "REFUSING malformed push payload: ${e.message}", e)
197	            null
198	        }
199	    }
200	
201	    private fun postQuestion(push: PushData) {
202	        val detail = runBlocking {
203	            try {
204	                withTimeout(WORK_TIMEOUT_MS) {
205	                    container.repository.loadQuestion(push.questionId)
206	                }
207	            } catch (e: TimeoutCancellationException) {
208	                Log.w(TAG, "question fetch timed out for ${push.questionId}", e)
209	                null
210	            }
211	        }
212	
213	        when (detail) {
214	            is FetchResult.Success -> {
215	                val question = detail.value
216	                if (question.state != QuestionState.PENDING) {
217	                    // It resolved between the bridge arming the push and this phone waking
218	                    // up. A notification must never outlive the thing it was about.
219	                    Log.i(TAG, "push for ${push.questionId} arrived already ${question.state}")
220	                    container.notifications.retract(push.questionId)
221	                    pushToWatch("resolved ${push.questionId}") {
222	                        container.watchBridge.pushQuestionById(push.questionId)
223	                    }
224	                    return
225	                }
226	                container.notifications.postQuestion(question)
227	                // The phone's own notification is setLocalOnly, so it is deliberately NOT
228	                // bridged to the wrist — a bridged copy would be the 1 024-character
229	                // truncation this product exists to avoid. The Data Layer carries the full
230	                // question instead, and this is where that starts.
231	                pushToWatch("question ${push.questionId}") {
232	                    container.watchBridge.pushQuestion(question)
233	                }
234	            }
235	
236	            is FetchResult.Failure -> {
237	                // Offline, revoked, or the desktop went away between arming and delivery.
238	                // The user still learns that something is blocked; they just have to open
239	                // the app to find out what. Inventing a headline here would be a lie.
240	                Log.w(TAG, "could not fetch ${push.questionId}: ${detail.error.message}")
241	                container.notifications.postContentless(push.questionId, push.questionCount)
242	                warnWatchNotToldOf(push.questionId)
243	            }
244	
245	            null -> {
246	                container.notifications.postContentless(push.questionId, push.questionCount)
247	                warnWatchNotToldOf(push.questionId)
248	            }
249	        }
250	    }
251	
252	    /**
253	     * Runs one bounded Data Layer push.
254	     *
255	     * Blocking, like the rest of this service: an FCM callback may be torn down as soon as
256	     * it returns, so work launched asynchronously here is work that may never happen. A
257	     * timeout is logged and does not affect the phone's own notification, which is already
258	     * posted — the wrist is a second surface, never a precondition for the first.
259	     */
260	    private fun pushToWatch(what: String, block: suspend () -> Unit) {
261	        runBlocking {
262	            try {
263	                withTimeout(WATCH_TIMEOUT_MS) { block() }
264	            } catch (e: TimeoutCancellationException) {
265	                Log.w(TAG, "watch push timed out: $what", e)
266	            }
267	        }
268	    }
269	
270	    /**
271	     * A contentless push means this phone could not fetch the body, and the Data Layer
272	     * contract has no contentless question — inventing one would be a message the watch
273	     * cannot decode. The watch catches up on its next foreground `hello`, which asks for
274	     * whatever is still pending. Logged so the gap is visible rather than assumed.
275	     */
276	    private fun warnWatchNotToldOf(questionId: String) {
277	        Log.w(TAG, "no body for $questionId, so the watch was not told; it will ask on next hello")
278	    }
279	
280	    private companion object {
281	        const val TAG = "CompanionPush"
282	
283	        /**
284	         * FCM allows roughly 20 s of work in this callback before it stops holding a
285	         * wakelock. Staying well inside that keeps the fetch from being killed mid-flight
286	         * and leaving neither a notification nor a log line.
287	         */
288	        const val WORK_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000L
289	
290	        /**
291	         * A Data Layer hop to a watch that may be asleep on the wrist. Play Services'
292	         * own send timeout is 10 s (see `WatchLink`); this bounds the whole push.
293	         */
294	        const val WATCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000L
295	    }
296	}
