package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.push

import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.LifecyclePushData

/**
 * (LIFECYCLE-ROUTING) What a parsed lifecycle push turns into, decided away from the
 * Android service — the same split, and for the same reason, as [routePush].
 *
 * Lifecycle alerts are routed here rather than in [routePush] on purpose. The question
 * path has behaviour a lifecycle alert must never inherit: it fetches the question body,
 * it retracts, it feeds the watch's answer screen. An alert that said "an agent finished"
 * and then offered an answer button would be lying about what tapping it does.
 */
interface LifecyclePushSurface {

    /**
     * Post the fixed alert for [LifecyclePushData.kind], and mirror it to the watch.
     *
     * One entry point rather than one per kind: the wording, the channel and the priority
     * are all a function of the kind, and the mapping lives with the notification builder
     * on each device rather than being spelled out again here.
     */
    fun post(push: LifecyclePushData)
}

/**
 * Remembers which events have already alerted.
 *
 * FCM delivers at-least-once, and the bridge may re-send after a reconnect, so without
 * this the same finished agent can buzz twice. Twice is worse than it sounds: the second
 * buzz carries no new information, and an alert class that buzzes for nothing is the one
 * the user turns off.
 */
interface LifecycleAlertGate {

    /**
     * @return `true` the first time this `eventId` is seen and `false` every time after,
     *   so the caller alerts exactly once per event.
     */
    fun admit(eventId: String): Boolean
}

/** What [routeLifecyclePush] did, so a caller can log it and a test can assert it. */
enum class LifecycleRoute {
    /** Past its expiry on arrival. A stale "finished" is noise; dropped. */
    EXPIRED,

    /** Already alerted for this event. Dropped without a second buzz. */
    DUPLICATE,

    /** Alerted on the phone and mirrored to the watch. */
    ALERTED,
}

/**
 * Route one parsed lifecycle push: expiry, then dedupe, then post.
 *
 * Dedupe deliberately sits AFTER expiry — a duplicate of an expired event must not consume
 * the one alert its event was entitled to, or a redelivery that arrives in time behind a
 * late one would be swallowed.
 */
fun routeLifecyclePush(
    push: LifecyclePushData,
    nowMs: Long,
    gate: LifecycleAlertGate,
    surface: LifecyclePushSurface,
): LifecycleRoute {
    if (push.isExpired(nowMs)) return LifecycleRoute.EXPIRED
    if (!gate.admit(push.eventId)) return LifecycleRoute.DUPLICATE

    surface.post(push)
    return LifecycleRoute.ALERTED
}

1	package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.notifications
2	
3	import android.content.Context
4	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.push.LifecycleAlertGate
5	
6	/**
7	 * The store behind [SeenLifecycleEvents], split out so the ring logic is testable off
8	 * device. One small file of ids; no migration story worth having.
9	 */
10	interface SeenEventStore {
11	
12	    /** Oldest first. */
13	    fun read(): List<String>
14	
15	    fun write(eventIds: List<String>)
16	}
17	
18	/**
19	 * (LIFECYCLE-DEDUPE) One alert per event, across process death.
20	 *
21	 * In-memory would have been enough for FCM's own retries within a session and wrong
22	 * everywhere else: [family.khaira.supersetcompanion.push.CompanionMessagingService] is
23	 * constructed per message, and a phone that was dozing gets its process killed between
24	 * the first delivery and the redelivery. The buzz that survives a restart is exactly the
25	 * one the user would call a bug.
26	 *
27	 * Bounded to [CAPACITY] ids, oldest evicted first. An unbounded list would grow with every
28	 * agent run for the life of the install, and the alerts worth deduping are recent by
29	 * construction — an event id that fell off the end is one whose notification the user
30	 * dealt with days ago.
31	 */
32	class SeenLifecycleEvents(
33	    private val store: SeenEventStore,
34	    private val capacity: Int = CAPACITY,
35	) : LifecycleAlertGate {
36	
37	    init {
38	        require(capacity > 0) { "a dedupe window of $capacity events remembers nothing" }
39	    }
40	
41	    @Synchronized
42	    override fun admit(eventId: String): Boolean {
43	        val seen = store.read()
44	        if (eventId in seen) return false
45	        store.write((seen + eventId).takeLast(capacity))
46	        return true
47	    }
48	
49	    companion object {
50	        /** Days of alerts on a busy machine, and a few hundred bytes on disk. */
51	        const val CAPACITY = 64
52	    }
53	}
54	
55	/** The on-disk implementation. */
56	class SharedPreferencesSeenEventStore(context: Context) : SeenEventStore {
57	
58	    private val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences(FILE, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
59	
60	    override fun read(): List<String> =
61	        prefs.getString(KEY_EVENT_IDS, null)
62	            ?.split(SEPARATOR)
63	            ?.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
64	            ?: emptyList()
65	
66	    override fun write(eventIds: List<String>) {
67	        // commit(), not apply(): this runs on FCM's delivery thread and the process is
68	        // routinely killed moments after onMessageReceived returns. An apply() that had
69	        // not reached disk would lose exactly the record the redelivery is checked
70	        // against — the buzz-twice bug this store exists to prevent.
71	        prefs.edit().putString(KEY_EVENT_IDS, eventIds.joinToString(SEPARATOR)).commit()
72	    }
73	
74	    private companion object {
75	        const val FILE = "companion_lifecycle_alerts"
76	        const val KEY_EVENT_IDS = "seen_event_ids"
77	
78	        /**
79	         * Safe as a separator because event ids are base64url — the character set that
80	         * [family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.Ids.requireOpaque16] enforces
81	         * excludes it, so no id can ever split itself in two.
82	         */
83	        const val SEPARATOR = ","
84	    }
85	}

1	package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.notifications
2	
3	import android.Manifest
4	import android.app.Notification
5	import android.app.NotificationChannel
6	import android.app.NotificationManager
7	import android.app.PendingIntent
8	import android.content.Context
9	import android.content.Intent
10	import android.content.pm.PackageManager
11	import android.util.Log
12	import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat
13	import androidx.core.content.ContextCompat
14	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.MainActivity
15	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.R
16	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.LifecycleKind
17	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol.LifecyclePushData
18	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.phone.model.QuestionDetail
19	import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
20	import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
21	import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow
22	
23	/**
24	 * Every notification this app posts, and — more importantly — every one it takes away.
25	 *
26	 * A notification must never outlive the thing it was about. Retraction over FCM is
27	 * best-effort (a dozing phone misses it), so [sweep] runs a full reconciliation against
28	 * the desktop's own list on **every** foreground. That is not belt-and-braces: the
29	 * likeliest stale buzz in real use comes from exactly the dozing case the push cannot
30	 * reach.
31	 *
32	 * Nothing here invents text. The push payload carries opaque ids only — no question text,
33	 * no option text, no workspace or branch name ever reaches Google — so when the question
34	 * body cannot be fetched over the sealed channel this posts a *contentless* notification
35	 * rather than a plausible-looking one.
36	 */
37	class CompanionNotifications(private val context: Context) : LostContactSurface {
38	
39	    private val manager: NotificationManager =
40	        context.getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java)
41	            ?: error("NotificationManager unavailable — the platform contract guarantees it")
42	
43	    private val deliveryState = MutableStateFlow(readDelivery())
44	
45	    /**
46	     * Whether a blocked-agent notification would actually reach the user right now.
47	     *
48	     * Android gives no callback when the permission is revoked or the channel is muted from
49	     * system settings, so this is a poll: [refreshDelivery] runs on every foreground and
50	     * after every attempt to post. That is enough — the states it reports can only be
51	     * changed by the user leaving the app to change them.
52	     */
53	    val delivery: StateFlow<NotificationDelivery> = deliveryState.asStateFlow()
54	
55	    fun refreshDelivery() {
56	        deliveryState.value = readDelivery()
57	    }
58	
59	    private fun readDelivery(): NotificationDelivery {
60	        val channel = manager.getNotificationChannel(CHANNEL_QUESTIONS)
61	        return NotificationDelivery(
62	            permissionGranted = canPost(),
63	            appEnabled = manager.areNotificationsEnabled(),
64	            questionsChannelImportance = channel?.importance,
65	        )
66	    }
67	
68	    fun ensureChannels() {
69	        manager.createNotificationChannel(
70	            NotificationChannel(
71	                CHANNEL_QUESTIONS,
72	                "Blocked agents",
73	                NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_HIGH,
74	            ).apply {
75	                description =
76	                    "An agent is blocked and you were not at the desk to see it. These are " +
77	                    "the only notifications that can be answered from the phone."
78	                enableVibration(true)
79	                setShowBadge(true)
80	            },
81	        )
82	        manager.createNotificationChannel(
83	            NotificationChannel(
84	                CHANNEL_READY,
85	                "Ready for review",
86	                NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT,
87	            ).apply {
88	                description =
89	                    "An agent finished and its work is waiting for you. Nothing is blocked, " +
90	                    "so this does not vibrate — turn it off here if you would rather find " +
91	                    "finished work yourself."
92	                enableVibration(false)
93	                setShowBadge(true)
94	            },
95	        )
96	        manager.createNotificationChannel(
97	            NotificationChannel(
98	                CHANNEL_ERROR,
99	                "Agent errors",
100	                NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_HIGH,
101	            ).apply {
102	                description =
103	                    "An agent stopped on an error. Nothing is blocked on an answer either — " +
104	                    "it simply will not continue on its own."
105	                enableVibration(true)
106	                setShowBadge(true)
107	            },
108	        )
109	        manager.createNotificationChannel(
110	            NotificationChannel(
111	                CHANNEL_LIVENESS,
112	                "Lost contact",
113	                NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT,
114	            ).apply {
115	                description =
116	                    "The desktop stopped answering while agents were still running. Raised " +
117	                    "locally by this phone, not by the desktop — which is the point."
118	                setShowBadge(false)
119	            },
120	        )
121	        // The first read happened before the channels existed; without this the app would
122	        // report its own "channel missing" fault for the lifetime of the process.
123	        refreshDelivery()
124	    }
125	
126	    /** True when this app holds `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. See [delivery] for whether it lands. */
127	    fun canPost(): Boolean =
128	        ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS) ==
129	            PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
130	
131	    /**
132	     * Posts a question the phone has successfully fetched. The text here came over the
133	     * sealed channel, never through Google.
134	     */
135	    fun postQuestion(detail: QuestionDetail) {
136	        val first = detail.questions.firstOrNull()
137	            ?: error("question ${detail.questionId} has no items — the bridge must not send that")
138	        val title = first.header.ifBlank { "An agent needs you" }
139	        val body = if (detail.isMultiPart) {
140	            "${detail.questions.size} questions · tap to answer"
141	        } else {
142	            first.question
143	        }
144	        post(
145	            questionId = detail.questionId,
146	            title = title,
147	            body = body,
148	            answerable = detail.answerable,
149	        )
150	    }
151	
152	    /**
153	     * Posts when the question body could not be fetched — offline, revoked, rate-limited.
154	     * Contentless on purpose: inventing a summary from an opaque id would be a lie, and
155	     * the id is genuinely all we have.
156	     */
157	    fun postContentless(questionId: String, questionCount: Int) {
158	        post(
159	            questionId = questionId,
160	            title = "An agent needs you",
161	            body = if (questionCount > 1) {
162	                "$questionCount questions waiting — open to read them"
163	            } else {
164	                "Open to read the question"
165	            },
166	            answerable = true,
167	        )
168	    }
169	
170	    /**
171	     * (LIFECYCLE-ALERT) An agent finished, or stopped on an error. Fixed wording, chosen
172	     * locally and driven only by [LifecyclePushData.kind].
173	     *
174	     * There is nothing to fetch and nothing to fetch it with: a lifecycle push carries
175	     * opaque ids only, and unlike a question there is no body endpoint that would make
176	     * the text more specific. So the phone says the one true thing it knows and lets the
177	     * app say the rest. The tap opens the app at home — not a question, because there is
178	     * no question, and an alert whose tap lands somewhere unanswerable teaches the user
179	     * to stop tapping.
180	     */
181	    fun postLifecycle(push: LifecyclePushData) {
182	        val alert = lifecycleAlert(push.kind)
183	        if (!canPost()) {
184	            refreshDelivery()
185	            Log.w(TAG, "notification permission not granted; ${alert.channelId} alert not posted")
186	            return
187	        }
188	        val notification = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, alert.channelId)
189	            .setSmallIcon(R.drawable.ic_notification)
190	            .setContentTitle(alert.title)
191	            .setContentText(alert.body)
192	            .setContentIntent(openAppIntent(null))
193	            .setCategory(alert.category)
194	            .setPriority(alert.priority)
195	            .setAutoCancel(true)
196	            .setOnlyAlertOnce(true)
197	            // The watch gets its own alert over the Data Layer (WearPaths.LIFECYCLE), with
198	            // wording written for a wrist. Without this the wrist shows both that and a
199	            // bridged copy of this one, for one event.
200	            .setLocalOnly(true)
201	            .build()
202	        // Tagged by the alert id, which is what identifies a lifecycle alert everywhere
203	        // else too — the bridge's collapse_key, the dedupe window, and the watch's own
204	        // notification id. A redelivery updates its own row; a different event is a
205	        // different fact and gets its own.
206	        manager.notify(push.eventId, ID_LIFECYCLE, notification)
207	    }
208	
209	    private fun lifecycleAlert(kind: LifecycleKind): LifecycleAlert = when (kind) {
210	        LifecycleKind.READY -> LifecycleAlert(
211	            channelId = CHANNEL_READY,
212	            title = "An agent finished",
213	            body = "Ready for review — open Superset to look over the work.",
214	            category = Notification.CATEGORY_STATUS,
215	            priority = NotificationCompat.PRIORITY_DEFAULT,
216	        )
217	
218	        LifecycleKind.ERROR -> LifecycleAlert(
219	            channelId = CHANNEL_ERROR,
220	            title = "An agent stopped on an error",
221	            body = "It will not continue on its own — open Superset to see what happened.",
222	            category = Notification.CATEGORY_ERROR,
223	            priority = NotificationCompat.PRIORITY_HIGH,
224	        )
225	    }
226	
227	    /** Everything one lifecycle kind changes about the notification, in one place. */
228	    private class LifecycleAlert(
229	        val channelId: String,
230	        val title: String,
231	        val body: String,
232	        val category: String,
233	        val priority: Int,
234	    )
235	
236	    override fun postLostContact(workingCount: Int, needsInputCount: Int) {
237	        if (!canPost()) {
238	            refreshDelivery()
239	            Log.w(TAG, "notification permission not granted; lost-contact warning not posted")
240	            return
241	        }
242	        val notification = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, CHANNEL_LIVENESS)
243	            .setSmallIcon(R.drawable.ic_notification)
244	            .setContentTitle("Lost contact with the desktop")
245	            .setContentText(
246	                "$needsInputCount waiting, $workingCount working at last contact. " +
247	                    "Agents keep running when Superset closes.",
248	            )
249	            .setStyle(
250	                NotificationCompat.BigTextStyle().bigText(
251	                    "$needsInputCount waiting for an answer and $workingCount working when the " +
252	                        "desktop last answered. The agents keep running under the detached pty " +
253	                        "daemon even though the bridge is gone, so this may need attention at " +
254	                        "the machine.",
255	                ),
256	            )
257	            .setContentIntent(openAppIntent(null))
258	            .setCategory(Notification.CATEGORY_STATUS)
259	            .setAutoCancel(true)
260	            // The watchdog can re-assert lost contact on any diagnostics change while the
261	            // desktop is still gone. Updating the counts in place is right; alerting again
262	            // for the same outage is not.
263	            .setOnlyAlertOnce(true)
264	            .build()
265	        manager.notify(TAG_LIVENESS, ID_LIVENESS, notification)
266	    }
267	
268	    override fun cancelLostContact() = manager.cancel(TAG_LIVENESS, ID_LIVENESS)
269	
270	    /** Retracts one question's notification, from either a push or a local resolution. */
271	    fun retract(questionId: String) {
272	        manager.cancel(questionId, ID_QUESTION)
273	    }
274	
275	    /**
276	     * The full foreground sweep. Cancels every posted question notification that the
277	     * desktop no longer reports as pending.
278	     *
279	     * @param stillPending question ids the desktop currently reports as unanswered.
280	     * @return the ids that were retracted, for logging — a silent sweep would hide a bug
281	     *   in whatever was supposed to have retracted them already.
282	     */
283	    fun sweep(stillPending: Set<String>): List<String> {
284	        val posted = manager.activeNotifications
285	            .filter { it.id == ID_QUESTION }
286	            .mapNotNull { it.tag }
287	        val stale = posted.filterNot { it in stillPending }
288	        stale.forEach { manager.cancel(it, ID_QUESTION) }
289	        if (stale.isNotEmpty()) {
290	            Log.i(TAG, "foreground sweep retracted ${stale.size} stale notification(s): $stale")
291	        }
292	        return stale
293	    }
294	
295	    /** Question ids this phone currently has on screen. */
296	    fun postedQuestionIds(): Set<String> =
297	        manager.activeNotifications
298	            .filter { it.id == ID_QUESTION }
299	            .mapNotNull { it.tag }
300	            .toSet()
301	
302	    private fun post(questionId: String, title: String, body: String, answerable: Boolean) {
303	        if (!canPost()) {
304	            // Loud in the log AND on screen: a dropped question notification is the whole
305	            // product failing, and this is the moment the app learns it is happening.
306	            refreshDelivery()
307	            Log.w(TAG, "notification permission not granted; question $questionId not posted")
308	            return
309	        }
310	        refreshDelivery()
311	        val builder = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, CHANNEL_QUESTIONS)
312	            .setSmallIcon(R.drawable.ic_notification)
313	            .setContentTitle(title)
314	            .setContentText(body.lineSequence().firstOrNull().orEmpty())
315	            .setStyle(NotificationCompat.BigTextStyle().bigText(body))
316	            .setContentIntent(openAppIntent(questionId))
317	            .setCategory(Notification.CATEGORY_MESSAGE)
318	            .setPriority(NotificationCompat.PRIORITY_HIGH)
319	            .setAutoCancel(true)
320	            .setOnlyAlertOnce(true)

341	/** [WatchLifecycleAlert.kind]. */
342	object WatchLifecycleKind {
343	    const val READY = "ready"
344	    const val ERROR = "error"
345	}

347	/**
348	 * An agent finished, or an agent failed (PROTOCOL.md §13.4).
349	 *
350	 * Content-free by construction, exactly like the FCM payload it came from: [eventId] and
351	 * [workspaceId] are opaque and the watch renders fixed local wording. There is no
352	 * headline, no source label and no item list here — not because they would not fit, but
353	 * because a lifecycle alert has nothing to say that the user's own workspace does not
354	 * already say better once they open it.
355	 *
356	 * There is no answer path either. The watch alerts once, on its own channels, and opens
357	 * the app at home when tapped; the question state machine never sees it.
358	 */
359	@Serializable
360	data class WatchLifecycleAlert(
361	    /** [WatchLifecycleKind]. */
362	    val kind: String,
363	    /** Opaque; identity of the alert, used to alert once and to address its notification. */
364	    val eventId: String,
365	    /** Opaque; identity of the workspace the alert is about. */
366	    val workspaceId: String,
367	    val raisedAtMs: Long,
368	    /**
369	     * Carried through from the push (§13.4 `x`), because the wrist needs its own boundary.
370	     *
371	     * The phone checks expiry before it sends, but that answers a question about a
372	     * different moment and a different clock. This hop is best-effort — `MessageClient`
373	     * delivers to a connected node or fails; it does NOT queue for a watch that is out of
374	     * range — yet the watch can still take the message minutes later, because the phone
375	     * only sends after its own wake-up, notification post and Data Layer round trip, and
376	     * the watch may be asleep when it lands. The watch re-checks rather than trusting a
377	     * decision made before the hop.
378	     */
379	    val expiresAtMs: Long,
380	) {
381	    /** Inclusive, matching every other expiry gate in the protocol. */
382	    fun isExpired(nowMs: Long): Boolean = nowMs >= expiresAtMs
383	}

387	 *
388	 * The same `requestId` is reported more than once by design — a §11.5 status read comes back
389	 * on this same path — and a later report may claim LESS than an earlier one. Which reports
390	 * may replace which is [WatchAnswerStatus.supersedes], not arrival order: `confirmed` is
391	 * terminal, `failed` yields only to `confirmed`, and `unconfirmed`/`unknown` yield to
392	 * anything.

422	 * `POST /v1/answer`; [requestId] is minted ONCE by the watch and must never be regenerated
423	 * for the same user action, or PROTOCOL.md §11.4 idempotency stops protecting it.
424	 */

426	data class WatchAnswerIntent(
427	    val questionId: String,
428	    val fingerprint: String,
429	    /** UUIDv4, lowercase, hyphenated. Watch-minted, stable for this attempt. */
430	    val requestId: String,
431	    /** One per item, in ascending `questionIndex` order, ALL of them. */
432	    val answers: List<WatchAnswerItem>,
433	    /**
434	     * The bridge's deliberate-send claim (2026-08-09): `true` whenever [answers] carries a
435	     * `freetext` item, because `POST /v1/answer` hard-requires it there — no biometric
436	     * ceremony backs it on any surface anymore. False on option-only sends. The phone's
437	     * boundary check refuses a free-text intent that arrives without it.
438	     */
439	    val confirmedBiometric: Boolean = false,
440	    val surface: String = "watch",
441	)

443	/**
444	 * Serialises with a `kind` discriminator to match PROTOCOL.md §11.2 exactly.
445	 *
446	 * `select`, `multiselect` and `freetext` all exist since 2026-08-09 — the watch renders
447	 * checkbox rows and takes free text through the system RemoteInput sheet. A build skew
448	 * (old counterpart, new item kind) fails loudly at deserialisation on the unknown
449	 * discriminator; phone and watch APKs ship in lockstep. Adding a member here is a
450	 * protocol change, not a UI change.
451	 */

453	sealed class WatchAnswerItem {
454	    abstract val questionIndex: Int

3	import android.util.Log
4	import com.google.android.gms.wearable.MessageEvent
5	import com.google.android.gms.wearable.WearableListenerService
6	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchAnswerResult
7	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchAnswerStatus
8	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchLifecycleAlert
9	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchQuestion
10	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchQuestionOversize
11	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchQuestionResolved
12	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WearJson
13	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WearPaths
14	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.notify.LifecycleNotifier
15	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.notify.NotificationBridging
16	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.notify.QuestionNotifier
17	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.state.QuestionStore
18	import kotlinx.serialization.SerializationException
19	import kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString
20	
21	private const val TAG = "CompanionWearListener"
22	
23	/**
24	 * The watch's only route to anything. It has no independent path to the desktop, so
25	 * every question and every answer travels through the phone over the Data Layer.
26	 *
27	 * This silently delivers nothing if app-watch and app-phone differ in applicationId or
28	 * signing key — no error, no callback. Both are pinned in the two build files.
29	 *
30	 * Error policy here, deliberate:
31	 *  * An **unknown path** is ignored with a warning. A newer phone build must be able to add
32	 *    a message type without bricking an older watch (PROTOCOL.md §0 forward compatibility).
33	 *  * An **undecodable payload on a known path** throws. That is not forward compatibility,
34	 *    it is the two sides disagreeing about a shape they both claim to implement, and it must
35	 *    be loud rather than producing a watch that quietly shows nothing.
36	 */
37	class CompanionWearListenerService : WearableListenerService() {
38	
39	    override fun onCreate() {
40	        super.onCreate()
41	        // Earliest hook this module owns. Does not cover install -> first launch; see
42	        // NotificationBridging for the two mechanisms that do.
43	        NotificationBridging.applyNoBridging(this)
44	    }
45	
46	    override fun onMessageReceived(event: MessageEvent) {
47	        val json = event.data.toString(Charsets.UTF_8)
48	        when (event.path) {
49	            WearPaths.QUESTION -> onQuestion(decode<WatchQuestion>(event.path, json))
50	            WearPaths.QUESTION_OVERSIZE -> onOversize(decode(event.path, json))
51	            WearPaths.QUESTION_RESOLVED -> onResolved(decode(event.path, json))
52	            WearPaths.ANSWER_RESULT -> onAnswerResult(decode(event.path, json))
53	            WearPaths.CONNECTION -> QuestionStore.onConnection(decode(event.path, json))
54	            WearPaths.LIFECYCLE -> onLifecycle(decode(event.path, json))
55	            else -> Log.w(TAG, "ignoring message on unknown path ${event.path}")
56	        }
57	    }
58	
59	    private fun onQuestion(question: WatchQuestion) {
60	        QuestionStore.onQuestion(question)
61	        val buzzed = QuestionNotifier.notifyQuestion(this, question)
62	        QuestionStore.setNotificationsBlocked(!buzzed)
63	    }
64	
65	    private fun onOversize(info: WatchQuestionOversize) {
66	        QuestionStore.onOversize(info)
67	        val buzzed = QuestionNotifier.notifyOversize(this, info)
68	        QuestionStore.setNotificationsBlocked(!buzzed)
69	    }
70	
71	    private fun onResolved(info: WatchQuestionResolved) {
72	        // A notification must never outlive the thing it was about (PROTOCOL.md §13.3) — cancel
73	        // first, unconditionally, whether or not the question is the one on screen.
74	        QuestionNotifier.cancel(this, info.questionId)
75	        QuestionStore.onResolved(info)
76	    }
77	
78	    private fun onAnswerResult(result: WatchAnswerResult) {
79	        QuestionStore.onAnswerResult(result)
80	        if (result.status == WatchAnswerStatus.CONFIRMED) {
81	            QuestionNotifier.cancel(this, result.questionId)
82	        }
83	    }
84	
85	    /**
86	     * (LIFECYCLE-ALERT) An agent finished or failed.
87	     *
88	     * Expiry is re-checked here rather than trusted from the phone. The phone dropped
89	     * expired pushes on arrival, but that check was made before the hop, on another
90	     * clock, and this watch may have been asleep when the message landed. Nothing is
91	     * queued for a disconnected watch — `MessageClient` drops rather than replays — so
92	     * lateness here is delay, not a backlog, and the wrist still decides for itself.
93	     *
94	     * [QuestionStore] is deliberately untouched. An alert that is not a question must not
95	     * displace one on screen, must not clear a selection the user has made, and must not
96	     * cancel a question notification — all three of which are what routing this through
97	     * the question paths would do.
98	     */
99	    private fun onLifecycle(alert: WatchLifecycleAlert) {
100	        if (alert.isExpired(System.currentTimeMillis())) {
101	            Log.i(TAG, "dropping expired lifecycle alert ${alert.eventId}")
102	            return
103	        }
104	        LifecycleNotifier.notify(this, alert)
105	    }
106	
107	    private inline fun <reified T> decode(path: String, json: String): T =
108	        try {
109	            WearJson.decodeFromString<T>(json)
110	        } catch (e: SerializationException) {
111	            throw IllegalArgumentException(
112	                "undecodable ${T::class.java.simpleName} on $path (${json.length} chars)",
113	                e,
114	            )
115	        }
116	}

package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear.notify

import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.wear.WatchLifecycleKind

/**
 * Everything a lifecycle alert says on the wrist, with no Android in it.
 *
 * Split from [LifecycleNotifier] so the wording, the channel split and the alert identity
 * can be asserted in a JVM test. The parts that need a Context — creating the channel,
 * posting, the PendingIntent — stay in the notifier, where a test could not reach them
 * anyway.
 */
data class LifecycleAlertText(
    val channelId: String,
    val channelName: String,
    val channelDescription: String,
    val title: String,
    val text: String,
    val vibrates: Boolean,
)

object LifecycleAlertPresentation {

    const val CHANNEL_READY = "companion.ready"
    const val CHANNEL_ERROR = "companion.errors"

    /**
     * Fixed local wording. The alert arrived carrying opaque ids only, so there is nothing
     * to interpolate and nothing to fetch: a lifecycle alert never has a headline the way
     * a question does.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException for a kind this build does not know — the same
     *   treatment an undecodable message gets in [family.khaira.supersetcompanion.wear
     *   .datalayer.CompanionWearListenerService], because both mean the phone app and the
     *   watch app are different versions and guessing would put wrong words on the wrist.
     */
    fun forKind(kind: String): LifecycleAlertText = when (kind) {
        WatchLifecycleKind.READY -> LifecycleAlertText(
            channelId = CHANNEL_READY,
            channelName = "Ready for review",
            channelDescription = "An agent finished. Nothing is blocked, so this does not buzz.",
            title = "An agent finished",
            text = "Ready for review",
            // A finished agent is not urgent: it will still be finished in an hour. The
            // buzz is reserved for things that are waiting on the user.
            vibrates = false,
        )

        WatchLifecycleKind.ERROR -> LifecycleAlertText(
            channelId = CHANNEL_ERROR,
            channelName = "Agent errors",
            channelDescription = "An agent stopped on an error and will not continue by itself.",
            title = "An agent stopped",
            text = "It hit an error",
            vibrates = true,
        )

        else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("unknown lifecycle kind '$kind'")
    }

    /**
     * The alert id is the identity on the wrist too — the same value the phone tags its
     * own notification with and the same one the bridge collapses on, so one event is one
     * row wherever it is shown, and a redelivery updates that row rather than adding one.
     *
     * The `lifecycle:` prefix keeps these out of [QuestionNotifier]'s id space, which is a
     * bare `questionId.hashCode()`.
     */
    fun notificationId(eventId: String): Int = "lifecycle:$eventId".hashCode()
}

1	package family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.protocol
2	
3	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.CompanionConstants
4	import family.khaira.supersetcompanion.core.ProtocolException
5	import java.security.SecureRandom
6	import java.util.UUID
7	
8	/**
9	 * Ids are **opaque bridge-minted handles** (PROTOCOL.md §0.1). The desktop's internal
10	 * identifiers — `tool_use_id`, `session_id`, transcript paths, the pty session handle —
11	 * are never sent to a client, and a client cannot construct a valid id it was not given.
12	 *
13	 * These validators exist so a malformed id fails at the boundary with a name attached,
14	 * rather than three layers later as a mysterious 400.
15	 */
16	object Ids {
17	    private val BASE64URL = Regex("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
18	    private val UUID_V4_LOWERCASE =
19	        Regex("^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")
20	
21	    /** A 16-byte opaque id: `deviceId`, `questionId`, `fingerprint`, `leaseId`, `projectId`, ... */
22	    fun requireOpaque16(value: String, field: String): String =
23	        requireOpaque(value, CompanionConstants.ID_CHARS_16B, field)
24	
25	    /** A 12-byte opaque id: `eventId`. */
26	    fun requireOpaque12(value: String, field: String): String =
27	        requireOpaque(value, CompanionConstants.ID_CHARS_12B, field)
28	
29	    /** A 32-byte opaque id: `ticket`. */
30	    fun requireOpaque32(value: String, field: String): String =
31	        requireOpaque(value, CompanionConstants.ID_CHARS_32B, field)
32	
33	    fun requireOpaque(value: String, chars: Int, field: String): String {
34	        if (value.length != chars) {
35	            throw ProtocolException("$field: expected $chars characters, got ${value.length}")
36	        }
37	        if (!BASE64URL.matches(value)) {
38	            throw ProtocolException("$field: not base64url-unpadded")
39	        }
40	        return value
41	    }
42	
43	    /** `requestId` is a client-minted UUIDv4, lowercase, hyphenated (§0.1). */
44	    fun requireRequestId(value: String, field: String = "requestId"): String {
45	        if (value.length != CompanionConstants.REQUEST_ID_CHARS || !UUID_V4_LOWERCASE.matches(value)) {
46	            throw ProtocolException("$field: must be a lowercase hyphenated UUIDv4")
47	        }
48	        return value
49	    }
50	
51	    /**
52	     * Mint the idempotency key for one write attempt.
53	     *
54	     * It must stay **stable for that attempt** and must never be regenerated as part of
55	     * a retry — there are no write retries (§11.4), and a fresh id would defeat the
56	     * bridge's idempotency record even if there were.
57	     */
58	    fun newRequestId(): String = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
59	
60	    /** 16 CSPRNG bytes. `SecureRandom` only — never `java.util.Random` (§15.1). */
61	    fun randomDeviceIdBytes(): ByteArray {
62	        val bytes = ByteArray(CompanionConstants.DEVICE_ID_BYTES)
63	        SecureRandom().nextBytes(bytes)
64	        return bytes
65	    }
66	}

name: Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)

# Self-repairing build of the vendored fork source at repo root.
# The build steps themselves are deterministic and live in
# .github/actions/arm64-build (thin shims over scripts/) — this file only
# orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop:
#
#   build-attempt-1 ──fail──> repair-1 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-2
#                                   ──fail──> repair-2 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-3
#
# Max 3 build attempts / 2 AI repairs, then verdict fails LOUD. Every repair
# is pushed to the repair branch (nightly candidate, or the dispatched branch
# for manual runs) and the next attempt builds that exact sha, so every
# deterministic gate re-runs on the repaired tree. (BUILD-REPAIR)
#
# Why the split matters: workflow YAML is frozen when a run starts and
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push .github/workflows changes — but .github/actions/**
# and scripts/** are ordinary repo files, checked out per attempt, so the
# repair AI can fix ~everything mid-run. Workflow-YAML fixes need the
# WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and
# take effect the NEXT run.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: 'Publish the desktop-v<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (default: the dispatched branch)'
        type: string
        default: ''
  # Reusable so nightly-merge.yml can invoke the exact same build.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      publish:
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build (default: the triggering ref)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (nightly passes the candidate)'
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      built_sha:
        description: 'The exact commit the successful attempt built (differs from the input ref when a repair landed)'
        value: ${{ jobs.verdict.outputs.built_sha }}

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: read # repair jobs download this run's failed-job logs

jobs:
  build-attempt-1:
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 180
    # Failures are handled by the repair loop; verdict is the single source of
    # truth for the workflow result. (Job-level continue-on-error masks the
    # failure in `needs.*.result`, so the loop keys off the `ok` OUTPUT — only
    # a fully green attempt sets it.)
    continue-on-error: true
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.done.outputs.ok }}
      sha: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      # Superset has paths deeper than Windows' 260-char MAX_PATH; without this
      # actions/checkout dies with "Filename too long". Must run BEFORE
      # checkout, so it cannot live in the composite action.
      - name: Configure git long paths (Windows MAX_PATH)
        shell: bash
        run: git config --system core.longpaths true || git config --global core.longpaths true
      # A direct dispatch's repair loop pushes to a live branch; racing a
      # nightly's candidate/advance would fail that nightly loudly (non-ff) —
      # refuse up front instead. Only guards direct dispatches: when called
      # from nightly-merge, github.workflow is the CALLER's name.
      - name: Direct-dispatch mutex — refuse while a nightly is active
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.workflow == 'Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ACTIVE=$(gh run list --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --workflow nightly-merge.yml --limit 50 --json databaseId,status --jq '[.[] | select(.status=="in_progress" or .status=="queued" or .status=="waiting" or .status=="requested" or .status=="pending")] | length')
          if [ "$ACTIVE" != "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::(BUILD-REPAIR) a nightly-merge run is in progress/queued — a direct build's repairs could race its candidate/advance. Retry after it finishes."
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Checkout fork source
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Record built sha
        id: sha
        shell: bash
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build, verify, publish
        uses: ./.github/actions/arm64-build
        with:
          publish: ${{ inputs.publish }}
          gh-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Mark attempt green
        id: done
        shell: bash
        run: echo "ok=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  repair-1:
    needs: build-attempt-1
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-attempt-1.outputs.ok != 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      repaired: ${{ steps.repair.outputs.repaired }}
      sha: ${{ steps.repair.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      # persist-credentials:false — the AI step must run credential-less
      # (build logs are untrusted input to it); the push step uses an
      # ephemeral URL-embedded token instead.
      - name: Checkout repair branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
          fetch-depth: 50
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Collect failure evidence
        shell: bash
        env:
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ needs.build-attempt-1.outputs.sha }}
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh collect
      - name: AI repair round 1 (credential-less)
        shell: bash
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ROUND: '1'
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh agent
      - name: Validate + push repair
        id: repair
        shell: bash
        env:
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          ROUND: '1'
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN != '' && secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN || github.token }}
          HAS_WORKFLOW_PAT: ${{ secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh push

  build-attempt-2:
    needs: [build-attempt-1, repair-1]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.repair-1.outputs.repaired == 'true' }}
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 180
    continue-on-error: true
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.done.outputs.ok }}
      sha: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Configure git long paths (Windows MAX_PATH)
        shell: bash
        run: git config --system core.longpaths true || git config --global core.longpaths true
      - name: Checkout repaired source
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.repair-1.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Record built sha
        id: sha

# Why the split matters: workflow YAML is frozen when a run starts and
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push .github/workflows changes — but .github/actions/**
# and scripts/** are ordinary repo files, checked out per attempt, so the
# repair AI can fix ~everything mid-run. Workflow-YAML fixes need the
# WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and
# take effect the NEXT run.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: 'Publish the desktop-v<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (default: the dispatched branch)'
        type: string
        default: ''
  # Reusable so nightly-merge.yml can invoke the exact same build.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      publish:
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build (default: the triggering ref)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (nightly passes the candidate)'
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      built_sha:
        description: 'The exact commit the successful attempt built (differs from the input ref when a repair landed)'
        value: ${{ jobs.verdict.outputs.built_sha }}

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: read # repair jobs download this run's failed-job logs

jobs:
  build-attempt-1:
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 180
    # Failures are handled by the repair loop; verdict is the single source of
    # truth for the workflow result. (Job-level continue-on-error masks the
    # failure in `needs.*.result`, so the loop keys off the `ok` OUTPUT — only
    # a fully green attempt sets it.)
    continue-on-error: true
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.done.outputs.ok }}
      sha: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      # Superset has paths deeper than Windows' 260-char MAX_PATH; without this
      # actions/checkout dies with "Filename too long". Must run BEFORE
      # checkout, so it cannot live in the composite action.
      - name: Configure git long paths (Windows MAX_PATH)
        shell: bash
        run: git config --system core.longpaths true || git config --global core.longpaths true
      # A direct dispatch's repair loop pushes to a live branch; racing a
      # nightly's candidate/advance would fail that nightly loudly (non-ff) —
      # refuse up front instead. Only guards direct dispatches: when called
      # from nightly-merge, github.workflow is the CALLER's name.
      - name: Direct-dispatch mutex — refuse while a nightly is active
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.workflow == 'Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ACTIVE=$(gh run list --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --workflow nightly-merge.yml --limit 50 --json databaseId,status --jq '[.[] | select(.status=="in_progress" or .status=="queued" or .status=="waiting" or .status=="requested" or .status=="pending")] | length')
          if [ "$ACTIVE" != "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::(BUILD-REPAIR) a nightly-merge run is in progress/queued — a direct build's repairs could race its candidate/advance. Retry after it finishes."
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Checkout fork source
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Record built sha
        id: sha
        shell: bash
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build, verify, publish
        uses: ./.github/actions/arm64-build
        with:
          publish: ${{ inputs.publish }}
          gh-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Mark attempt green
        id: done
        shell: bash
        run: echo "ok=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  repair-1:
    needs: build-attempt-1
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build-attempt-1.outputs.ok != 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      repaired: ${{ steps.repair.outputs.repaired }}
      sha: ${{ steps.repair.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      # persist-credentials:false — the AI step must run credential-less
      # (build logs are untrusted input to it); the push step uses an
      # ephemeral URL-embedded token instead.
      - name: Checkout repair branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
          fetch-depth: 50
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Collect failure evidence
        shell: bash
        env:
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ needs.build-attempt-1.outputs.sha }}
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh collect
      - name: AI repair round 1 (credential-less)
        shell: bash
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          ROUND: '1'
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh agent
      - name: Validate + push repair
        id: repair
        shell: bash
        env:
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          ROUND: '1'
          REPAIR_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.repair_branch || github.ref_name }}
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN != '' && secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN || github.token }}
          HAS_WORKFLOW_PAT: ${{ secrets.WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-repair.sh push

  build-attempt-2:
    needs: [build-attempt-1, repair-1]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.repair-1.outputs.repaired == 'true' }}
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 180
    continue-on-error: true
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.done.outputs.ok }}
      sha: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Configure git long paths (Windows MAX_PATH)
        shell: bash
        run: git config --system core.longpaths true || git config --global core.longpaths true
      - name: Checkout repaired source
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.repair-1.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Record built sha
        id: sha
        shell: bash
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build, verify, publish
        uses: ./.github/actions/arm64-build
        with:
          publish: ${{ inputs.publish }}
          gh-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Mark attempt green
        id: done
        shell: bash
        run: echo "ok=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  repair-2:
    needs: [repair-1, build-attempt-2]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.repair-1.outputs.repaired == 'true' && needs.build-attempt-2.outputs.ok != 'true' }}

1	# Fork feature manifest
2	
3	This file is the source of truth for **what our fork adds on top of upstream
4	superset**. The nightly upstream-merge workflow greps every marker below against
5	the merged tree; **if any marker is missing the merge is rejected** (a feature
6	was dropped or an upstream change clobbered it) and the build hard-aborts into
7	the recovery loop. Markers are deliberately distinctive identifiers that only
8	exist because of our feature code.
9	
10	When you add a new custom feature, add a marker row here in the same commit.
11	When upstream **deprecates/removes** a feature we mirrored, remove its marker row
12	in the merge that drops it (the only legitimate way a marker leaves this list).
13	
14	## Features
15	
16	| Feature | What it is | Marker |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Native Windows ARM64 packaging | one-click NSIS installer; ARM64 node-pty/libsql/tokenizers | `npm:@lydell/node-pty`, `bun-windows-arm64` |
19	| Window controls | native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close set on Windows | `titleBarOverlay` |
20	| Windows behaviour fixes | child-process patch, cmd.exe fallback, force-foreground, watchdog, WebGL recovery, fast startup | `windows-child-process` |
21	| Agent status dots (Claude + Codex) | per-terminal dot + workspace rollup; host-service POST + JSONL watcher | `pane-map-hook`, `StatusIndicator` |
22	| Companion lifecycle alerts | phone + custom watch receive distinct ready-for-review and terminal-agent-failure notifications; ready fires once per real work cycle, tool/subagent/admin failures are excluded, and presence/sidebar curation match blocked-agent push behavior | `(COMPANION-LIFECYCLE-ALERTS)` |
23	| Claude Stop unhooked from notify.sh | upstream's raw Stop passthrough must never race superset-notify.py (it wiped the blue dot + yellow-hold) | `CLAUDE-STOP-UNHOOKED` |
24	| Compaction shows working | Claude context compaction (manual /compact + auto) drives the yellow dot via PreCompact / SessionStart(source=compact) | `(COMPACT-YELLOW)` |
25	| Team/workflow work shows working | background_tasks[] entry types split the post-turn dot: agent-type work (teammate/subagent/workflow) holds yellow; shell-only goes blue | `(TEAM-YELLOW)` |
26	| Codex-companion job holds the dot | detached codex worker is invisible to background_tasks[]; an active (pid-alive) codex job for the session holds yellow incl. through StopFailure AND the JSONL watcher's user-interrupt turn-end (System 1 mirrors the same check via `codexJobActive` in agent-jsonl-watcher.ts, so a codex-only session can't false-green when the user interrupts the Claude turn — the codex worker is a separate process on its own API and keeps running) | `_codex_job_active` |
27	| Manual compact restores shell-blue | a manual /compact ending while only a background shell runs restores the BackgroundRunning blue (turn-end snapshot marker) instead of false-greening; the JSONL-watcher re-attach after compaction must not wipe that blue | `_shellbg_marker_path`, `(BLUE-SPECTATOR)` |
28	| Watcher ignores replayed and counterfeit turn-ends | the JSONL watcher emits ONE turn-end of its own — a user interrupt — because Claude Code fires no hook for it; every other turn-end, including a terminal API error, is the hook's (Claude Code runs its StopFailure hooks whenever the turn's last record is an api-error and superset-notify.py's StopFailure branch answers `Stop`), so hook-is-truth holds and the watcher's api-error contribution is auto-resume signalling only, which asserts no dot state. The watcher's own emit still bypasses superset-notify.py, and the renderer clears the background-running axis on every non-`BackgroundRunning` agent event, so a `Stop` fired off the wrong line wipes the blue the hook just restored (live: compact-end `BackgroundRunning`, then 763ms later the watcher re-parsed the compaction-rewritten transcript, matched a HISTORICAL "Request interrupted by user" and greened the dot under a still-running background shell). Two gates now stand between a matched line and an emit. FIRST, the line must BE an interrupt: the marker was a raw PHRASE match, and this repo's own agent traffic quotes it constantly — measured over 10,695 local transcripts the phrase predicate matched 1217 lines of which 70 were quotes (tool_results and long teammate messages), and 9 of the 10 interrupt-releases in a live log window were false `Stop`s fired MID-TURN. So it is parsed to Claude Code's EXACT synthetic record — a user entry whose message content is a single `text` block equal to `[Request interrupted by user]` — which drops every quote and keeps all 1147 genuine records. SECOND, the turn must have ended JUST NOW: Claude Code re-presents already-written entries (compaction rewrite, post-truncation re-read from offset 0, discover-poll whole-file read), so each entry is replay-gated on its own `uuid` (already judged → never counts again, at any age) and `timestamp` age, which must be no older than 120s and no further in the future than a 5s clock-skew tolerance (a backward NTP step would otherwise make ALL history read as fresh). A file that already existed when the watcher started is never replayed whole through a cold gate, but it is no longer tailed blind either: Codex seeds it to EOF, and Claude re-reads a bounded 256KB tail under a third gate layer — a pre-start fence suppressing every entry stamped strictly before the watcher started (no skew slack: both stamps come from the same machine's clock). The fence is held on the file's own state, not a per-pass local, so a read that throws after the offset was rewound cannot make the retry re-read that history UNFENCED. Seeding blind would SWALLOW an append that landed between `fs.watch` going live and the deferred seed reaching that file, and an interrupt has no hook fallback at all, so that dot would stay stuck; the tail is bounded because reading a multi-megabyte transcript synchronously at startup is what starves the renderer. A blocked match emits NOTHING, so the hook's blue stands and an AUTO compact no longer gets a false turn-end. A genuine interrupt still emits a bare `Stop` (the (BA) blue latch has no self-clear, and the Agent-Complete chime is Stop-only), and that verdict is explicit — never derived from best-effort marker cleanup | `(WATCHER-BLUE-STOMP)` |
29	| ws native modules off | host-service `ws` must use pure-JS mask/unmask — a broken packaged bufferutil wedges WS receivers and kills ALL terminal keyboard input | `WS_NO_BUFFER_UTIL` |
30	| Shell-running blue dot | OSC 133 C/D command-running detection | `scanForOsc133Cd` |
31	| Non-git / multi-repo workspaces | open a non-git folder as a plain workspace | `resolveNonGitFolder` |
32	| Multi-repo branch workspaces | "Open from multi-folder" groups N git repos; "+" fans the same branch out as a worktree per repo under one container workspace | `readMultiRepoConfig`, `createMultiRepoWorkspaceFlow` |
33	| Multi-repo member management | Project Settings "Repositories" section adds/removes member repos of a multi-repo project. Add is lazy (included in NEW branch workspaces only — cleanup already tolerates a missing member worktree); remove force-removes that repo's worktrees from every existing branch container (confirm dialog; repo + branches kept) BEFORE the config rewrite so no orphan worktrees/registrations strand. Min 2 members enforced | `addMultiRepoMember`, `MultiRepoMembersSection` |
34	| Workspace branch label | the open workspace page names its branch top-right in the tab bar (click copies) — the only branch surface a non-git multi-repo container has | `WorkspaceBranchLabel` |
35	| Workspace-create failure toast | every workspace/worktree create failure raises a toast with the actual reason (e.g. a GitHub/network timeout) from the one `recordFailure` chokepoint — so a transient failure no longer reads as a silent "stuck creating → reload" | `(CREATE-FAIL-TOAST)` |
36	| Thread snooze / archive | per-thread timed Snooze + sticky Archive in the sidebar | `getWorkspaceSidebarBucket`, `APP_LAUNCH_ID`, `DashboardSidebarStateSection` |
37	| Sidebar row projection carries the fork state fields | the host-owned sidebar row projection (`rawSidebarWorkspaces` in `useDashboardSidebarData`) must carry `snoozeUntil`/`snoozeLaunchId`/`archivedAt`/`completedAt`/`deletedAt` from `v2WorkspaceLocalState` — the v1.14.2 upstream merge rebuilt that mapping and silently dropped them, which broke snooze (rows never left the active lane), emptied the Recycle Bin, vanished archived masters, and resurfaced completed threads under Archived | `(SIDEBAR-STATE-PROJECTION)` |
38	| Master rows snoozeable | `snoozeWorkspace` inserts a pre-snoozed local-state row for an auto-included main that has none yet (mirrors `archiveWorkspace`) — Snooze on a master row used to silently no-op | `(SNOOZE-MAIN)` |
39	| Sessions snooze / archive too | project-less "session" rows get the same Snooze and Archive semantics as project threads, surfaced in two top-level `Snoozed Sessions` / `Archived Sessions` subsections under the Sessions header (revealed from its right-click menu). The bucket classifier was already project-agnostic, so a snoozed or archived session simply LEFT the active lane and could never be recovered — the only surfaces that rendered an inactive row were the per-project ones, and a session has no project row to hang either the rows or the reveal/collapse flags off. The flags therefore live on the fixed-size `v2UserPreferences` singleton rather than a per-entity key, and hiding a session never navigates away from it: an open session stays open in the pane it is already in. Sessions still never reach the Kanban board — every card is bound to a sidebar project id and a session's is null | `(SESSION-LIFECYCLE)` |
40	| Sticky project removal | "Remove project from sidebar" tombstones EVERY workspace of the project incl. mains, and passive workspace route mounts (session restore, kanban split) use `placeWorkspaceFromPassiveMount`, which never re-inserts the project's sidebar row and never resurrects an existing hidden row — a removed project can only come back via an EXPLICIT open (Workspaces page, project setup/import) | `(REMOVE-STICKY)` |
41	| Case-insensitive repo-path dedupe | host-service `project.findByPath` / import-collision checks compare `projects.repoPath` case-insensitively on win32/darwin (case-insensitive filesystems) — a case-only folder rename used to miss the existing row and mint a duplicate project (cloud slug conflict suffixed `-2` instead of reusing) | `(PATH-CI-DEDUPE)` |
42	| Merge semantic review gate | every nightly upstream merge — clean or conflicted — is reviewed by Opus against this manifest BEFORE it may commit/build/publish: a cleanly-merging upstream hunk that semantically breaks a fork feature (the v1.14.2 sidebar-projection incident) is caught here, not in production. Review is fresh after every adaptation and fails closed: no parsable verdict, a final BREAKAGE verdict, or a review run that modified the tree all hard-abort with the baseline untouched | `(MERGE-SEMANTIC-GATE)` |
43	| Nightly proactive port + bounded adaptation | after conflict resolution, Opus compares the old/new upstream tag trees against fork-owned files and surgically ports cleanly-merging API refactors before the gates; semantic BREAKAGE findings then drive at most two repair rounds, each followed by ReferenceError + marker gates and a fresh review. This closes the desktop-v1.16.0 class where upstream removed collections/exports used only by fork files, so git produced no conflict for the resolver to see | `(MERGE-ADAPT)` |
44	| Self-repairing build | a failed ARM64 build attempt triggers a bounded Opus 5 repair loop (max 3 attempts / 2 repairs): the repair agent reads the failed job's log, fixes the checked-out tree (scripts/, .github/actions/, source — all take effect the NEXT attempt of the SAME run), and pushes to the repair branch; every deterministic gate re-runs on the repaired sha. Repairs can never change the app version or touch FEATURES.md; workflow-YAML fixes need `WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN` and land next run | `(BUILD-REPAIR)` |
45	| Sidebar hover-freeze | rows never re-sort while the pointer is over the project list (order applies on leave) | `(HOVER-FREEZE)` |
46	| Terminal links | plain click copies a URL/path, Ctrl/Cmd+click opens; `.html` paths open in Chrome (OS default fallback) | `useLinkClickHint`, `openHtmlInBrowser` |
47	| Agent-hook bash-wrap | Gemini/Cursor `.sh` hooks run via Git-for-Windows bash | `agent-wrappers` |
48	| Kanban board | device-local board mirroring branches + Queued column | `v2KanbanCards`, `KANBAN_QUEUE_COLUMN_ID` |
49	| Kanban host-served workspace source | every fork surface that needs the workspace universe (kanban seed/prune/render, bound-card actions, collapse-split, recycle-bin destroy URL, sidebar snooze/archive fallbacks, is-local gate) reads the host-served lists (`useHostWorkspaces`), NEVER the Electric `v2Workspaces` mirror — upstream's offline-first migration stopped writing new rows to the cloud table, so Electric reads silently miss every post-migration branch | `(KANBAN-HOST-SOURCE)` |
50	| Kanban Completed column | fixed FINAL column: dropping a card or choosing Mark completed on an active non-main worktree stamps an editable completed date and hides the thread from the sidebar ENTIRELY (drag out un-completes/restores); per-column date filter (all / last calendar month / custom range) for work-done reports; completed cards survive branch deletion as frozen records; main cards can't complete | `KANBAN_COMPLETED_COLUMN_ID`, `(KANBAN-MARK-COMPLETED)` |
51	| Kanban append-only backup | daily write-once JSON snapshot of the board; code can never delete/overwrite one | `writeKanbanBackup` |
52	| Kanban sidebar button toggles | sidebar Kanban press: anywhere → full-screen board; part-screen split → full-screen (closing then reopens that workspace full size); full-screen → close back to the remembered previous page (fallback Workspaces list) | `(KANBAN-TOGGLE)` |
53	| Subagent tool events never stomp the red | a PostToolUse whose payload carries `agent_id` (ran inside a subagent) maps to the red-respecting SubagentActive — background agents' tool completions must not clear a pending AskUserQuestion/permission red; only a main-loop completion does. SubagentStart likewise | `(SUBTOOL-RED)` |
54	| Async background-tool completions never stomp the red | the Workflow / Agent / Task tools spawn background agents and complete on the MAIN loop (no agent_id) WHILE the main loop is blocked on an AskUserQuestion/permission red — so their PostToolUse maps to SubagentActive, not Start, instead of wrongly clearing the pending red (the SUBTOOL-RED sequential-main-loop assumption breaks for async-spawning tools) | `(ASYNC-TOOL-RED)` |
55	| Untagged background-agent tool completions never stomp the red | teammate/fork tool completions (ordinary Read/Bash/Edit/…) stream in attributed to the PARENT session WITHOUT an agent_id, so the SUBTOOL-RED/ASYNC-TOOL-RED checks miss them and they would Start-clear a pending AskUserQuestion red. A `<terminalId>.askq/` DIR holds one marker PER OWNER (the raising agent_id, or `_main`), set synchronously at PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion; while ANY marker exists an untagged ordinary PostToolUse maps to the red-respecting SubagentActive (and refreshes `.bgactive`, since the blocked main loop means that tool is genuine teammate activity). Per-owner so concurrent questions (main + a subagent) are independent. The renderer has ONE permission axis per terminal, so a single CENTRAL GUARD wraps the whole decision and enforces "rendered red ⇔ `.askq` dir non-empty" in one place: it counts owners before and after the inner decision, then (DOWNGRADE) turns any red-CLEARING result (Start, or a green/blue turn-end) into the red-respecting SubagentActive while any owner remains (stamping `.mainstopped` on a held turn-end so the last SubagentStop still finalizes green), and (UPGRADE) turns a NON-clearing result (SubagentActive yellow/agent/codex hold, or a None no-op) into Start when this event removed the LAST owner — so a just-answered/cancelled/reaped question's red can't latch behind a yellow hold. One choke point, so NO branch — answer, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop (incl. its cancelled-with-question and still-other-work paths), the compact paths — can drop a co-pending red OR strand a resolved one. (The native-notification manager likewise only chimes "complete" on Stop and "awaiting" on permission, never on SubagentActive.) An owner's marker is cleared by its own answer (PostToolUse:AskUserQuestion), its SubagentStop, or the main turn boundary (Stop/UserPromptSubmit clear only `_main`); dead non-`_main` owners are reaped against `background_tasks` ids on Stop/SubagentStop (MARKER-RECONCILE-style) so a subagent that died without a clean stop can't pin red; the whole dir clears on session end / API abort / fresh SessionStart (its hook is registered UNSCOPED so the non-compact source is reached), and a main interrupt clears only `_main` (detached teammates survive). The JSONL watcher emits its direct interrupt `Stop` as `SubagentActive` instead while a live `.askq` owner remains (it bypasses the Python guard). Synchronous + per-owner = no timing window and no cross-question clearing; a tool-PERMISSION red (no `.askq` marker) still clears on its approved tool's main-loop Start — no approval-clear regression. SubagentStop of a subagent that stopped WITH its own question still open emits Start (central guard keeps any other owner) so a cancelled subagent question's red can't latch; the watcher's held interrupt also stamps `.mainstopped` so a later SubagentStop still finalizes green; and an askq owner is NEVER reaped from run-marker age alone (a subagent legitimately BLOCKED on an open question has no activity, so age-reaping it would drop a LIVE red) — when `background_tasks` is absent a leaked owner just errs YELLOW until a session/abort/fresh-start boundary clears it. Accepted limits (all inherent to the fire-and-forget hook→POST→last-writer-wins pipeline, not specific to this feature): a generic Notification (tool-permission) red is unguarded (its approval is indistinguishable from a teammate tool without a request id); and a sub-ms TOCTOU window (a Start in flight before a question opens). Fully closing that TOCTOU window would need pipeline-wide event sequencing | `(UNTAGGED-BG-RED)` |
56	| Working-cadence events unhooked from notify.sh | upstream's raw `notify.sh` passthrough is NOT registered on Claude's UserPromptSubmit / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure either (same fix as CLAUDE-STOP-UNHOOKED). The host maps all three to `Start`, and notify.sh bypasses superset-notify.py's central red guard — in a forks/teammates run the forks' PostToolUse completions stream in every 1-5s and each raw `Start` cleared the main loop's pending AskUserQuestion red to yellow. superset-notify.py owns these for Claude (with agent_id discrimination + the guard), so dropping the raw duplicates loses nothing; only binding (SessionStart/SessionEnd) + the native PermissionRequest stay | `(CLAUDE-WORKING-UNHOOKED)` |
57	| Subagent StopFailure stays scoped | a StopFailure carrying an `agent_id` is ONE subagent/fork aborting on a rate-limit/API error, not the whole Claude session dying — it is handled by a SELF-SCOPED inline branch that drops ONLY that fork's run + question markers and never the shared session state (sibling markers, the main `_main` question owner, the agent-bg snapshot), and (like the main-abort branch) never trusts the abort payload's `background_tasks`; the remaining run-marker count + the `.mainstopped` sentinel decide the hold and the central red guard re-holds any still-open question. The full-abort StopFailure branch (clears run_dir + every marker + the `.askq` guard, then greens) would otherwise stomp the main loop's still-pending AskUserQuestion red when a fork hit a limit. Also: superset-notify.py now OWNS `PostToolUseFailure` (aliased to PostToolUse through the red guard) since notify.sh stopped raw-posting it | `(STOPFAIL-SUBAGENT)` |
58	| Layered dot axes | a source's dot status is DERIVED as the highest-precedence active axis (permission > working > review, + the separate blue axes) — events latch/unlatch axes they have evidence about, so a lower assert can never overwrite a higher active state | `applySourceAxes` |
59	| Leaked yellow-hold markers self-heal | a SubagentStop arriving with a mismatched/missing agent_id leaks its run-dir marker and pins the dot yellow with nothing running; at every Stop/SubagentStop the payload's background_tasks[] (ground truth) reaps any marker not listed as still running | `(MARKER-RECONCILE)` |
60	| Subagent markers track per-marker activity | each subagent's run-dir marker is touched on every PostToolUse it fires (not just SubagentStart), so its mtime reflects last activity and the conservative 12h leaked-marker backstop can't false-green a still-working subagent; the COMMON orphan-on-API-error leak is handled fast by the hook's own StopFailure run-dir clear — see `(API-ABORT-RELEASE)` — instead of a flaky short timer | `(MARKER-INACTIVE)` |
61	| Orphaned subagent markers reaped on API abort | a main Claude session's stream abort (`API Error: Stream idle timeout - partial response received`, an isApiErrorMessage line) ends the turn and ORPHANS in-flight subagents WITHOUT firing their SubagentStop, leaking run-dir markers that would pin the dot yellow with nothing running. The abort DOES reach superset-notify.py: Claude Code runs its `StopFailure` hooks whenever the turn's last assistant record is an api-error, so the hook's full-abort StopFailure branch owns the release — it clears the whole run dir plus the sentinel / compact / agent-bg / shell-bg / bg-active markers and the `.askq` guard dir, then greens (a codex-companion job on its OWN API still holds yellow, and the central red guard re-holds any question the abort did not kill). Deterministic, event-driven, no timer, and on the same turn-end path as every other dot decision. The JSONL watcher does NOT own this: an earlier fork revision had it reap off the transcript's isApiErrorMessage line, which duplicated the hook and let a replayed transcript chunk fire a turn-end that stomped the hook's background-blue — see `(WATCHER-BLUE-STOMP)`. The watcher still reads api-errors, but only to signal `(AUTO-RESUME)`; it asserts no dot state for them | `(API-ABORT-RELEASE)` |
62	| Dot state survives renderer reloads | the v2-notifications dot store persists to sessionStorage — an in-place window reload (Ctrl+R / error boundary / crash recovery) no longer wipes every dot; the background-running blue has no self-heal until the next turn end, so a reload used to hide a running background task for hours. Clears on real app restart (no stale dots across launches) | `(DOT-PERSIST)` |
63	| Sidebar agent chips ride the fork dot pipeline | upstream's workspace-agents-row chips (agent logo + status dot under a sidebar row) originally had their own status pipe (host binding raw `lastEventType`, 4-case map that read fork events like SubagentActive/BackgroundRunning as idle) and a broken liveness filter (`terminal_sessions.status` stays `active` forever for a closed-tab pty → chips trapped permission-red for days). Upstream re-landed a separate facepile chip in desktop-v1.18.0 that never got this fix (its own binding-derived status pipe, so it stale-reds); the fork deletes that chip outright — see `(AGENTS-CHIP-REMOVED)` — leaving the per-tab chips as the only agent chip surface | `(CHIP-DOT-UNIFY)` |
